literature.headline_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期乙型肝炎病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: LFIA 与 qPCR 的一致性因标记物和样本类型而异,血液中 HIV 和 HCV 抗体检测的一致性较高,而肝脏和脾脏的一致性较低。在符合预定 qPCR 阳性标准的样本中,LFIA 阳性样本往往比 LFIA 阴性样本表现出更高的病毒载量,肝脏中的 HBV 达到统计学显着性。 [10.1128/spectrum.01681-26]
脑脊液分析证实结核性脑膜炎,胸部计算机断层扫描显示弥漫性粟粒结节,提示血行播散性结核病。血清学乙型肝炎表面抗原、e抗原和核心抗体呈阳性,表明病毒复制活跃。 [10.1186/s40249-026-01519-5]
乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染与病毒和 宿主 蛋白的糖基化改变有关,这会影响病毒进入、免疫逃避和疾病进展,而 HBV 感染会重塑 宿主 糖基化。 [10.1007/s10482-026-02453-0]
研究发现,乙型肝炎病毒 家族史与 HBsAg 清除风险较低显着相关。大约 37% 的这种负相关是由基线 HBsAg 水平升高介导的。 [10.3748/wjg.127443]
机制分析表明,Oxy229 损害了 HBV-NTCP 复合物从质膜到细胞内囊泡的重新定位。 [10.1073/pnas.2603986123]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: LFIA agreement with qPCR varied by marker and specimen type, with substantial agreement for HIV and HCV antibody detection in blood and lower agreement in liver and spleen. [10.1128/spectrum.01681-26]

Cerebrospinal fluid analysis confirmed tuberculous meningitis, and chest computed tomography revealed diffuse miliary nodules suggestive of hematogenous disseminated tuberculosis. Serology was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, e-antigen, and core antibody, indicating active viral replication. [10.1186/s40249-026-01519-5]

Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with altered glycosylation of both viral and host proteins, which influences viral entry, immune evasion and disease progression, while HBV infection remodels host glycosylation. [10.1007/s10482-026-02453-0]
EHF, FIB-4 achieved the highest area under the curve [AUC; 0.911, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.844-0.969) followed by APRI (0.843, 95% CI: 0.755-0.923). [10.4274/dir.2026.264052]

The study found that family history of hepatitis B virus was significantly associated with a lower hazard of HBsAg clearance. Approximately 37% of this negative association was mediated by elevated baseline HBsAg levels. [10.3748/wjg.127443]

news.headline_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期乙型肝炎病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 一项 II 期研究评估了 siRNA 疗法 HRS-5635 治疗慢性 HBV 感染的效果。治疗 结束后 24 周,最高剂量(400 mg)显示 19% 的患者出现 功能性治愈,HBsAg 水平低于 0.05 IU/mL。该研究已在 AASLD 年会上发表。 [news-e4d9ca169e2a2182]
该文章报告了美国肝移植受者中乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 率不理想的情况,正如一位传染病专家所强调的那样。这是报告的问题,而不是 暴发 或已确认的事件。 [news-f7a38f3fcdb3a134]
该报告提供了 AASLD 2026 会议关于 慢性乙型肝炎 和迟发性遗传性胆汁淤积症和 Alagille 综合征的最新信息。它包括研究摘要和专家评论,但没有报告已证实或疑似的 暴发 事件。 [news-fe306b1f0998e5fb]
Precision BioSciences 公布了 ELIMINATE-B 研究的 1 期数据,显示使用 PBGENE-HBV 进行基因编辑可以消除 92% 具有可检测 pgRNA 的患者中的病毒 储存宿主 (共价闭合环状DNA),其中包括 0.4 mg/kg 剂量水平的所有 6 名可评估患者。这被认为是这种方法迄今为止最完整的人类证据。 [news-154f3d7e9d3113c7]
研究人员发现,与乙型肝炎 疫苗 应答者和健康捐赠者相比,慢性乙型肝炎 患者表现出明显更少的独特 T 细胞受体 α 链和 β 链互补决定区 3 序列。这项研究由 Bioengineer.org 报道。 [news-98ad7d60a62a5cc8]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Hepatitis B virus news developments.
key_findings_en: A phase II study evaluated the siRNA therapy HRS-5635 for treating chronic HBV infection. The highest dose (400 mg) showed a functional cure in 19% of patients 24 weeks after treatment ended, with HBsAg levels below 0.05 IU/mL. The study was presented at the AASLD annual meeting. [news-e4d9ca169e2a2182]

The article reports on suboptimal vaccination rates for Hepatitis B among liver transplant recipients in the United States, as highlighted by an expert in infectious disease. This is a reported issue, not an outbreak or confirmed event. [news-f7a38f3fcdb3a134]

The report provides updates from the AASLD 2026 conference on chronic hepatitis B and late-onset genetic cholestasis and Alagille syndrome. It includes summaries of studies and expert commentary, but no confirmed or suspected outbreak events are reported. [news-fe306b1f0998e5fb]

Precision BioSciences presented Phase 1 data from the ELIMINATE-B study showing that gene editing using PBGENE-HBV can eliminate the viral reservoir (cccDNA) in 92% of patients with detectable pgRNA, including all six evaluable patients at the 0.4 mg/kg dose level. [news-154f3d7e9d3113c7]

Researchers found that individuals with chronic hepatitis B exhibit significantly fewer unique T-cell receptor alpha-chain and beta-chain complementarity-determining region 3 sequences compared to hepatitis B vaccine responders and healthy donors. This study was reported by Bioengineer.org. [news-98ad7d60a62a5cc8]

该文章报告了美国肝移植受者中乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 率不理想的情况,正如一位传染病专家所强调的那样。这是报告的问题,而不是 暴发 或已确认的事件。 [news-f7a38f3fcdb3a134]。
该报告提供了 AASLD 2026 会议关于 慢性乙型肝炎 和迟发性遗传性胆汁淤积症和 Alagille 综合征的最新信息。它包括研究摘要和专家评论,但没有报告已证实或疑似的 暴发 事件。 [news-fe306b1f0998e5fb]。
Precision BioSciences 公布了 ELIMINATE-B 研究的 1 期数据,显示使用 PBGENE-HBV 进行基因编辑可以消除 92% 具有可检测 pgRNA 的患者中的病毒 储存宿主 (共价闭合环状DNA),其中包括 0.4 mg/kg 剂量水平的所有 6 名可评估患者。这被认为是这种方法迄今为止最完整的人类证据。

papers.title: The Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Antiviral Activity of ABI ‐4334, A Novel Next‐Generation Hepatitis B Capsid Assembly Modulator
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Novel, well‐tolerated, short‐term therapeutics for chronic hepatitis B virus infection (cHBV) are needed. ABI‐4334 is a next‐generation capsid assembly modulator that targets the HBV core protein. The safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of ABI‐4334 in healthy volunteers and participants with cHBV and antiviral effects in participants with cHBV were examined in two Phase 1 studies. Study 101 was a placebo‐controlled study of healthy volunteers that included four single‐ascending dose cohorts and two once‐daily multiple‐ascending dose cohorts randomized 6:2 (ABI‐4334:placebo), and one crossover food‐effect cohort randomized 3:3 (fed:fasted). Study 102 was a randomized, blinded, placebo‐controlled study where participants with cHBV were randomized 8:2 (ABI‐4334 [2 dose cohorts]:placebo). Overall, 54 healthy volunteers and 20 participants with cHBV were included in Studies 101 and 102, respectively. Most participants (75%) in Study 102 were hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) negative and generally had lower baseline HBV DNA and pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) levels. ABI‐4334 was well tolerated, with no treatment‐emergent serious adverse events (AEs) or treatment‐emergent AEs leading to study discontinuation. The mean ABI‐4334 plasma half‐life ranges were comparable across doses in both studies. Following multiple‐dose administration in participants with cHBV, the steady‐state mean plasma half‐life ranged from 17.5 to 27.5 h. HBV DNA declines were observed in both HBeAg‐positive ( n = 3) and ‐negative ( n = 13) participants across doses. Reductions in pgRNA were observed in participants with detectable pgRNA at baseline. ABI‐4334 was well tolerated, with pharmacokinetics and antiviral results supporting the continued development of ABI‐4334 as a monotherapy or component of novel combination regimens for cHBV. Trial Registration: Study 101 (NCT05569941). Study 102 (NCT06384131)

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the safety, tolerability, and antiviral activity of ABI-4334, a novel capsid assembly modulator targeting HBV core protein, in two Phase 1 trials. Study 101 involved healthy volunteers with single- and multiple-ascending dose cohorts, while Study 102 included participants with chronic HBV infection randomized 8:2 (ABI-4334:placebo). The results showed HBV DNA declines in both HBeAg-positive and -negative participants, as well as reductions in pgRNA in those with detectable baseline levels. ABI-4334 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events reported. These findings support its continued development as a monotherapy or combination treatment for chronic HBV. The evidence is strong, but the limited sample sizes and Phase 1 design may affect generalizability.

papers.title_zh: 新型下一代乙型肝炎衣壳组装调节剂 ABI ‐4334 的安全性、药代动力学和 抗病毒药物 活性
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Novel, well‐tolerated, short‐term therapeutics for chronic hepatitis B virus infection (cHBV) are needed. ABI‐4334 is a next‐generation capsid assembly modulator that targets the HBV core protein. The safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of ABI‐4334 in healthy volunteers and participants with cHBV and antiviral effects in participants with cHBV were examined in two Phase 1 studies. Study 101 was a placebo‐controlled study of healthy volunteers that included four single‐ascending dose cohorts and two once‐daily multiple‐ascending dose cohorts randomized 6:2 (ABI‐4334:placebo), and one crossover food‐effect cohort randomized 3:3 (fed:fasted). Study 102 was a randomized, blinded, placebo‐controlled study where participants with cHBV were randomized 8:2 (ABI‐4334 [2 dose cohorts]:placebo). Overall, 54 healthy volunteers and 20 participants with cHBV were included in Studies 101 and 102, respectively. Most participants (75%) in Study 102 were hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) negative and generally had lower baseline HBV DNA and pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) levels. ABI‐4334 was well tolerated, with no treatment‐emergent serious adverse events (AEs) or treatment‐emergent AEs leading to study discontinuation. The mean ABI‐4334 plasma half‐life ranges were comparable across doses in both studies. Following multiple‐dose administration in participants with cHBV, the steady‐state mean plasma half‐life ranged from 17.5 to 27.5 h. HBV DNA declines were observed in both HBeAg‐positive ( n = 3) and ‐negative ( n = 13) participants across doses. Reductions in pgRNA were observed in participants with detectable pgRNA at baseline. ABI‐4334 was well tolerated, with pharmacokinetics and antiviral results supporting the continued development of ABI‐4334 as a monotherapy or component of novel combination regimens for cHBV. Trial Registration: Study 101 (NCT05569941). Study 102 (NCT06384131)
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要:需要针对 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒感染 (cHBV) 的新型、耐受性良好的短期疗法。ABI-4334 是一种针对 HBV 核心蛋白的下一代衣壳组装调节剂。在两项 1 期研究中检查了 ABI-4334 在健康志愿者和 cHBV 参与者中的安全性、耐受性和药代动力学,以及 抗病毒药物 对 cHBV 参与者的影响。研究101是一项针对健康志愿者的安慰剂对照研究,包括四名单次递增剂量队列研究和两项每日一次多次递增剂量队列研究随机6:2(ABI-4334:安慰剂),以及一项交叉食物效应队列研究随机3:3(进食:禁食)。研究 102 是一项随机、盲法、安慰剂对照研究,其中 cHBV 参与者按 8:2 随机分配(ABI-4334 [2 剂量 队列研究]:安慰剂)。总体而言,研究 101 和研究 102 分别纳入了 54 名健康志愿者和 20 名患有 cHBV 的参与者。研究 102 中的大多数参与者 (75%) 乙型肝炎 e 抗原 (HBeAg) 阴性,并且基线 HBV DNA 和前基因组 RNA (pgRNA) 水平普遍较低。ABI-4334 耐受性良好,没有出现 治疗 突发严重不良事件 (AE) 或 治疗 突发 AE 导致研究中止。两项研究中不同剂量的 ABI-4334 平均血浆半衰期范围相当。cHBV 参与者多剂量给药后,稳态平均血浆半衰期为 17.5 至 27.5 小时。在不同剂量的 HBeAg 阳性 (n = 3) 和阴性 (n = 13) 参与者中均观察到 HBV DNA 下降。在基线时可检测到 pgRNA 的参与者中观察到 pgRNA 减少。ABI-4334 耐受性良好,药代动力学和 抗病毒药物 结果支持 ABI-4334 作为 cHBV 单一疗法或新型联合疗法的组成部分的持续开发。试验注册:研究 101 (NCT05569941)。研究 102 (NCT06384131)

papers.title: Hepatitis B and D: Interferon-Based Therapy-For Clinical Trials or Standard of Care-Back to the Future?
papers.abstract: Interferon (IFN) has historically played a major role in chronic viral hepatitis B and D management over the last three decades. Widening utilisation of nucleoside/nucleotide analogues (NUCs) for hepatitis B viral suppression, which have a better side-effect profile, alongside the recent licensing of bulevirtide for treatment of hepatitis D, means that its clinical use has further declined. Pegylated-interferon alpha (peg-IFNα) treatment is suboptimal with poor tolerability and achieves durable clearance of hepatitis B and D in only a limited number of patients. Nevertheless, its use in hepatitis B has significantly increased the number of patients achieving hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss compared to those on NUCs alone. Evidence has shown that peg-IFNα is also associated with overall improved long-term clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis D, even for the many whose hepatitis D viral load rebounds after discontinuation. Clinical trials have recently focused on peg-IFNα in combination with novel antiviral therapies in the goal for finite cure in hepatitis B and D. This article focuses on recent research advances, examining if peg-IFNα treatment may still play an important role in hepatitis B and D treatment.

Widening utilisation of nucleoside/nucleotide analogues (NUCs) for hepatitis B viral suppression, which have a better side-effect profile, alongside the recent licensing of bulevirtide for treatment of hepatitis D, means that its clinical use has further declined. Pegylated-interferon alpha (peg-IFNα) treatment is suboptimal with poor tolerability and achieves durable clearance of hepatitis B and D in only a limited number of patients. Nevertheless, its use in hepatitis B has significantly increased the number of patients achieving hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss compared to those on NUCs alone. Evidence has shown that peg-IFNα is also associated with overall improved long-term clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis D, even for the many whose hepatitis D viral load rebounds after discontinuation. Clinical trials have recently focused on peg-IFNα in combination with novel antiviral therapies in the goal for finite cure in hepatitis B and D. This article focuses on recent research advances, examining if peg-IFNα treatment may still play an important role in hepatitis B and D treatment.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the historical and current role of interferon-based therapy in managing hepatitis B and D. It highlights the decline in clinical use due to the availability of nucleoside/nucleotide analogues (NUCs) and bulevirtide, which offer better side-effect profiles. Pegylated-interferon alpha (peg-IFNα) is noted as suboptimal with poor tolerability and limited durable clearance rates. However, its use in hepatitis B has increased HBsAg loss compared to NUCs alone. Additionally, peg-IFNα is associated with improved long-term clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis D, despite viral load rebounds post-treatment. The review focuses on recent research advances and the potential for peg-IFNα to still play an important role in treatment strategies.

papers.abstract_zh: 过去三十年来,干扰素 (IFN) 在慢性病毒性乙型肝炎和丁型肝炎的治疗中发挥了重要作用。核苷/核苷酸类似物(NUC)在抑制乙型肝炎病毒方面的广泛应用(其副作用较小),加上最近获得的用于丁型肝炎 治疗 的 bulevirtide 许可,意味着其临床使用进一步下降。聚乙二醇化干扰素α (peg-IFNα) 治疗 效果欠佳,耐受性差,仅在有限数量的患者中实现了乙型肝炎和丁型肝炎的持久清除。尽管如此,与单独使用 NUC 的患者相比,其在乙型肝炎中的使用显着增加了实现乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 消失的患者数量。有证据表明,peg-IFNα 还与慢性丁型肝炎的长期临床结果的整体改善相关,即使对于许多丁型肝炎病毒载量在停药后反弹的人来说也是如此。最近的临床试验重点关注 peg-IFNα 与新型 抗病毒药物 疗法的联合治疗,以实现乙型肝炎和丁型肝炎的有限治愈。本文重点介绍最新的研究进展,探讨 peg-IFNα 治疗 是否仍可能在乙型肝炎和丁型肝炎 治疗 中发挥重要作用。

papers.title: Chronic Hepatitis B in the United States: Current Landscape, Unmet Needs and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection represents a major public health challenge in the US, with substantial unmet needs related to timely diagnosis, treatment, monitoring and disease management. This narrative review explores the CHB landscape in the US, including gaps in patient care, the evolving therapeutic landscape, the clinical utility of serological biomarkers to improve outcomes and the experiences of people living with hepatitis B (PLWHB). Hepatitis B remains underdiagnosed and undertreated in the US, and current efforts are insufficient to meet the associated World Health Organization 2030 elimination targets. Latest guidelines from the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the Infectious Diseases Society of America, representing a North American perspective, signify a shift towards expanded treatment eligibility criteria and shared decision-making. Nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) are the current standard of care in the US, but functional cure is rarely achieved with NAs alone. Novel finite therapies targeting functional cure, such as antisense oligonucleotides, small interfering RNAs, immune modulators and combination or sequential regimens, are under investigation. Because of the unpredictable, complex nature of CHB, biomarkers such as quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen offer prognostic value for treatment decisions and could help guide individualised CHB management. PLWHB experience psychological impacts and health-related concerns, including fear of transmission and hepatitis B virus-related complications. Opportunities for improvement of CHB management include increased screening and linkage to care, development of more treatments targeting functional cure, adoption of serological biomarkers to inform treatment decisions and prioritising the lived experiences and preferences of PLWHB.

analysis.summary_en: This review highlights the significant public health challenge posed by chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in the United States, emphasizing the need for improved diagnosis, treatment, and disease management. The review outlines the current landscape of CHB, noting that it remains underdiagnosed and undertreated, with insufficient progress towards meeting WHO 2030 elimination targets. It discusses the limitations of nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) in achieving a functional cure and highlights the potential of novel therapies and serological biomarkers to improve outcomes. The review also underscores the importance of incorporating the lived experiences and preferences of people living with hepatitis B (PLWHB) into management strategies. These findings suggest a need for expanded treatment eligibility, shared decision-making, and further research into more effective therapeutic approaches.

papers.title_zh: 美国的 慢性乙型肝炎:当前形势、未满足的需求和未来方向。
papers.source_body_en: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection represents a major public health challenge in the US, with substantial unmet needs related to timely diagnosis, treatment, monitoring and disease management. This narrative review explores the CHB landscape in the US, including gaps in patient care, the evolving therapeutic landscape, the clinical utility of serological biomarkers to improve outcomes and the experiences of people living with hepatitis B (PLWHB). Hepatitis B remains underdiagnosed and undertreated in the US, and current efforts are insufficient to meet the associated World Health Organization 2030 elimination targets. Latest guidelines from the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the Infectious Diseases Society of America, representing a North American perspective, signify a shift towards expanded treatment eligibility criteria and shared decision-making. Nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) are the current standard of care in the US, but functional cure is rarely achieved with NAs alone. Novel finite therapies targeting functional cure, such as antisense oligonucleotides, small interfering RNAs, immune modulators and combination or sequential regimens, are under investigation. Because of the unpredictable, complex nature of CHB, biomarkers such as quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen offer prognostic value for treatment decisions and could help guide individualised CHB management. PLWHB experience psychological impacts and health-related concerns, including fear of transmission and hepatitis B virus-related complications. Opportunities for improvement of CHB management include increased screening and linkage to care, development of more treatments targeting functional cure, adoption of serological biomarkers to inform treatment decisions and prioritising the lived experiences and preferences of PLWHB.

papers.title: The dual role of protein glycosylation in HBV infection: facilitating viral pathogenesis and shaping host defense
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B is the most prevalent chronic viral infection worldwide, posing a serious threat to global public health. Protein glycosylation, a critical post-translational modification, regulates diverse physiological processes. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with altered glycosylation of both viral and host proteins, which influences viral entry, immune evasion and disease progression, while HBV infection remodels host glycosylation. Given the sensitivity of glycosylation patterns to pathological perturbations, it is particularly relevant to examine how HBV exploits host glycosylation machinery to facilitate viral persistence and pathogenesis. This review is organised around a dual-role framework: one arm covers the proviral functions of glycosylation (viral entry, envelope protein folding, processing, assembly and secretion, persistence, immune escape and disease progression), the other the host-protective functions of the same pathways (glycosylation-dependent restriction factors, glycan-dependent ER quality control and ERAD, cellular stress responses and immune regulation). This exploration provides insights into the glycan-dependent mechanisms underlying HBV infection and their implications for developing novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Multidisciplinary management of disseminated tuberculosis with tuberculous meningitis and active hepatitis B in a critically ill pregnant woman in the third trimester: a case report
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Tuberculous meningitis (TBM) in pregnancy is rare but life-threatening, with substantial maternal and fetal risks. Third-trimester disseminated tuberculosis involving the central nervous system with concurrent active hepatitis B infection has scarcely been reported, particularly among remote pastoral populations with limited healthcare access. This report highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of this triple comorbidity and underscores the value of multidisciplinary team (MDT) management in such complex scenarios. Case presentation A 24-year-old pastoralist at 30 weeks of gestation presented with headache, vomiting, fever, and nuchal rigidity. Cerebrospinal fluidanalysis confirmed TBM, and chest computed tomography revealed diffuse miliary nodules suggestive of hematogenous disseminated tuberculosis. Serology was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, e-antigen, and core antibody, indicating active viral replication. Given life-threatening intracranial hypertension [intracranial pressure (ICP) > 330 mmH 2 O] in late pregnancy, osmotic agents were withheld for fetal safety, and lumbar cisternal drainage was performed. An MDT comprising respiratory medicine, obstetrics, hepatology, pharmacy, and critical care nursing specialties was assembled. Anti-tuberculosis therapy was intensified to isoniazid, rifampicin, linezolid, and moxifloxacin; ethambutol was discontinued due to fetal optic neuritis, and tenofovir was added for hepatitis B management. Following stabilization, the patient was transferred to a higher-level facility at 35 weeks of gestation and underwent cesarean section at 36 weeks, delivering a live preterm female infant (2320 g, 1-min Apgar score of 8). Both mother and neonate were discharged without complications on December 1, 2025. Conclusions This case demonstrates that early recognition, individualized anti-tuberculosis regimens, and coordinated multidisciplinary collaboration are critical for achieving favorable outcomes in pregnant patients with disseminated tuberculosis complicated by TBM and concurrent hepatitis B infection. The successful management relied on integrated critical care and a multidisciplinary approach, which proved effective even in resource-limited pastoral settings.

papers.title_zh: 妊娠晚期危重孕妇播散性结核病合并结核性脑膜炎和活动性乙型肝炎的多学科治疗:病例报告
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Tuberculous meningitis (TBM) in pregnancy is rare but life-threatening, with substantial maternal and fetal risks. Third-trimester disseminated tuberculosis involving the central nervous system with concurrent active hepatitis B infection has scarcely been reported, particularly among remote pastoral populations with limited healthcare access. Cerebrospinal fluidanalysis confirmed TBM, and chest computed tomography revealed diffuse miliary nodules suggestive of hematogenous disseminated tuberculosis. Serology was positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, e-antigen, and core antibody, indicating active viral replication. Given life-threatening intracranial hypertension [intracranial pressure (ICP) > 330 mmH 2 O] in late pregnancy, osmotic agents were withheld for fetal safety, and lumbar cisternal drainage was performed. An MDT comprising respiratory medicine, obstetrics, hepatology, pharmacy, and critical care nursing specialties was assembled. Anti-tuberculosis therapy was intensified to isoniazid, rifampicin, linezolid, and moxifloxacin; ethambutol was discontinued due to fetal optic neuritis, and tenofovir was added for hepatitis B management. Following stabilization, the patient was transferred to a higher-level facility at 35 weeks of gestation and underwent cesarean section at 36 weeks, delivering a live preterm female infant (2320 g, 1-min Apgar score of 8). Both mother and neonate were discharged without complications on December 1, 2025. Conclusions This case demonstrates that early recognition, individualized anti-tuberculosis regimens, and coordinated multidisciplinary collaboration are critical for achieving favorable outcomes in pregnant patients with disseminated tuberculosis complicated by TBM and concurrent hepatitis B infection. The successful management relied on integrated critical care and a multidisciplinary approach, which proved effective even in resource-limited pastoral settings.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 妊娠期结核性脑膜炎(TBM)很少见,但危及生命,对母体和胎儿具有很大的风险。妊娠晚期播散性结核病累及中枢神经系统并并发活动性乙型肝炎感染的报道很少,特别是在医疗保健机会有限的偏远牧区人群中。本报告强调了这种三重合并症的诊断和治疗挑战,并强调了多学科团队 (MDT) 管理在这种复杂情况下的价值。病例介绍 一名 24 岁牧民在妊娠 30 周时出现头痛、呕吐、发烧和颈项强直。脑脊液分析证实了 TBM,胸部计算机断层扫描显示弥漫性粟粒结节,提示血行播散性结核病。血清学乙型肝炎表面抗原、e抗原和核心抗体呈阳性,表明病毒复制活跃。由于妊娠晚期出现危及生命的颅内高压[颅内压(ICP)>330 mmH 2 O],为了胎儿安全,停用渗透剂,并进行腰大池引流。组建了包括呼吸内科、产科、肝病学、药学和重症监护护理专业的 MDT。抗结核治疗加强为异烟肼、利福平、利奈唑胺和莫西沙星;由于胎儿视神经炎而停用乙胺丁醇,并加用替诺福韦治疗乙型肝炎。病情稳定后,患者在妊娠 35 周时被转移到更高级别的机构,并在 36 周时接受剖腹产手术,产下一名活产早产女婴(2320 克,1 分钟阿普加评分为 8)。母亲和新生儿均于 2025 年 12 月 1 日出院,无并发症。结论 该病例表明,早期识别、个体化抗结核治疗方案和协调的多学科合作对于播散性结核病合并 TBM 并并发乙型肝炎感染的妊娠患者取得良好结局至关重要。成功的管理依赖于综合重症监护和多学科方法,即使在资源有限的牧区环境中,这种方法也被证明是有效的。

papers.title: Knowledge, attitudes, practices, and vaccination gaps related to hepatitis B among adolescents in a hyperendemic, fragile setting: A cross-sectional study from Mogadishu, Somalia.
papers.abstract: BackgroundHepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa, yet evidence on adolescents' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) toward HBV is limited in Somalia. This study assessed HBV-related KAP and associated factors among high school students in Mogadishu.ObjectivesTo assess HBV-related knowledge, attitudes, practices, and vaccination status among high school students in Mogadishu, Somalia, and identify associated factors.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 392 high school students using a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics summarized KAP levels. Associations between sociodemographic variables and KAP outcomes were examined using chi-square tests and logistic regression.ResultsAlthough 98.0% of students had heard of HBV, 63.0% of participants demonstrated good knowledge of hepatitis B, while 37.0% had poor knowledge. Positive attitudes toward HBV were reported by 27.0% of participants, whereas 73.0% had negative attitudes. Just over half of respondents (52.5%) reported good preventive practices, while 47.5% had poor practices. HBV vaccination coverage was 39.3%. In multivariable analysis, grade level was significantly associated with the KAP domains, although the pattern of association varied across knowledge, attitudes, and practices.ConclusionHigh school students in Mogadishu exhibited substantial gaps in HBV knowledge, negative attitudes, and low vaccination uptake. Educational grade level was a key determinant of HBV-related KAP, highlighting the need for targeted, school-based interventions to strengthen adolescent HBV prevention.
papers.journal: The International journal of risk & safety in medicine

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染仍然是撒哈拉以南非洲地区的一个主要公共卫生问题,但索马里青少年对 HBV 的知识、态度和做法 (KAP) 的证据有限。本研究旨在通过评估摩加迪沙高中生中与 HBV 相关的 KAP 和相关因素来解决这一差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对索马里摩加迪沙的 392 名高中生进行了一项横断面研究,以评估 HBV 相关知识、态度、实践和 疫苗接种 状况。该研究的重点是处于高流行、脆弱环境中的青少年。

elements_zh.main_results: 尽管98.0%的学生听说过乙型肝炎病毒,但63.0%的学生表现出良好的知识,而37.0%的学生则知识较差。27.0% 的参与者对 HBV 持积极态度,73.0% 的参与者持消极态度。超过一半的受访者 (52.5%) 报告了良好的预防措施,而 47.5% 的受访者报告了不良的预防措施。HBV 疫苗接种 覆盖率为 39.3%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管关联模式因知识、态度和实践而异,但年级水平与 KAP 领域显着相关。这凸显了需要采取有针对性的、以学校为基础的干预措施,以加强青少年乙型肝炎的预防。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了解决索马里青少年对乙型肝炎的知识差距和消极态度的重要性,这可以为制定更有效的学校预防策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,无法确定因果关系。然而,由于使用了统计分析和高流行环境中高中生的代表性样本,证据是强有力的。

papers.title: Hepatite B crônica: progressão da doença, complicações e estratégias terapêuticas — uma revisão narrativa da literatura Chronic Hepatitis B: disease progression, complications, and therapeutic strategies — a literature review
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B is an important public health problem due to its potential to progress to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Disease progression is influenced by viral, immunological, clínical, metabolic, and host-related factors, as well as by conditions associated with diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up. This study aimed to analyze the available evidence on the clinical progression of chronic hepatitis B, its main associated factors, complications, and therapeutic strategies. This is a narrative literature review based on searches conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, LILACS, and SciELO, considering publications from January 2015 to July 2026 in Portuguese, English, and Spanish. Scientific studies, clinical guidelines, and technical and normative documents addressing the natural history of infection, factors associated with disease progression, complications, and treatment were prioritized. The literature indicates that the progression of chronic hepatitis B results from the interaction between viral replication, immune response, and host characteristics, and may also be influenced by coinfections, alcohol consumption, metabolic disorders, and conditions affecting access to healthcare. Antiviral therapy plays a central role in suppressing viral replication and reducing the risk of disease progression, whereas longitudinal follow-up remains essential for identifying complications and stratifying risk. In conclusion, the management of chronic hepatitis B requires an integrated approach involving prevention, early diagnosis, individualized assessment, timely treatment, and continuous follow-up.

papers.title: Fusion of segmental right-lobe IVIM-DWI metrics and GPR for non-invasive assessment of chronic hepatitis B–related hepatic fibrosis: a pilot study
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: A segmental intravoxel incoherent motion diffusion-weighted imaging (IVIM-DWI)/gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase-to-platelet ratio (GPR) fusion model was evaluated for the non-invasive assessment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) fibrosis (controls vs. advanced) and compared with the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4). METHODS: This retrospective study included 139 participants: 42 healthy controls (HCs), 46 with early hepatic fibrosis (EHF), and 51 with advanced hepatic fibrosis (AHF). IVIM-DWI parameters (apparent diffusion coefficient, slow diffusion component, fast diffusion component, and perfusion fraction) were extracted from segmental analysis of the right hepatic lobe (segments V-VIII). The GPR, APRI, and FIB-4 were calculated from laboratory values. The IVIM + GPR fusion model was developed using logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap internal validation. RESULTS: For HCs vs. EHF, FIB-4 achieved the highest area under the curve [AUC; 0.911, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.844-0.969) followed by APRI (0.843, 95% CI: 0.755-0.923). The IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.745, 95% CI: 0.643-0.847) outperformed IVIM alone (AUC = 0.652) and GPR alone (AUC = 0.730) but did not outperform APRI or FIB-4. AHF, the IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.698) was comparable to APRI (0.573) and FIB-4 (0.637), with no significant differences among methods. CONCLUSION: FIB-4/APRI outperformed the fusion model for controls vs. early fibrosis, whereas fusion added no value over GPR for early vs. In the absence of a biopsy-proven S0 CHB group, HCs vs. EHF discriminates between HCs and established fibrosis rather than detecting incident fibrosis. The model should be considered, at most, a supplementary, opportunistic adjunct during abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) rather than a replacement for FIB-4/APRI. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The GPR uses only gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase and platelets, making it practical in resource- limited settings. The fusion model may provide supplementary, opportunistic information during abdominal MRI or when serum markers are confounded by extrahepatic factors, but it should remain complementary pending validation in larger cohorts; FIB-4 and APRI remain first-line where laboratory panels are available.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 139 participants: 42 healthy controls (HCs), 46 with early hepatic fibrosis (EHF), and 51 with advanced hepatic fibrosis (AHF). IVIM-DWI parameters (apparent diffusion coefficient, slow diffusion component, fast diffusion component, and perfusion fraction) were extracted from segmental analysis of the right hepatic lobe (segments V-VIII). The GPR, APRI, and FIB-4 were calculated from laboratory values. The IVIM + GPR fusion model was developed using logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap internal validation. RESULTS: For HCs vs. EHF, FIB-4 achieved the highest area under the curve [AUC; 0.911, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.844-0.969) followed by APRI (0.843, 95% CI: 0.755-0.923). The IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.745, 95% CI: 0.643-0.847) outperformed IVIM alone (AUC = 0.652) and GPR alone (AUC = 0.730) but did not outperform APRI or FIB-4. AHF, the IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.698) was comparable to APRI (0.573) and FIB-4 (0.637), with no significant differences among methods. CONCLUSION: FIB-4/APRI outperformed the fusion model for controls vs. early fibrosis, whereas fusion added no value over GPR for early vs. In the absence of a biopsy-proven S0 CHB group, HCs vs. EHF discriminates between HCs and established fibrosis rather than detecting incident fibrosis. The model should be considered, at most, a supplementary, opportunistic adjunct during abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) rather than a replacement for FIB-4/APRI. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The GPR uses only gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase and platelets, making it practical in resource- limited settings. The fusion model may provide supplementary, opportunistic information during abdominal MRI or when serum markers are confounded by extrahepatic factors, but it should remain complementary pending validation in larger cohorts; FIB-4 and APRI remain first-line where laboratory panels are available.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated a segmental IVIM-DWI/GPR fusion model for non-invasive assessment of chronic hepatitis B fibrosis, comparing it with APRI and FIB-4. The model showed improved performance over IVIM and GPR alone but was not superior to APRI or FIB-4 in distinguishing healthy controls from early fibrosis. For advanced fibrosis, the fusion model was comparable to APRI and FIB-4. The authors concluded that the fusion model may offer supplementary information during abdominal MRI or when serum markers are affected by extrahepatic factors, but it should not replace FIB-4 or APRI. The study's limitations include the absence of a biopsy-proven S0 CHB group, which restricts the model's ability to detect incident fibrosis. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the study's retrospective design and limited sample size.

papers.source_body_en: PURPOSE: A segmental intravoxel incoherent motion diffusion-weighted imaging (IVIM-DWI)/gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase-to-platelet ratio (GPR) fusion model was evaluated for the non-invasive assessment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) fibrosis (controls vs. advanced) and compared with the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4). IVIM-DWI parameters (apparent diffusion coefficient, slow diffusion component, fast diffusion component, and perfusion fraction) were extracted from segmental analysis of the right hepatic lobe (segments V-VIII). AHF, the IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.698) was comparable to APRI (0.573) and FIB-4 (0.637), with no significant differences among methods. CONCLUSION: FIB-4/APRI outperformed the fusion model for controls vs. early fibrosis, whereas fusion added no value over GPR for early vs. In the absence of a biopsy-proven S0 CHB group, HCs vs. EHF discriminates between HCs and established fibrosis rather than detecting incident fibrosis. The model should be considered, at most, a supplementary, opportunistic adjunct during abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) rather than a replacement for FIB-4/APRI. papers.title: Anti-Viral Treatment Eligibility and Treatment Uptake Among People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Australia: The REACH-B Study.
papers.abstract: Treatment indication for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) varies across clinical guidelines. This study evaluated treatment eligibility and uptake in a large Australian cohort of people with CHB. The REACH-B study recruited people with CHB managed through a national network of healthcare services. Participants were categorised into three groups: (1) receiving antiviral therapy; (2) untreated despite eligibility; (3) untreated and ineligible. Treatment eligibility was determined using Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) criteria, and by international clinical guidelines. Among 3648 participants (56% male; median age 48 years; 49% born in North-East or South-East Asia; 27% First Nations Australians), 14% were HBeAg positive and 7% had cirrhosis. Overall, 47% (n = 1666) were on antiviral therapy, 45% (n = 1573) were untreated and ineligible and 7% (n = 251) were untreated despite eligibility based on Australian PBS criteria. In adjusted analysis, the likelihood of remaining untreated despite eligibility was higher among women (aOR 1.59, 95% CI 1.34, 1.88) and younger participants (age 41-60 vs. > 60 years: aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.01-2.28; ≤ 40 vs. > 60 years: aOR 2.65, 95% CI 1.60, 4.40). The proportion untreated despite eligibility increased to 13% when applying 2024 World Health Organisation guidelines and ranged 2%-44% based on other guidelines, highlighting the variability across the guidelines. In conclusion, among REACH-B participants, most eligible individuals receive treatment. Lower treatment uptake among women and younger people despite eligibility partly reflects lower threshold for elevated ALT in women, and clinician determination of non-CHB related ALT elevation. As treatment guidelines evolve and eligibility criteria broaden, monitoring treatment patterns is important.

papers.source_body_en: Treatment indication for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) varies across clinical guidelines. This study evaluated treatment eligibility and uptake in a large Australian cohort of people with CHB. The REACH-B study recruited people with CHB managed through a national network of healthcare services. Participants were categorised into three groups: (1) receiving antiviral therapy; (2) untreated despite eligibility; (3) untreated and ineligible. Overall, 47% (n = 1666) were on antiviral therapy, 45% (n = 1573) were untreated and ineligible and 7% (n = 251) were untreated despite eligibility based on Australian PBS criteria. In adjusted analysis, the likelihood of remaining untreated despite eligibility was higher among women (aOR 1.59, 95% CI 1.34, 1.88) and younger participants (age 41-60 vs. > 60 years: aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.01-2.28; ≤ 40 vs. > 60 years: aOR 2.65, 95% CI 1.60, 4.40). The proportion untreated despite eligibility increased to 13% when applying 2024 World Health Organisation guidelines and ranged 2%-44% based on other guidelines, highlighting the variability across the guidelines. In conclusion, among REACH-B participants, most eligible individuals receive treatment. Lower treatment uptake among women and younger people despite eligibility partly reflects lower threshold for elevated ALT in women, and clinician determination of non-CHB related ALT elevation. As treatment guidelines evolve and eligibility criteria broaden, monitoring treatment patterns is important.

papers.title: Triple burden at the HIV–hepatitis B–malaria interface: viral–parasite interactions, epidemiological complexity and the case for integrated surveillance and community-based prevention in sub-Saharan Africa
papers.abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and malaria overlap across sub-Saharan Africa, yet they differ in how they spread, how long they last and how programmes measure success. This critical narrative review examines the evidence for biological interaction at each interface, the diagnostic and epidemiological traps that their overlap creates, and the case for integrated surveillance and community prevention. HIV-associated immunosuppression consistently increases the frequency and severity of malaria, and acute malaria transiently raises plasma HIV RNA. HIV accelerates the natural history of chronic HBV. Because HIV treatment and prevention are shifting towards regimens and long-acting products with no activity against HBV, a documented hepatitis B surface antigen result has become essential before any regimen change. Antiretroviral and antimalarial drugs also interact in clinically relevant ways. A direct interaction between HBV and Plasmodium is plausible, through interferon-mediated suppression of HBV during malaria, but it rests mainly on animal models and small, inconsistent human studies, and no reliable estimate of triple infection exists. Fever, anaemia and abnormal liver tests during malaria can mask a concurrent chronic viral infection, and routine facility data can produce apparent coinfection patterns that reflect testing intensity rather than biology. Drawing on the World Health Organization’s guidance on integrated disease surveillance and response, we describe a detect–verify–act approach that links community signals, confirmatory testing and confidential longitudinal records, while each infection keeps its own indicators and review cycle. Integration should rest on shared delivery, not on assumed shared pathogenesis, and prospective cohorts and implementation trials are needed to show whether it improves outcomes and equity.

papers.source_body_en: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and malaria overlap across sub-Saharan Africa, yet they differ in how they spread, how long they last and how programmes measure success. This critical narrative review examines the evidence for biological interaction at each interface, the diagnostic and epidemiological traps that their overlap creates, and the case for integrated surveillance and community prevention. HIV-associated immunosuppression consistently increases the frequency and severity of malaria, and acute malaria transiently raises plasma HIV RNA. HIV accelerates the natural history of chronic HBV. Because HIV treatment and prevention are shifting towards regimens and long-acting products with no activity against HBV, a documented hepatitis B surface antigen result has become essential before any regimen change. Antiretroviral and antimalarial drugs also interact in clinically relevant ways. A direct interaction between HBV and Plasmodium is plausible, through interferon-mediated suppression of HBV during malaria, but it rests mainly on animal models and small, inconsistent human studies, and no reliable estimate of triple infection exists. Fever, anaemia and abnormal liver tests during malaria can mask a concurrent chronic viral infection, and routine facility data can produce apparent coinfection patterns that reflect testing intensity rather than biology. Drawing on the World Health Organization’s guidance on integrated disease surveillance and response, we describe a detect–verify–act approach that links community signals, confirmatory testing and confidential longitudinal records, while each infection keeps its own indicators and review cycle. Integration should rest on shared delivery, not on assumed shared pathogenesis, and prospective cohorts and implementation trials are needed to show whether it improves outcomes and equity.

papers.title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
papers.abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of reliable methods for predicting individual treatment response in chronic hepatitis B patients, as long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in some individuals but not all.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This opinion review discusses the potential of machine learning to improve prediction of fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B, focusing on clinical tools that are limited in capturing dynamic fibrosis processes.
analysis.methods: The authors review how machine learning can be applied to analyze images, integrate clinical and pathological data, and predict treatment response through serial measurements during antiviral therapy.
analysis.main_results: Machine learning has shown early but encouraging results in three areas: quantitative image analysis, multimodal integration of clinical and pathological data, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that machine learning's greatest value lies in complementing existing tools, particularly for identifying patients unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone, rather than replacing them.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that machine learning could enhance surveillance and personalized treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B, improving the prediction of fibrosis reversal and guiding clinical decisions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the fact that most current models are developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, which may affect their generalizability and require prospective multi-center validation.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of machine learning to improve the prediction of liver fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B patients. It highlights the limitations of conventional clinical tools in capturing dynamic fibrosis processes and emphasizes the need for more robust models. The authors argue that machine learning can complement existing methods by identifying patients who may not benefit from antiviral therapy alone. While the study is an opinion review, it suggests that integrating clinical and pathological data through machine learning could enhance surveillance and treatment strategies. The evidence is based on existing models, which are limited by their derivation from small, single-center cohorts. The findings indicate that machine learning may offer new insights into personalized prediction but require further validation for broader clinical application.

papers.title_zh: 通过机器学习实现针对慢性乙型肝炎相关肝纤维化的个性化预测
papers.source_body_en: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

papers.title: Disruption of the NTCP–EGFR receptor complex as a strategy for selective inhibition of hepatitis B and D virus entry
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) enter hepatocytes through a coordinated process mediated by a receptor complex consisting of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), and host entry cofactors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Here, we established an in vitro assay to evaluate the NTCP–EGFR interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupted this molecular interaction. Oxy229 selectively inhibited HBV and HDV infection to HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes. Mechanistic analysis revealed that Oxy229 impaired the relocalization of HBV–NTCP complex from the plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles. Notably, Oxy229 did not compromise the physiological functions of NTCP and EGFR, i.e., bile acid transporter and activation of downstream EGFR signaling pathways including Ras–MAPK and PI3K–Akt pathways, indicating selective inhibition of viral entry. Compound derivative analysis identified Oxy283, which acquired dual inhibitory activity against both NTCP–EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization, resulting in enhanced anti-HBV potency. These findings establish the functional significance of NTCP–receptor complex formation in the HBV/HDV entry and highlight this machinery as a potential target for antiviral intervention.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mechanism of hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) entry into hepatocytes, focusing on the NTCP–EGFR receptor complex. The researchers developed an in vitro assay to evaluate this interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupts the complex, selectively inhibiting HBV and HDV infection without affecting NTCP or EGFR physiological functions. Further analysis revealed that Oxy283, a derivative of Oxy229, has enhanced anti-HBV potency by targeting both NTCP–EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization. These findings highlight the NTCP–receptor complex as a potential antiviral target. The study's evidence is strong, as it is based on direct mechanistic analysis and selective inhibition of viral entry. However, the findings are limited to in vitro settings and do not include clinical or in vivo data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 乙型和丁型肝炎病毒(HBV、HDV)通过受体复合物介导的协调过程进入肝细胞,该受体复合物由牛磺胆酸钠共转运多肽(NTCP)和宿主进入辅助因子(包括表皮生长因子受体(EGFR))组成。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这里,我们建立了一种体外测定法来评估 NTCP-EGFR 相互作用,并鉴定出 Oxy229,一种基于氧甾醇的化合物,可以破坏这种分子相互作用。
elements_zh.methods: Oxy229 选择性抑制 HBV 和 HDV 对 HepG2-NTCP 细胞和原代人肝细胞的感染。
elements_zh.main_results: 机制分析表明,Oxy229 损害了 HBV-NTCP 复合物从质膜到细胞内囊泡的重新定位。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 值得注意的是,Oxy229 不会损害 NTCP 和 EGFR 的生理功能,即胆汁酸转运蛋白和下游 EGFR 信号通路(包括 Ras-MAPK 和 PI3K-Akt 通路)的激活,表明对病毒进入的选择性抑制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 化合物衍生物分析确定了 Oxy283,它获得了针对 NTCP-EGFR 相互作用和 NTCP 多聚化的双重抑制活性,从而增强了抗 HBV 效力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些发现确立了 NTCP-受体复合物形成在 HBV/HDV 进入中的功能意义,并强调该机制作为 抗病毒药物 干预的潜在目标。

papers.title: Nucleos(t)ide analogue discontinuation strategy to achieve the functional cure for chronic hepatitis B? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Functional cure rate is low during continuous nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy, and therapy suspension has demonstrated interesting off-treatment responses. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate how stable, HBsAg positive-virally suppressed patients would respond to drug discontinuation in terms of HBsAg clearance, clinical remission, virological relapses, alanine-aminotransferases (ALT) flares, and necessity of therapy reintroduction were performed. Included studies were prospective, experimental and observational studies, including data on outcomes after NA discontinuation in HBV DNA negative patients with positive HBsAg, involving at least 20 patients receiving entecavir or tenofovir, published from 2008 to February 2026, written in English language. RESULTS: A total of 28 papers (4495 patients) were included in the analysis, with low risk of bias: HBsAg clearance rate at 24, 48 and 96 weeks were of 3%, 8% and 11% (95% IC 1-8%, 4-15%, 7-15%) respectively, with low to moderate heterogeneity (I2=58.4%%, 66.5%, 47.3%); according to the HBeAg status at NA introduction, in those HBeAg negative the HBsAg clearance rates were 3%, 8% and 10% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively, while in those HBeAg positive 2.3 and 3.4% at 24 and 48 weeks, respectively. Overall a higher HBsAg clearance rate (39% at 96 weeks, 95% CI=10-78%, I2=83.3%) was described in patients with HBsAg <100 UI/ml at discontinuation. Treatment reintroduction due to virological and clinical relapse rates were 21%, 12%, and 17% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: These results showed an overall low rate of HBsAg clearance after NA discontinuation, except for the patients with low HBsAg titers at this time. Thus, NA discontinuation must be balanced in the single case for the risk of virological and clinical relapses.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the response of HBV-infected patients to nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) discontinuation. The study included 28 papers with 4495 patients, focusing on HBsAg clearance, clinical remission, and relapse rates. The findings indicated a low HBsAg clearance rate after NA discontinuation, with rates of 3%, 8%, and 11% at 24, 48, and 96 weeks, respectively. The results emphasize the need for careful consideration of NA discontinuation in individual cases due to the risk of relapse.

papers.title: Evaluation of point-of-care testing (POCT) for blood-borne infections in forensic autopsy specimens.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA)-based point-of-care testing (POCT) for viral antigen and antibody detection enables rapid screening for blood-borne viral infections and may be particularly valuable in forensic autopsy settings, where incomplete antemortem medical histories and invasive procedures increase the risk of occupational exposure. However, its performance in postmortem specimens remains unclear. We evaluated the applicability of LFIA-based POCT for detecting human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and hepatitis B virus (HBV) in autopsy specimens, focusing on postmortem decomposition and the use of solid organ tissues as alternatives to blood. A total of 309 cases were analyzed using LFIA and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) across blood, liver, and spleen specimens. Agreement was assessed using overall, positive, and negative percent agreement and Cohen’s kappa coefficient ( κ ). Positivity rates were compared by specimen type and decomposition status. LFIA agreement with qPCR varied by marker and specimen type, with substantial agreement for HIV and HCV antibody detection in blood and lower agreement in liver and spleen. Fresh specimens generally demonstrated higher LFIA positivity rates than decomposed specimens. Among specimens meeting predefined qPCR positivity criteria, LFIA-positive specimens tended to exhibit higher viral loads than LFIA-negative specimens, reaching statistical significance for HBV in liver, with similar but non-significant trends for blood HBV and liver HCV. LFIA-based POCT may serve as a preliminary screening tool in postmortem settings, particularly when blood is available. Nevertheless, negative results do not exclude infection—especially with low viral loads or advanced decomposition—and should be confirmed by molecular testing. IMPORTANCE Forensic personnel performing autopsies face significant occupational risks from exposure to blood-borne viruses, including human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B virus, and hepatitis C virus. Unlike clinical settings, forensic autopsies frequently involve bodies with unknown infection histories, making rapid infection screening essential for personnel safety. Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA)-based point-of-care testing (POCT) for viral antigen and antibody detection offers a rapid, infrastructure-free screening option; however, its performance in postmortem specimens has not been systematically evaluated. This study suggests that rapid immunochromatographic POCT may serve as a preliminary screening tool in forensic autopsy settings, particularly when blood specimens are available. However, a negative result does not exclude infection, especially in cases with low viral load or advanced decomposition, and confirmatory molecular testing remains necessary. These findings provide practical guidance for forensic professionals on appropriate specimen selection and interpretation of LFIA results, ultimately supporting safer autopsy practices.

papers.title_zh: 法医尸检标本中血源性感染的即时检测(POCT)评估。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA)-based point-of-care testing (POCT) for viral antigen and antibody detection enables rapid screening for blood-borne viral infections and may be particularly valuable in forensic autopsy settings, where incomplete antemortem medical histories and invasive procedures increase the risk of occupational exposure. However, its performance in postmortem specimens remains unclear. We evaluated the applicability of LFIA-based POCT for detecting human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and hepatitis B virus (HBV) in autopsy specimens, focusing on postmortem decomposition and the use of solid organ tissues as alternatives to blood. A total of 309 cases were analyzed using LFIA and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) across blood, liver, and spleen specimens. Agreement was assessed using overall, positive, and negative percent agreement and Cohen’s kappa coefficient ( κ ). Positivity rates were compared by specimen type and decomposition status. LFIA agreement with qPCR varied by marker and specimen type, with substantial agreement for HIV and HCV antibody detection in blood and lower agreement in liver and spleen. Fresh specimens generally demonstrated higher LFIA positivity rates than decomposed specimens. Among specimens meeting predefined qPCR positivity criteria, LFIA-positive specimens tended to exhibit higher viral loads than LFIA-negative specimens, reaching statistical significance for HBV in liver, with similar but non-significant trends for blood HBV and liver HCV. LFIA-based POCT may serve as a preliminary screening tool in postmortem settings, particularly when blood is available. Nevertheless, negative results do not exclude infection—especially with low viral loads or advanced decomposition—and should be confirmed by molecular testing. IMPORTANCE Forensic personnel performing autopsies face significant occupational risks from exposure to blood-borne viruses, including human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B virus, and hepatitis C virus. Unlike clinical settings, forensic autopsies frequently involve bodies with unknown infection histories, making rapid infection screening essential for personnel safety. Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA)-based point-of-care testing (POCT) for viral antigen and antibody detection offers a rapid, infrastructure-free screening option; however, its performance in postmortem specimens has not been systematically evaluated. This study suggests that rapid immunochromatographic POCT may serve as a preliminary screening tool in forensic autopsy settings, particularly when blood specimens are available. However, a negative result does not exclude infection, especially in cases with low viral load or advanced decomposition, and confirmatory molecular testing remains necessary. These findings provide practical guidance for forensic professionals on appropriate specimen selection and interpretation of LFIA results, ultimately supporting safer autopsy practices.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 基于侧流免疫分析 (LFIA) 的病毒抗原和抗体检测即时检测 (POCT) 能够快速筛查血源性病毒感染,在法医尸检环境中可能特别有价值,因为在法医尸检环境中,不完整的生前病史和侵入性操作会增加职业暴露的风险。然而,其在尸检标本中的表现仍不清楚。我们评估了基于 LFIA 的 POCT 在检测尸检标本中人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV)、丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 和 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 方面的适用性,重点关注死后分解和使用实体器官组织作为血液替代品。使用 LFIA 和定量聚合酶链反应 (qPCR) 对血液、肝脏和脾脏标本总共 309 例进行了分析。使用总体一致性百分比、正一致性百分比和负一致性百分比以及 Cohen 的 kappa 系数 (κ) 来评估一致性。根据标本类型和分解状态比较阳性率。LFIA 与 qPCR 的一致性因标记物和样本类型而异,血液中 HIV 和 HCV 抗体检测的一致性较高,而肝脏和脾脏的一致性较低。新鲜标本的 LFIA 阳性率通常高于腐烂标本。在符合预定 qPCR 阳性标准的标本中,LFIA 阳性标本往往比 LFIA 阴性标本表现出更高的病毒载量,肝脏中 HBV 达到统计学显着性,血液 HBV 和肝脏 HCV 具有相似但不显着的趋势。基于 LFIA 的 POCT 可以作为尸检中的初步筛查工具,特别是在有血液的情况下。然而,阴性结果并不能排除感染,尤其是病毒载量较低或分解较严重的情况,应通过分子检测来确认。重要性 进行尸检的法医人员面临着暴露于血源性病毒(包括人类免疫缺陷病毒、乙型肝炎病毒 和丙型肝炎病毒)的重大职业风险。与临床环境不同,法医尸检经常涉及感染史未知的尸体,因此快速感染筛查对于人员安全至关重要。基于侧流免疫分析 (LFIA) 的病毒抗原和抗体检测即时检测 (POCT) 提供了一种快速、无需基础设施的筛查选项;然而,其在尸检标本中的性能尚未得到系统评估。这项研究表明,快速免疫层析 POCT 可以作为法医尸检环境中的初步筛查工具,特别是在有血液样本的情况下。然而,阴性结果并不能排除感染,特别是在病毒载量低或分解严重的情况下,仍然需要进行确认性分子检测。这些发现为法医专业人员适当选择标本和解释 LFIA 结果提供了实用指导,最终支持更安全的尸检实践。

papers.title: Evaluation of Anti-HBs Levels in Children Who Received Three Doses of Hepatitis B Vaccine According to Age Groups and Gestational Age: A Retrospective Single-Center Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Anti-HBs levels decline after infant hepatitis B vaccination, especially during school age and adolescence, but data evaluating both age and gestational age-related effects in a large pediatric cohort remain limited. Methods In this retrospective, single-center, cross-sectional study, we included 6,510 children aged 9 months–18 years who had completed three hepatitis B vaccine doses and had at least one quantitative anti-HBs measurement between 2021 and 2023. Seronegativity was defined as anti-HBs < 10 mIU/mL. Children were grouped by age (9 months–5 years, 6–11 years, 12–18 years) and gestational age (early preterm < 32 weeks, late preterm 32–36+6 weeks, term ≥ 37 weeks). Comparisons used Kruskal–Wallis, chi-square, ANCOVA, and logistic regression. Results Overall seronegativity was 30.6% (1,989/6,510), and the median anti-HBs level was 34.30 mIU/mL (IQR 6.72–143.23). Anti-HBs levels decreased significantly with age (medians 99.17, 23.94, and 12.55 mIU/mL for the 9 months–5 years, 6–11 years, and 12–18 years groups; p < 0.001), while seronegativity increased (14.4%, 33.9%, and 45.5%; p < 0.001). Age group was the strongest independent predictor of seronegativity (6–11 years: OR 3.218, 95% CI 2.521–4.108; 12–18 years: OR 5.348, 95% CI 4.183–6.839). Among 4,242 children with gestational age data, gestational age was not independently associated with seronegativity after adjustment (p = 0.109), and seronegativity rates were comparable across groups (34.5% early preterm, 25.8% late preterm, 36.9% term; p = 0.168). In children born at term, mean anti-HBs was 525.05 ± 401.31 mIU/mL at ≤ 3 years versus 74.99 ± 143.60 mIU/mL at ≥ 4 years. Conclusion Anti-HBs levels decline significantly with age after three-dose hepatitis B vaccination, whereas gestational age is not an independent predictor of seronegativity. Targeted serological follow-up and individualized booster strategies, particularly for high-risk groups, may be warranted.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated anti-HBs levels in children who received three doses of hepatitis B vaccine, focusing on age and gestational age effects. It found that seronegativity increased significantly with age, while gestational age was not independently associated with seronegativity. The results highlight the need for targeted serological follow-up and individualized booster strategies, especially for high-risk groups. The study's retrospective, single-center design may limit generalizability, but the large sample size and statistical methods support its findings. These results contribute to understanding the long-term immune response to hepatitis B vaccination in children and may inform future vaccination strategies.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项回顾性、单中心、横断面研究涉及 6,510 名 9 个月至 18 岁的儿童,他们在 2021 年至 2023 年间完成了三剂乙型肝炎 疫苗 剂量,并至少进行了一次定量抗 HBs 测量。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用了 Kruskal-Wallis、卡方、ANCOVA 和逻辑回归等统计方法来比较不同年龄组和胎龄类别的抗 HBs 水平和血清阴性。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体血清阴性率为 30.6% (1,989/6,510),中位抗 HBs 水平为 34.30 mIU/mL (IQR 6.72–143.23)。抗 HBs 水平随着年龄的增长而显着下降,而血清阴性水平则随着年龄组的增加而增加。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,在接受三剂乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 后,抗 HBs 水平随着年龄的增长而显着下降,并且未发现孕龄是血清阴性的独立预测因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,有针对性的血清学随访和个体化加强策略可能是必要的,特别是对于高危人群,以保持足够的乙型肝炎免疫力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和单中心设置而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。然而,由于样本量大和统计调整,证据是强有力的。

Received 3 August, 2026; Accepted 13 October, 2026 Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease. In Côte d’Ivoire, HDV is systematic not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)- positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication. This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAg- positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI), using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). A cross-sectional study based on a non-probability convenience sample was conducted in March 2021. HDV RNA was detected by nested RT-PCR targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888–1122 and 313–485). Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and and mean age was 37 ± 9 years. HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%). Among them, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity 90.7% (39/43). This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data not the entire cohort of 51 donors. HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia. Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates. These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection. Key words: Hepatitis B virus/hepatitis delta virus (HBV/HDV) co-infection, nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), molecular epidemiology, convenience sample, transfusion medicine, West Africa. INTRODUCTION Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most widespread infectious agents worldwide. An estimated 254 million people were living with chronic HBV infection in 2022, resulting in approximately 1.1 million deaths, while only 13% of carriers had been diagnosed and 3% had received treatment (World Health Organization [WHO], 2024). Sub-Saharan Africa bears a disproportionate share of this burden, with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) prevalence exceeding 8% in many areas and estimated at 9 to 12% among the general adult population in Côte d’Ivoire (WHO, 2021). A meta-analysis involving more than 3.5 million African blood donors reported a pooled HBsAg seroprevalence of 10.09% in West Africa, the highest among the continent’s five regions (Quintas et al., 2024). This substantial burden is consistent with findings indicating that HBsAg prevalence among blood donors at the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI) remained stable over two decades (Seri et al., 2018). Hepatitis delta virus (HDV), first described by Rizzetto in 1977 (Rizzetto et al., 1980), is a defective RNA virus that depends on HBV surface antigen for its replication and transmission. Consequently, HDV infection occurs only in HBsAg-positive individuals, either through simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection or through HDV superinfection in individuals with pre-existing chronic HBV infection. Approximately 90% of individuals with chronic HBV infection who acquire HDV superinfection progress to chronic HDV infection, whereas simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection is usually resolved, although serological markers may persist without ongoing viral replication (Rizzetto et al., 2021). This distinction is important when comparing anti-HDV antibody prevalence, which indicates previous or current exposure, with HDV RNA positivity, which provides evidence of active viral replication. HBV/HDV coinfection is associated with more severe liver disease than HBV monoinfection, increasing the risk of cirrhosis by approximately two- to three-fold and the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma by approximately two-fold. Cirrhosis may develop in 70 to 80% of affected patients within 5 to 10 years (Fattovich et al., 2000; Negro, 2014; Noureddin and Gish, 2014). Globally, an estimated 15–20 million HBsAg-positive individuals are thought to have HDV infection, although these estimates may be inflated when subpopulation weighting is not adequately considered (Rizzetto, 2015; Polaris Observatory Collaborators, 2024). Data on HDV infection in sub-Saharan Africa remain limited and heterogeneous. Reported anti-HDV seroprevalence ranges from approximately 7% in pooled estimates for West Africa to more than 25% in Central Africa (Stockdale et al., 2017). Country-specific estimates also vary considerably, ranging from 1 to 54% in Cameroon (Besombes et al., 2020), 7 to 22% in Mauritania (Mansour et al., 2012; Lunel-Fabiani et al., 2013), and 8 to 9% in Nigeria (Opaleye et al., 2016). In Senegal, active HDV replication confirmed by RNA testing was detected in 61.5% of anti-HDV-seropositive individuals, despite an Dechi et al. 21 overall anti-HDV seroprevalence of only 1.5% (Wembulua et al., 2025). These findings illustrate the distinction between antibody-based estimates of exposure and RNA- based evidence of active infection. Before the present study, published data on HBV/HDV coinfection in Côte d’Ivoire were very limited. Received 3 August, 2026; Accepted 13 October, 2026 Chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection exacerbates hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver disease. In Côte d’Ivoire, HDV is systematic not systematically screened among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)- positive blood donors, and most regional estimates rely on anti-HDV serology, which indicates exposure but not active replication. This study aimed to determine HDV RNA replication positivity among HBsAg- positive blood donors followed at the Blood Donor Medical Follow-up Centre (CMSDS) of the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI), using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). A cross-sectional study based on a non-probability convenience sample was conducted in March 2021. HDV RNA was detected by nested RT-PCR targeting two genomic regions (nucleotides 888–1122 and 313–485). Of 51 donors included, 75% were male (n = 38) and and mean age was 37 ± 9 years. HBV DNA results were available for 43 donors (84%). Among them, HDV RNA positivity was 88.9% (32/36) in those with detectable HBV viraemia and 100% (7/7) in those with undetectable viral load, giving an overall positivity 90.7% (39/43). This figure applies only to donors with available viral load data not the entire cohort of 51 donors. HDV RNA was also detected in donors receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with suppressed HBV viraemia. Given the convenience sample of donors already in follow-up care, findings are hypothesis-generating rather than population-level estimates. These results support larger representative studies and systematic HDV screening during follow-up of individuals with chronic HBV infection. INTRODUCTION Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most widespread infectious agents worldwide. An estimated 254 million people were living with chronic HBV infection in 2022, resulting in approximately 1.1 million deaths, while only 13% of carriers had been diagnosed and 3% had received treatment (World Health Organization [WHO], 2024). Sub-Saharan Africa bears a disproportionate share of this burden, with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) prevalence exceeding 8% in many areas and estimated at 9 to 12% among the general adult population in Côte d’Ivoire (WHO, 2021). A meta-analysis involving more than 3.5 million African blood donors reported a pooled HBsAg seroprevalence of 10.09% in West Africa, the highest among the continent’s five regions (Quintas et al., 2024). This substantial burden is consistent with findings indicating that HBsAg prevalence among blood donors at the National Blood Transfusion Centre of Côte d’Ivoire (CNTSCI) remained stable over two decades (Seri et al., 2018). Hepatitis delta virus (HDV), first described by Rizzetto in 1977 (Rizzetto et al., 1980), is a defective RNA virus that depends on HBV surface antigen for its replication and transmission. Consequently, HDV infection occurs only in HBsAg-positive individuals, either through simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection or through HDV superinfection in individuals with pre-existing chronic HBV infection. Approximately 90% of individuals with chronic HBV infection who acquire HDV superinfection progress to chronic HDV infection, whereas simultaneous HBV/HDV coinfection is usually resolved, although serological markers may persist without ongoing viral replication (Rizzetto et al., 2021). This distinction is important when comparing anti-HDV antibody prevalence, which indicates previous or current exposure, with HDV RNA positivity, which provides evidence of active viral replication. HBV/HDV coinfection is associated with more severe liver disease than HBV monoinfection, increasing the risk of cirrhosis by approximately two- to three-fold and the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma by approximately two-fold. Cirrhosis may develop in 70 to 80% of affected patients within 5 to 10 years (Fattovich et al., 2000; Negro, 2014; Noureddin and Gish, 2014). analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) RNA replication among hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive blood donors in Côte d'Ivoire. Using nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), HDV RNA was detected in two genomic regions. Of 51 donors, 43 had HBV DNA results, with 90.7% showing HDV RNA positivity. Notably, HDV RNA was detected in donors with suppressed HBV viraemia on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF). The study, based on a convenience sample, is hypothesis-generating and underscores the need for systematic HDV screening in chronic HBV patients. However, it does not provide population-level estimates due to its limited scope.

papers.abstract_zh: 慢性丁型肝炎病毒 (HDV) 感染会加剧 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 相关肝病。在科特迪瓦,未对乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 阳性献血者进行系统性筛查,大多数区域估计依赖于抗 HDV 血清学,这表明暴露但不活跃复制。本研究旨在确定 HBsAg 阳性献血者中 HDV RNA 复制阳性情况。科特迪瓦国家输血中心 (CNTSCI) 的献血者医疗随访中心 (CMSDS) 使用巢式逆转录聚合酶链式反应 (RT-PCR)。2021 年 3 月进行了一项基于非概率便利样本的横断面研究。通过针对两个基因组区域(核苷酸 888-1122 和 313-485)的巢式 RT-PCR 检测了 HDV RNA。51 名捐献者中其中,75% 为男性 (n = 38),平均年龄为 37 ± 9 岁。43 名捐献者 (84%) 可获得 HBV DNA 结果。其中,可检测到 HBV 病毒血症的 HDV RNA 阳性率为 88.9% (32/36),病毒载量无法检测到的患者为 100% (7/7),总体阳性率为 90.7% (39/43)。该数字仅适用于具有可用病毒载量数据的捐献者,而不是 51 名捐献者的全部 队列研究。在接受富马酸替诺福韦二吡呋酯 (TDF) 且 HBV 病毒血症受到抑制的捐献者中也检测到 HDV RNA。考虑到已经处于后续护理中的捐献者的方便样本,研究结果是假设生成而不是人群水平估计。这些结果支持更大规模的代表性研究和个体随访期间的系统性 HDV 筛查关键词:乙型肝炎病毒/丁型肝炎病毒(HBV/HDV)合并感染,巢式逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR),分子流行病学,方便样本,输血医学,西非。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在利用巢式逆转录聚合酶链反应 (RT-PCR) 确定在科特迪瓦国家输血中心 (CNTSCI) 的献血者医疗随访中心 (CMSDS) 随访的 HBsAg 阳性献血者中 HDV RNA 复制阳性情况。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2021 年 3 月进行了一项基于非概率便利样本的横断面研究。在 51 名捐赠者中,75% 为男性 (n = 38),平均年龄为 37 ± 9 岁。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过针对两个基因组区域(核苷酸 888-1122 和 313-485)的巢式 RT-PCR 检测 HDV RNA。43 名捐献者 (84%) 可获得 HBV DNA 结果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 43 名有 HBV DNA 结果的捐献者中,可检测到 HBV 病毒血症的 HDV RNA 阳性率为 88.9% (32/36),而病毒载量未检测到的捐献者则为 100% (7/7),总体阳性率为 90.7% (39/43)。在接受富马酸替诺福韦二吡呋酯 (TDF) 且 HBV 病毒血症受到抑制的捐赠者中也检测到了 HDV RNA。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果支持在慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染者的随访过程中进行更大规模的代表性研究和系统性丁型肝炎病毒筛查。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了对慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染者进行系统性丁型肝炎病毒筛查的必要性,特别是在没有常规检测丁型肝炎病毒的地区。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 考虑到已经接受后续护理的捐赠者的方便样本,研究结果是假设生成而不是人口水平的估计。
