papers.title: Interferon therapy reduces incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with high risk of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND The proportion of patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is as high as 85.69% among HCC patients in China. Current anti-HBV drugs include nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs) and interferon (IFN). AIM To compare the impact of NAs and IFN therapy on the occurrence of HCC in patients at high risk of HBV-related HCC. METHODS We enrolled 368 patients with high risk of HBV-related HCC, and 120 received subcutaneous injections of IFN, with or without NAs, constituting the IFN group. The remaining 248 patients were assigned to the NAs group, and received treatment with NAs alone. RESULTS For patients with a high risk of HBV-related HCC, after a 5-year treatment period, HCC incidence in the IFN group was 2.54%, while the NAs group showed a significantly higher incidence of 25.74% (P CONCLUSION IFN-based therapy, compared with NAs, significantly reduced the risk of HCC in patients with high risk of HBV-related HCC.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 368 patients with high risk of HBV-related HCC, with 120 patients receiving IFN therapy (with or without NAs) and 248 patients receiving NA therapy alone.
analysis.methods: Patients were enrolled and followed for a 5-year treatment period. HCC incidence was monitored and compared between the IFN group and the NAs group using statistical analysis to determine significance.
analysis.main_results: After 5 years of treatment, the HCC incidence in the IFN group was 2.54%, while the NAs group had a significantly higher incidence of 25.74% (P < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that IFN-based therapy significantly reduces HCC risk compared to NAs alone in high-risk HBV patients, highlighting a novel therapeutic approach.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that IFN-based therapy could be a more effective option for reducing HCC incidence in patients at high risk of HBV-related HCC, potentially informing treatment guidelines and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the clear comparison between IFN and NAs groups and the statistically significant results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of interferon (IFN) therapy versus nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs) on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence in patients at high risk of HBV-related HCC. The research aimed to address the high prevalence of HBV-related HCC in China and evaluate therapeutic efficacy. A retrospective cohort study enrolled 368 patients, with 120 receiving IFN therapy and 248 receiving NA therapy alone. After 5 years, HCC incidence was 2.54% in the IFN group and 25.74% in the NAs group (P < 0.001). The authors concluded that IFN-based therapy significantly reduces HCC risk compared to NAs alone, offering a novel therapeutic approach. These findings may inform treatment guidelines for high-risk HBV patients. The study's retrospective design introduces potential limitations, but the results are robust due to the clear comparison and statistical significance.

papers.title: Clonorchis sinensis co-infection potentiates polymorphonuclear-myeloid-derived suppressor cells expansion and metabolic reprogramming in chronic hepatitis B patients
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Clonorchis sinensis (C. sinensis ) co-infection is known to accelerate disease progression and induce immune tolerance in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV), particularly in regions where both infections are endemic. Metabolic reprogramming has emerged as a key driver of immunosuppression. These metabolic shifts are often orchestrated by myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), which expand during chronic infections to promote immune tolerance. sinensis co-infection reprograms metabolism to favor MDSC-linked suppression and how this process relates to normal liver enzyme levels remains unclear. AIM To investigate whether C. sinensis co-infection induces MDSC- linked metabolic reprogramming in patients with HBV and normal liver enzyme levels. METHODS In this cross-sectional study, a total of 117 participants were enrolled and assigned to four groups: Healthy controls (n = 30), C. sinensis mono-infected participants (n = 29), HBV mono-infected participants (n = 28), and co-infected participants (n = 30). Serum cytokine profiles were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, amino acid metabolites using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and MDSC subsets using flow cytometry. Spearman correlation and mediation analyses were performed to explore the relationships among inflammation, metabolism, and immunity. RESULTS HBV mono-infected and co-infected patients showed no statistically significant differences in liver enzyme and HBV DNA levels. However, compared with the HBV mono-infected group, the co-infected group had higher levels of the inflammatory cytokine: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), accompanied by markedly lower interferon-γ (IFN-γ) levels. Flow cytometric assay revealed that polymorphonuclear MDSCs (PMN-MDSCs) showed the greatest expansion in the co-infected group, and their proportion correlated strongly with IL-6 and TNF-α levels. Metabolically, the co-infected group had a significantly higher ornithine-to-arginine ratio. Mediation analysis suggested that PMN-MDSCs accounted for approximately 45% of the total effect of IL-6 on IFN-γ suppression. sinensis co-infection was associated with immunosuppression through IL-6/TNF-α-linked PMN-MDSC expansion and elevated ornithine-to-arginine ratio, resulting in suppressed IFN-γ production despite normal liver enzyme levels.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of Clonorchis sinensis co-infection on immune and metabolic profiles in patients with HBV and normal liver enzyme levels. A cross-sectional design was used, enrolling 117 participants into four groups. Methods included cytokine profiling, amino acid metabolite analysis, and flow cytometry to assess MDSC subsets. Results showed no significant differences in liver enzymes or HBV DNA levels between HBV mono-infected and co-infected patients, but co-infected individuals had higher IL-6 and TNF-α levels and lower IFN-γ levels. Mediation analysis indicated that PMN-MDSCs accounted for 45% of the effect of IL-6 on IFN-γ suppression. The authors suggest that C. sinensis co-infection may induce immunosuppression through IL-6/TNF-α-linked PMN-MDSC expansion and metabolic shifts. The study's findings may inform future research on immune modulation in HBV co-infection scenarios, though the cross-sectional design limits causal inference. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on correlational data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨华支睾吸虫合并感染是否会在肝酶水平正常的 HBV 患者中诱导 MDSC 相关的代谢重编程。背景强调,已知中华支原体合并感染会加速乙型肝炎患者的疾病进展并诱导免疫耐受,特别是在流行地区。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面研究纳入了 117 名参与者,分为四组:健康对照(n = 30)、中华支原体单一感染参与者(n = 29)、HBV 单一感染参与者(n = 28)和混合感染参与者(n = 30)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用化学发光免疫测定法测量血清细胞因子谱,使用液相色谱-串联质谱法测量氨基酸代谢物,并使用流式细胞术测量MDSC子集。流式细胞术检测显示,多形核MDSC(PMN-MDSC)在共感染组中表现出最大的扩增,并且其比例与IL-6和TNF-α水平密切相关。
elements_zh.main_results: HBV单一感染和合并感染患者的肝酶和HBV DNA水平无统计学差异。然而,共同感染组的炎症细胞因子:白细胞介素-6 (IL-6) 和肿瘤坏死因子-α (TNF-α) 水平较高,同时干扰素-γ (IFN-γ) 水平明显较低。中介分析表明,PMN-MDSC 约占 IL-6 对 IFN-γ 抑制总效应的 45%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,中华线虫合并感染与通过 IL-6/TNF-α 连接的 PMN-MDSC 扩增和鸟氨酸与精氨酸比率升高而产生的免疫抑制有关,导致尽管肝酶水平正常,但 IFN-γ 的产生受到抑制。这一发现强调了共感染可能调节 HBV 患者 免疫应答 的新机制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于了解合并感染 HBV 患者的免疫调节,并可能指导未来基于免疫的治疗和针对合并感染情况的 监测 策略的研究。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是横断面的,限制了其建立因果关系的能力。证据基于相关性和中介分析,可能无法完全捕捉感染与 免疫应答 之间复杂的相互作用。信心是中等的。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景已知华支睾吸虫(C. sinensis)合并感染会加速乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)患者的疾病进展并诱导免疫耐受,特别是在两种感染流行的地区。代谢重编程已成为免疫抑制的关键驱动因素。这些代谢变化通常是由骨髓源性抑制细胞(MDSC)精心策划的,这些细胞在慢性感染期间会扩张以促进免疫耐受。中华丝虫合并感染会重新编程代谢以有利于 MDSC 相关的抑制,而这一过程与正常肝酶水平的关系仍不清楚。目的 探讨中华支原体合并感染是否会诱导肝酶水平正常的 HBV 患者发生 MDSC 相关的代谢重编程。方法 在这项横断面研究中,总共招募了 117 名参与者,并分为四组:健康对照(n = 30)、单一感染中华支原体的参与者(n = 29)、单一感染 HBV 的参与者(n = 28)和混合感染的参与者(n = 30)。使用化学发光免疫测定法测量血清细胞因子谱,使用液相色谱-串联质谱法测量氨基酸代谢物,并使用流式细胞术测量MDSC子集。进行 Spearman 相关性和中介分析来探讨炎症、代谢和免疫之间的关系。结果 HBV单一感染和合并感染患者的肝酶和HBV DNA水平无统计学差异。然而,与HBV单一感染组相比,合并感染组的炎症细胞因子白细胞介素6(IL-6)和肿瘤坏死因子-α(TNF-α)水平较高,同时干扰素-γ(IFN-γ)水平明显较低。流式细胞术检测显示,多形核MDSC(PMN-MDSC)在共感染组中表现出最大的扩增,并且其比例与IL-6和TNF-α水平密切相关。在代谢方面,共同感染组的鸟氨酸与精氨酸的比率显着较高。中介分析表明,PMN-MDSC 约占 IL-6 对 IFN-γ 抑制总效应的 45%。中华线虫合并感染通过 IL-6/TNF-α 连接的 PMN-MDSC 扩增和鸟氨酸与精氨酸比率升高与免疫抑制相关,导致尽管肝酶水平正常,但 IFN-γ 的产生受到抑制。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于了解合并感染 HBV 患者的免疫调节,并可能指导未来基于免疫的治疗和针对合并感染情况的 监测 策略的研究。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是横断面的,限制了其建立因果关系的能力。证据基于相关性和中介分析,可能无法完全捕捉感染与 免疫应答 之间复杂的相互作用。信心是中等的。

papers.title: Prevalence of hepatitis B and hepatitis C in the general population of Pakistan: a systematic review and meta-analysis of serological and active infection, 2010–2025
papers.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis will estimate the pooled prevalence of hepatitis B (HBsAg) and hepatitis C (anti-HCV and HCV RNA) in the general population of Pakistan from 2010 to 2025. HBsAg, anti-HCV and HCV RNA will be pooled separately. The review will examine how prevalence varies by province, time period (2010-2015, 2016-2020, 2021-2025), sex, age group, urban/rural setting, and diagnostic method. Only general-population studies will be included. Blood donors, haemodialysis, thalassaemia, pregnant-women-only, prisoner, injecting drug use and liver-disease-selected samples will be excluded. Databases: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, PakMediNet and Google Scholar. Two independent reviewers will screen, extract data and assess quality using the JBI Checklist for Prevalence Studies. Analysis will use a random-effects model in R. Reporting will follow PRISMA 2020.

papers.title: Seroprotection Status Against Hepatitis B among Children on Bawean Island, Indonesia
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major global public health concern, particularly in developing regions. Vaccination significantly reduces infection rates, but seroprotection may decline over time, necessitating periodic evaluation. This study evaluated the seroprotection rates against hepatitis B and the prevalence of HBV infection among children on Bawean Island, Indonesia. A cross-sectional study was conducted involving 90 children aged 3-15 years from various villages on Bawean Island. Blood samples were collected to determine hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) levels using an Electrochemiluminescence Immunoassay (ECLIA). Seroprotection was defined as anti-HBs titers ≥10 mIU/mL. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS Version 25, utilizing the chi-square test for categorical variables and the Spearman correlation test for continuous data. None of the subjects were reactive for HBsAg (0%). The overall anti-HBs seroprotection rate among the children was 67.8 %. There was a significant difference between seroprotection status and age (p<0.001). However, no significant difference was found between seroprotection status and sex (p=0.259) or basic immunization history (p=0.627). A significant negative correlation was found between age and Anti-HBs titers (r=-0.404, p<0.001). This study demonstrates the presence of seroprotection among children on Bawean Island. The significant age-dependent decline in anti-HBs titers highlights the potential need for a booster vaccination strategy in this remote island population to ensure long-term immunity.
papers.journal: INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF CLINICAL PATHOLOGY AND MEDICAL LABORATORY

papers.title: Chaos control and bifurcations of a discrete Hepatitis B virus model
papers.abstract: In this paper, we examine the local dynamics, bifurcation sets, basic reproduction number (BRN), chaos, convergence rate and bifurcation analysis at equilibrium states of a four-dimensional discrete HBV model. More specifically, we first give the mathematical formulation of a four-dimensional discrete HBV model, and then local behavior is explored by the linear stability theory. Moreover, at equilibrium states, we have identified the bifurcation sets, and then we have studied the bifurcations at equilibrium states of the discrete HBV model by the bifurcation theory. We have studied chaos and convergence rate for the understudied HBV model. Finally, our theoretical outcomes are confirmed numerically.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the associations between family history of hepatitis B virus, baseline hepatitis B surface antigen levels and surface antigen clearance in patients with chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in China, focusing on patients with chronic hepatitis B who received pegylated interferon-α treatment. The study included a sample of patients with documented family history of hepatitis B virus and baseline HBsAg levels.
analysis.methods: The study utilized a retrospective cohort design, analyzing medical records of patients with chronic hepatitis B. It assessed family history of hepatitis B virus, baseline HBsAg levels, and outcomes related to HBsAg clearance following pegylated interferon-α treatment.
analysis.main_results: The study found that family history of hepatitis B virus was significantly associated with a lower hazard of HBsAg clearance. Approximately 37% of this negative association was mediated by elevated baseline HBsAg levels.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as suggesting that patients with a family history of hepatitis B virus may have a reduced likelihood of achieving HBsAg clearance with pegylated interferon-α, potentially requiring lower baseline HBsAg levels to achieve similar outcomes as those without family history.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of personalized treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B patients based on their family history and baseline HBsAg levels, potentially improving therapeutic outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on medical records, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the associations between family history of hepatitis B virus, baseline hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels, and HBsAg clearance in patients with chronic hepatitis B. A retrospective cohort study was conducted in China, analyzing medical records of patients who received pegylated interferon-α treatment. The results showed that family history of hepatitis B virus was significantly linked to a lower hazard of HBsAg clearance, with approximately 37% of this association mediated by elevated baseline HBsAg levels. The authors interpreted these findings as indicating that HBFH-positive patients may require lower baseline HBsAg levels to achieve comparable clearance rates to HBFH-negative patients. The study's findings may inform personalized treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B patients, considering their family history and baseline HBsAg levels. However, the study's retrospective design and reliance on medical records limit the confidence in its results, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨 乙型肝炎病毒 家族史、基线乙型肝炎表面抗原水平和 慢性乙型肝炎 患者表面抗原清除率之间的关联。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在中国进行了一项回顾性 队列研究 研究,重点关注接受聚乙二醇化干扰素-α 治疗 的 慢性乙型肝炎 患者。该研究纳入了有 乙型肝炎病毒 家族史和基线 HBsAg 水平记录的患者样本。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用回顾性 队列研究 设计,分析 队列研究 患者的医疗记录。它评估了 乙型肝炎病毒 家族史、基线 HBsAg 水平以及聚乙二醇化干扰素-α 治疗 后与 HBsAg 清除相关的结果。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,乙型肝炎病毒 家族史与 HBsAg 清除风险较低显着相关。大约 37% 的这种负相关是由基线 HBsAg 水平升高介导的。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为,有 乙型肝炎病毒 家族史的患者使用聚乙二醇化干扰素-α 实现 HBsAg 清除的可能性可能降低,可能需要较低的基线 HBsAg 水平才能达到与无家族史患者相似的结果。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于根据 慢性乙型肝炎 患者的家族史和基线 HBsAg 水平制定个性化 治疗 策略,从而有可能改善治疗结果。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对医疗记录的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨 乙型肝炎病毒 家族史、基线乙型肝炎表面抗原水平和 慢性乙型肝炎 患者表面抗原清除率之间的关联。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在中国进行了一项回顾性 队列研究 研究,重点关注接受聚乙二醇化干扰素-α 治疗 的 慢性乙型肝炎 患者。该研究纳入了有 乙型肝炎病毒 家族史和基线 HBsAg 水平记录的患者样本。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究采用回顾性 队列研究 设计,分析 队列研究 患者的医疗记录。它评估了 乙型肝炎病毒 家族史、基线 HBsAg 水平以及聚乙二醇化干扰素-α 治疗 后与 HBsAg 清除相关的结果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究发现,乙型肝炎病毒 家族史与 HBsAg 清除风险较低显着相关。大约 37% 的这种负相关是由基线 HBsAg 水平升高介导的。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为,有 乙型肝炎病毒 家族史的患者使用聚乙二醇化干扰素-α 实现 HBsAg 清除的可能性可能降低,可能需要较低的基线 HBsAg 水平才能达到与无家族史患者相似的结果。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于根据 慢性乙型肝炎 患者的家族史和基线 HBsAg 水平制定个性化 治疗 策略,从而有可能改善治疗结果。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对医疗记录的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

papers.full_text: Abstract Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a blood-borne virus that is nationally notifiable in Australia. Despite inclusion of the HBV vaccine in the childhood National Immunisation Program, local and overseas-acquired cases occur. An increase in newly acquired HBV cases in metropolitan Perth between 1 August 2023 and 31 July 2024 prompted an outbreak investigation. Epidemiological analyses of demographics, disease onset, and risk factors were combined with laboratory investigations, including whole genome sequencing (WGS) for genotyping and phylogenetic analysis.Twenty newly acquired cases were included, with three additional cases investigated. Most cases were aged over 30 years (n = 18, 78%) and reported casual unprotected sex (n = 17, 74%); some were born overseas (n = 8, 33%) or used intravenous drugs (n = 7, 30%). Four had received at least three HBV vaccines, although timing of doses varied. Of the 20 sequenced cases, 12 were locally acquired sub-genotype A2 HBV. Three sub-genotype A2 clusters and one sub-genotype B3 cluster were identified.This study is one of the first in Australia to investigate a potential HBV outbreak using WGS. Although genetic diversity within individual patient samples (within-host sequence heterogeneity) complicated relatedness analyses and limited the assessment of transmission pathways, WGS complemented epidemiological methods, which had demonstrated few links. The increase in sub-genotype A2 cases was likely due to coincident introductions of multiple HBV strains into Perth with some limited local transmission. Acknowledgements The Master of Applied Epidemiology scholarship for RS is funded by the Boorloo Public Health Unit, Western Australia. No other funding was provided for this investigation.The authors wish to thank staff at the Boorloo Public Health Unit who undertake the public health follow up of hepatitis B in metropolitan Perth, and the Pathogen and Surveillance Unit and Molecular Diagnostics Section, PathWest for their assistance in the development of the whole genome sequencing assay. Funding The Master of Applied Epidemiology scholarship for RS is funded by the Boorloo Public Health Unit, Western Australia. No other funding was provided for this investigation. Data were collected under statutory public health powers for the purpose of communicable disease control in accordance with the Western Australian Public Health Act 2016 and Public Health Regulations 2017. Ethics approval for the use of these data for research purposes was granted by the Australian National University Human Research Ethics Committee (Reference: 2017/090). analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate a rise in newly acquired hepatitis B cases in metropolitan Perth to understand the potential outbreak and transmission dynamics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An outbreak investigation was conducted in metropolitan Perth between 1 August 2023 and 31 July 2024, including 20 newly acquired cases and three additional cases for further analysis.
analysis.methods: Epidemiological analyses of demographics, disease onset, and risk factors were combined with laboratory investigations, including whole genome sequencing (WGS) for genotyping and phylogenetic analysis.
analysis.main_results: Most cases were aged over 30 years (n = 18, 78%) and reported casual unprotected sex (n = 17, 74%); some were born overseas (n = 8, 33%) or used intravenous drugs (n = 7, 30%). Of the 20 sequenced cases, 12 were locally acquired sub-genotype A2 HBV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified three sub-genotype A2 clusters and one sub-genotype B3 cluster, highlighting the role of WGS in complementing traditional epidemiological methods to better understand transmission patterns.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the increase in sub-genotype A2 cases may be due to multiple introductions of HBV strains into Perth, with limited local transmission, informing targeted public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Genetic diversity within individual patient samples complicated relatedness analyses, and the study's results were limited by the small sample size and the lack of clear epidemiological links.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated a rise in newly acquired hepatitis B cases in metropolitan Perth between 1 August 2023 and 31 July 2024. The outbreak was analyzed using epidemiological data and whole genome sequencing (WGS) to determine transmission dynamics. Most cases were over 30 years old and reported casual unprotected sex, with some born overseas or using intravenous drugs. Of the 20 sequenced cases, 12 were sub-genotype A2 HBV, and three clusters of this genotype were identified, along with one sub-genotype B3 cluster. The study suggests that the increase in cases may result from multiple introductions of HBV strains into Perth, with limited local transmission. While WGS provided insights, within-host sequence heterogeneity complicated relatedness analyses. The findings have implications for public health surveillance and intervention strategies in the region.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究确定了三个亚基因型 A2 簇和一个亚基因型 B3 簇,强调了 WGS 在补充传统流行病学方法以更好地了解 传播 模式方面的作用。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate a rise in newly acquired hepatitis B cases in metropolitan Perth to understand the potential outbreak and transmission dynamics.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: An outbreak investigation was conducted in metropolitan Perth between 1 August 2023 and 31 July 2024, including 20 newly acquired cases and three additional cases for further analysis.
analysis_en.methods: Epidemiological analyses of demographics, disease onset, and risk factors were combined with laboratory investigations, including whole genome sequencing (WGS) for genotyping and phylogenetic analysis.
analysis_en.main_results: Most cases were aged over 30 years (n = 18, 78%) and reported casual unprotected sex (n = 17, 74%); some were born overseas (n = 8, 33%) or used intravenous drugs (n = 7, 30%). Of the 20 sequenced cases, 12 were locally acquired sub-genotype A2 HBV.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified three sub-genotype A2 clusters and one sub-genotype B3 cluster, highlighting the role of WGS in complementing traditional epidemiological methods to better understand transmission patterns.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the increase in sub-genotype A2 cases may be due to multiple introductions of HBV strains into Perth, with limited local transmission, informing targeted public health interventions.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Genetic diversity within individual patient samples complicated relatedness analyses, and the study's results were limited by the small sample size and the lack of clear epidemiological links.

papers.title_zh: 对大都市中新感染乙型肝炎增加的调查:来自整个 基因组 测序的见解
papers.source_body_en: Three sub-genotype A2 clusters and one sub-genotype B3 cluster were identified.This study is one of the first in Australia to investigate a potential HBV outbreak using WGS. Although genetic diversity within individual patient samples (within-host sequence heterogeneity) complicated relatedness analyses and limited the assessment of transmission pathways, WGS complemented epidemiological methods, which had demonstrated few links. Abstract Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a blood-borne virus that is nationally notifiable in Australia. Despite inclusion of the HBV vaccine in the childhood National Immunisation Program, local and overseas-acquired cases occur. An increase in newly acquired HBV cases in metropolitan Perth between 1 August 2023 and 31 July 2024 prompted an outbreak investigation. Epidemiological analyses of demographics, disease onset, and risk factors were combined with laboratory investigations, including whole genome sequencing (WGS) for genotyping and phylogenetic analysis.Twenty newly acquired cases were included, with three additional cases investigated. Most cases were aged over 30 years (n = 18, 78%) and reported casual unprotected sex (n = 17, 74%); some were born overseas (n = 8, 33%) or used intravenous drugs (n = 7, 30%). Four had received at least three HBV vaccines, although timing of doses varied. Of the 20 sequenced cases, 12 were locally acquired sub-genotype A2 HBV. The increase in sub-genotype A2 cases was likely due to coincident introductions of multiple HBV strains into Perth with some limited local transmission. papers.title: Gambaran Hasil Pemeriksaan Blood Borne Virus (HIV, HBV, HCV) dan Profil Leukosit pada Pasien Gagal Ginjal yang Menjalani Hemodialisis
papers.abstract: Salah satu masalah kesehatan yang masih terus meningkat prevalensinya di seluruh dunia adalah penyakit ginjal kronis (PGK). Pasien PGK yang menjalani hemodialisis memiliki risiko terpapar Blood Borne Virus (BBV) karena adanya prosedur yang melibatkan paparan darah secara berulang. Selain itu, kondisi uremia pada PGK dapat berkaitan dengan proses inflamasi kronis yang tercermin melalui perubahan profil leukosit. Studi ini berguna untuk mengkarakterisasi profil leukosit dan hasil tes BBV pada pasien PGK yang menjalani hemodialisis di Rumah Sakit PKU Muhammadiyah di Yogyakarta. Sesuai dengan data dari tahun 2025 rekam medis, studi ini mengenakan metode deskriptif dengan pendekatan retrospektif. Sampel penelitian terdiri atas 33 pasien yang diperoleh melalui teknik purposive sampling. Pemeriksaan BBV mencakup HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus), HBV (Hepatitis B Virus), dan HCV (Hepatitis C Virus) menggunakan rapid test, sementara pemeriksaan profil leukosit dilakukan dengan hematology analyzer 5-diff. Analisis data dilakukan secara deskriptif. Sebagian besar responden berjenis kelamin laki-laki (54,5%) dan berada pada kelompok usia 18–59 tahun (63,6%). Hasil pemeriksaan menunjukkan seluruh responden nonreaktif terhadap HIV dan negatif HBV, sedangkan HCV positif ditemukan pada 2 responden (6,1%). Rerata jumlah leukosit mencapai 10,13 × 103/μL, dengan rerata neutrofil 75,97% dan limfosit 14,73%. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, HCV masih ditemukan pada sebagian kecil pasien hemodialisis, sementara HIV dan HBV tidak ditemukan. Profil leukosit memperlihatkan kecenderungan peningkatan neutrofil disertai penurunan limfosit yang dapat menggambarkan adanya respons inflamasi pada pasien PGK yang menjalani hemodialisis.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize the leukocyte profile and Blood Borne Virus (BBV) test results in hemodialysis patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Among 33 patients, 2 were positive for HCV, while all were negative for HIV and HBV. The leukocyte profile showed an increase in neutrophils and a decrease in lymphocytes, indicating an inflammatory response in CKD patients undergoing hemodialysis.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 萨拉赫·萨图·玛萨拉·克塞哈坦·杨·玛西·特鲁斯·曼宁卡特·普雷瓦伦西尼亚·杜尼亚·阿达拉·潘亚基特·金贾尔·克罗尼斯(PGK)。Pasien PGK 是血液透析的危险因素,血源性病毒 (BBV) 会导致血液透析。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究方法是在 33 小时内进行有目的抽样。
elements_zh.methods: Pemeriksaan BBV mencakup HIV(人类免疫缺陷病毒)、HBV(乙型肝炎病毒)、HCV(丙型肝炎病毒)menggunakan快速检测、sementara pemeriksaan profil leukosit dilakukan dengan血液分析仪5-diff。分析数据 dilakukan secara deskriptif。
elements_zh.main_results: Hasil pemeriksaan menunjukkan seluruh 响应非反应性 HIV 和阴性 HBV,sedangkan HCV 阳性 ditemukan pada 2 响应 (6,1%)。Rerata jumlah leukosit mencapai 10,13 × 103/μL,dengan rerata neutrofil 75,97% 和 limfosit 14,73%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 根据上述结果,HCV仍存在于部分接受透析的PGK患者中,而HIV和HBV未被检测到。白细胞谱显示中性粒细胞增加和淋巴细胞减少的趋势,这可能反映了接受透析的PGK患者存在炎症反应。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究的结果可以提供关于接受透析的PGK患者中BBV,特别是HCV的患病率信息。这有助于提高对该人群BBV感染的监测和预防水平。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在我的记忆中进行研究,以验证数据的正确性和正确性。请注意,乙肝病毒感染的方法。

papers.title_original: Advances in the immunological basis and therapeutic strategies for functional cure of chronic hepatitis B

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the immunological mechanisms underlying chronic hepatitis B and identify therapeutic strategies for achieving a functional cure. The background highlights that persistent viral reservoirs and sustained antigen-driven immune dysfunction are major constraints in the functional cure of chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This review article provides an overview of the immunological basis and therapeutic strategies for the functional cure of chronic hepatitis B. It outlines the mechanisms of immune dysfunction and their implications for treatment approaches, with no specific study population or design described.
analysis.methods: The review synthesizes human clinical evidence and discusses the potential of biomarker-guided stratification and rational sequencing of therapies to balance efficacy against immune-mediated liver injury.
analysis.main_results: The review identifies key mechanisms such as hepatitis B virus-specific T-cell exhaustion, B-cell dysfunction, hepatic immune tolerance, innate immune dysregulation, and metabolic and gut-liver axis remodeling as constraints to achieving a functional cure. It also outlines emerging therapeutic strategies including pegylated interferon, therapeutic vaccination, immune checkpoint modulation, and innate immune activation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that understanding these mechanisms can inform the development of a staged strategy for durable HBsAg loss. The novelty lies in linking these immunological mechanisms to therapeutic approaches for functional cure.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the design of future studies and therapeutic strategies aimed at achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B by addressing immune dysfunction and viral reservoirs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a review and does not present original clinical data, which limits the strength of the evidence. The confidence in the findings is moderate as they are based on existing literature rather than new experimental results.

analysis.summary_en: This review article explores the immunological mechanisms that hinder the functional cure of chronic hepatitis B, emphasizing persistent viral reservoirs and sustained antigen-driven immune dysfunction. It outlines key mechanisms such as T-cell exhaustion, B-cell dysfunction, hepatic immune tolerance, innate immune dysregulation, and metabolic and gut-liver axis remodeling. The authors propose emerging therapeutic strategies, including pegylated interferon, therapeutic vaccination, immune checkpoint modulation, and innate immune activation, to address these challenges. The review highlights the importance of biomarker-guided stratification and rational treatment sequencing to balance efficacy with the risk of immune-mediated liver injury. While the study provides valuable insights into the immunological basis of chronic hepatitis B, its findings are based on existing literature, limiting the strength of the evidence. The review serves as a foundation for future research and therapeutic development in the field of hepatitis B.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探索 慢性乙型肝炎 背后的免疫学机制,并确定实现 功能性治愈 的治疗策略。背景强调,持续的病毒储存宿主和持续的抗原驱动的免疫功能障碍是慢性乙型肝炎的功能性治愈的主要限制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本综述文章概述了 慢性乙型肝炎 的免疫学基础和治疗策略。它概述了免疫功能障碍的机制及其对 治疗 方法的影响,但没有描述具体的研究人群或设计。
elements_zh.methods: 该综述综合了人类临床证据,并讨论了生物标志物引导的分层和合理的治疗排序以平衡免疫介导的肝损伤疗效的潜力。
elements_zh.main_results: 该综述确定了 乙型肝炎病毒 特异性 T 细胞耗竭、B 细胞功能障碍、肝脏免疫耐受、先天免疫失调以及代谢和肠肝轴重塑等关键机制作为实现 功能性治愈 的限制。它还概述了新兴的治疗策略,包括聚乙二醇干扰素、治疗性 疫苗接种、免疫检查点调节和先天免疫激活。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,了解这些机制可以为制定持久 HBsAg 消失的分阶段策略提供信息。新颖之处在于将这些免疫机制与 功能性治愈 的治疗方法联系起来。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为未来研究和治疗策略的设计提供信息,旨在通过解决免疫功能障碍和病毒 储存宿主 来实现 慢性乙型肝炎 的 功能性治愈。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the immunological mechanisms underlying chronic hepatitis B and identify therapeutic strategies for achieving a functional cure. The background highlights that persistent viral reservoirs and sustained antigen-driven immune dysfunction are major constraints in the functional cure of chronic hepatitis B.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This review article provides an overview of the immunological basis and therapeutic strategies for the functional cure of chronic hepatitis B. It outlines the mechanisms of immune dysfunction and their implications for treatment approaches, with no specific study population or design described.
analysis_en.methods: The review synthesizes human clinical evidence and discusses the potential of biomarker-guided stratification and rational sequencing of therapies to balance efficacy against immune-mediated liver injury.
analysis_en.main_results: The review identifies key mechanisms such as hepatitis B virus-specific T-cell exhaustion, B-cell dysfunction, hepatic immune tolerance, innate immune dysregulation, and metabolic and gut-liver axis remodeling as constraints to achieving a functional cure. It also outlines emerging therapeutic strategies including pegylated interferon, therapeutic vaccination, immune checkpoint modulation, and innate immune activation.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that understanding these mechanisms can inform the development of a staged strategy for durable HBsAg loss. The novelty lies in linking these immunological mechanisms to therapeutic approaches for functional cure.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the design of future studies and therapeutic strategies aimed at achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B by addressing immune dysfunction and viral reservoirs.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a review and does not present original clinical data, which limits the strength of the evidence. The confidence in the findings is moderate as they are based on existing literature rather than new experimental results.

papers.title: Hepatitis B Reactivation and Infection in People with HIV on Tenofovir-Sparing Antiretroviral Therapy
papers.abstract: As more people with HIV (PWH) transition to tenofovir (TXF)-sparing antiretroviral therapy (ART), the risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation (HBVr) and new infection (HBVi) is a concern. We conducted a retrospective study of 5,776 PWH in the Centers for AIDS Research Network of Integrated Clinical Systems cohort without active HBV infection with ≥1 TXF-sparing ART regimen prescribed after 5/1/2014 and examined episodes of HBVi/r defined as new HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity or HBV viremia. We calculated rate of HBVi/r over total time on TXF-sparing ART per 10,000 person-years. We identified 17 cases of HBVi/r over a median 5.3 years of follow up. The rate of HBVi was 3.9 per 10,000 person-years, and rate of HBVr was 6.0 per 10,000 person-years, with possible higher risk for those who were HBV surface antibody (HBsAb) negative at cohort entry and among those not on ART with no anti-HBV activity. Liver injury, defined as alanine aminotransferase lab value ≥ 100 U/L, occurred within 3 months in only one HBVi case. HBVi/r on TXF-sparing ART was rare in this U.S. HBVi/r occurred in some with prior HBsAb positivity, but significant hepatic flares were not observed. When starting TXF-sparing ART, providers should check complete HBV serologies, offer initial or additional vaccination as needed, and monitor for potential HBVi/r.

The research highlights the importance of monitoring HBV status and ensuring vaccination when starting such therapies. papers.title: Characteristics of needlestick injuries and post-exposure practices among healthcare workers in private hospitals in Alexandria, Egypt
papers.abstract: Abstract Needlestick injuries (NSIs) are a major occupational hazard among healthcare workers (HCWs), with potential exposure to blood-borne pathogens and associated health consequences. A retrospective record-based study was conducted using 318 records of HCWs who experienced NSIs during 2023–2024 in four private hospitals in Alexandria, Egypt, all with standardized NSI reporting systems. Data included demographic and occupational characteristics, injury circumstances, safety practices, hepatitis B vaccination status, infection prevention and control (IPC) training, and post-exposure management. Most NSIs occurred among female HCWs (61.6%), and nurses represented the largest affected occupational group (63.5%). Syringes were involved in 65.1% of NSIs, while sudden patient movement was the most frequently reported contributing factor (26.1%). Among records with documented IPC training status, 79.8% indicated no prior training, while training status was missing in 36.2% of records. Overall, 16.0% of HCWs were documented as unvaccinated against hepatitis B. Post-exposure actions were not documented in 30.8% of records, and only 29.6% of HCWs underwent documented post-exposure testing for hepatitis C virus, hepatitis B, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). These findings highlight gaps in IPC training, hepatitis B vaccination, and post-exposure management and underscore the need for standardized reporting, timely post-exposure care, and improved occupational safety practices.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 针刺伤 (NSI) 是医护人员 (HCW) 的主要职业危害,可能会接触血源性病原体并产生相关的健康后果。使用 2023 年至 2024 年期间在埃及亚历山大的四家私立医院经历过 NSI 的 318 名医护人员的记录进行了一项基于记录的回顾性研究,所有医院均采用标准化的 NSI 报告系统。数据包括人口和职业特征、受伤情况、安全实践、乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 状态、感染预防和控制 (IPC) 培训以及暴露后管理。大多数 NSI 发生在女性医护人员 (61.6%) 中,护士是受影响最大的职业群体 (63.5%)。65.1% 的 NSI 涉及注射器,而患者突然移动是最常报告的促成因素 (26.1%)。在记录有 IPC 培训状态的记录中,79.8% 表示之前没有接受过培训,而 36.2% 的记录中缺少培训状态。总体而言,16.0% 的医护人员未接种乙型肝炎疫苗。30.8% 的记录中未记录暴露后行为,只有 29.6% 的医护人员接受了有记录的丙型肝炎病毒、乙型肝炎和人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV) 暴露后检测。这些发现凸显了 IPC 培训、乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 和暴露后管理方面的差距,并强调了标准化报告、及时的暴露后护理和改进职业安全实践的必要性。

Meeting Coverage > AASLD Another Drug Shows Potential for Functional Cures in Chronic Hepatitis B — With highest dose of siRNA therapy, 19% achieved a functional cure 24 weeks after treatment ended by Terrence Rudd, Staff Writer, MedPage Today November 10, 2026 • 3 min read Add MedPage Today on Google MedpageToday Reductions in hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were observed with a novel small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapy in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, according to a phase II study. Among patients randomized to monotherapy with one of four doses of the siRNA HRS-5635, all 32 on the highest dose (400 mg) had HBsAg levels less than 100 IU/mL after 48 weeks of treatment, with 88% still at that level 24 weeks after treatment ended. Among this high-dose group, 16% achieved a functional cure, with an HBsAg clearance level of less than 0.05 IU/mL after 48 weeks -- a percentage that rose to 19% by 24 weeks post-treatment, reported Xieer Liang, PhD, of Southern Medical University in Guangzhou, China, at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseasesopens in a new tab or window annual meeting in Denver. "A dose-dependent antiviral response was observed with HRS-5635," Liang said. "All HRS-5635 regimens were generally safe and well-tolerated." An estimated 240 million people worldwide have chronic HBV infection, including about 640,000 U.S. adultsopens in a new tab or window. Chronic HBV can cause liver damage, cirrhosis, liver cancer, and death. Five antivirals and two immune modulators are approved in the U.S. opens in a new tab or windowto treat chronic HBV, with treatment regimens lasting from 6 months to over 1 year. In a previous phase II trialopens in a new tab or window, siRNA therapy with an immunomodulator reduced HBsAg in patients with chronic HBV infection. Last month, the FDA approved another nucleic acid-based therapeutic, the antisense oligonucleotide drug bepirovirsen (Hibsago)opens in a new tab or window, for patients with chronic HBV taking antiviral therapy based on results from the B-Well 1 and B-Well 2opens in a new tab or window studies. In those trials, 19% to 20% of patients with HBsAg levels between 100 and 3,000 IU/mL had a functional cure with bepirovirsen at week 72. The current trial included patients with chronic HBV on stable nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy who had HBsAg levels over 100 and less than 3,000 IU/mL and HBV DNA levels less than 20 IU/mL. Patients could be hepatitis B envelope antigen (HBeAg) positive or negative, but they couldn't have cirrhosis. All patients received tenofovir amibufenamide during 48 weeks of HRS-5635 treatment. Mean age ranged from 41.5 to 44.6 years in the four treatment groups, 59.4% to 76.7% were men, and mean HBsAg ranged from 1,058.2 IU/mL to 1,200.4 IU/mL. Most patients were HBeAg negative (65.6% to 73.3%). The investigators defined functional cure as sustained HBV DNA suppression and HBsAg clearance of less than 0.05 IU/mL, with or without seroconversion, sustained for 24 weeks after treatment. Among patients in the 400-mg group, 45% converted from HBeAg positive to HBeAg negative after 48 weeks of treatment, a percentage that slid to 27% at 24 weeks after treatment. In patients receiving the 400-mg dose who were HBeAg negative and had HBsAg below 1,000 IU/mL at baseline, 33% reached the functional cure rate of HBsAg less than 0.05 IU/mL. Across the four groups, 46.9% to 60% had a treatment-related adverse event. There were only two such events that were grade 3 or higher, and no serious adverse events related to treatment and no deaths occurred. Upper respiratory tract infections were the most common adverse event, occurring in 25% to 33.3% of patients in the four groups. Alanine transaminase elevations occurred in up to 6.7% of patients during and after treatment, Liang said, but levels were generally stable during treatment, and no elevations reached a grade 3 level. The follow-up period of 24 weeks after treatment ended was relatively short, Liang cautioned, but a longer-duration extension study is ongoing, along with a phase III trialopens in a new tab or window. analysis.time: The study results were reported at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases annual meeting in Denver on November 10, 2026. The treatment period lasted 48 weeks, with follow-up at 24 weeks post-treatment.
analysis.location_and_population: The trial was conducted in China, involving patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection who were on stable nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy. Participants had HBsAg levels over 100 and less than 3,000 IU/mL and HBV DNA levels less than 20 IU/mL. Most were HBeAg negative (65.6% to 73.3%) and did not have cirrhosis.
analysis.event: A phase II study evaluated the siRNA therapy HRS-5635 for treating chronic HBV infection. The highest dose (400 mg) showed a functional cure in 19% of patients 24 weeks after treatment ended, with HBsAg levels below 0.05 IU/mL. The study was presented at the AASLD annual meeting.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Among the 32 patients on the highest dose, 19% achieved a functional cure 24 weeks post-treatment. The study found a dose-dependent antiviral response, with all four HRS-5635 doses reducing HBsAg levels. The therapy was generally safe and well-tolerated, with only two treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or higher and no serious adverse events or deaths.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study results were reported at the AASLD annual meeting, and the therapy was described as generally safe and well-tolerated. The functional cure was defined as sustained HBV DNA suppression and HBsAg clearance for 24 weeks post-treatment. The findings are based on a phase II trial and are not yet confirmed for broader application.

news.content_title: Hepatitis B Cure Closer After Gene Editing Eliminates Viral Reservoir in Every Target-Dose Patient
news.content: A nurse loads a syringe with a vaccine against hepatitis at a free immunization clinic for students before the start of the school year, in Lynwood, California August, 27, 2013. Nurses are immunizing children in preparation for the first day of public school on September 3. The clinic offers the mandatory vaccinations for school children against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, hepatitis B, MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) and chickenpox as well as some optional ones. AFP PHOTO / Robyn Beck ROBYN BECK/AFP via Getty Images For the roughly 254 million people living with chronic hepatitis B worldwide, every approved therapy amounts to a managed retreat. Antiviral drugs suppress the virus but rarely vanquish it, and patients typically face a lifetime of daily pills. The reason no treatment has achieved a true cure in more than four decades of trying comes down to a single molecular adversary: covalently closed circular DNA , or cccDNA — a tightly wound viral genome that hides inside the nuclei of infected liver cells and continues churning out new virus particles even as antivirals hold the outer infection in check. Today, at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) The Liver Meeting® 2026 in Denver, Colorado, Durham-based biotechnology company Precision BioSciences presented the most complete human evidence yet that gene editing can eliminate that reservoir — and do it durably. The stakes extend beyond "cure" in the conventional sense. Even patients who achieve what hepatologists call a functional cure — the loss of detectable hepatitis B surface antigen — still carry residual cccDNA in liver tissue. That dormant reservoir can reactivate when immunity wanes, posing an underappreciated danger for the hundreds of thousands of chronic HBV patients who each year require chemotherapy, organ transplantation, or biological therapies. A therapy that eliminates cccDNA would address the root cause of that reactivation risk, not merely its clinical readout. A Late-Breaking Moment in Denver The late-breaking oral presentation, delivered at 2:15 p.m. MST by lead investigator Dr. Man-Fung Yuen — Chair Professor at The University of Hong Kong and Chief of the Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology at Queen Mary Hospital — covers updated Phase 1 data from the ELIMINATE-B study ( NCT06680232 on ClinicalTrials.gov ) of PBGENE-HBV , Precision's wholly owned in vivo gene editing program. The dataset is the most expansive yet reported for any in vivo gene editing approach targeting hepatitis B: 25 patients, 59 total drug administrations, four dose levels, and a data cutoff of September 28, 2026 . The headline result: among 12 patients with detectable pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) at the start of the trial, 11 (92%) reached undetectable pgRNA following treatment — including all six evaluable patients dosed at the 0.4 mg/kg level that Precision has selected to advance into a global Phase 2 study. Why pgRNA — and Why It Matters pgRNA, or pregenomic RNA, is a transcript produced exclusively from cccDNA. That exclusivity makes it unusually informative as a biomarker: when pgRNA disappears from a patient's blood, the most straightforward explanation is that the cccDNA driving its production has been eliminated or permanently silenced in the liver. It is, in essence, a molecular readout of the gene edit working as designed. The clinical significance of that readout was quantified in a landmark study: Terrault et al. found that patients with undetectable pgRNA at the time of nucleoside/nucleotide analog (NUC) therapy discontinuation have an approximately 10-fold increased probability of achieving a viral cure — sustained undetectable HBV DNA off all therapy — compared with those with detectable pgRNA. Undetectable pgRNA is therefore not merely a mechanistic marker; it is the strongest available predictor that a treatment has opened the door to genuine, off-treatment cure. That distinction separates PBGENE-HBV from other hepatitis B candidates in development. Antisense oligonucleotides, RNA interference agents, and capsid assembly modulators can knock down circulating viral proteins, but they leave cccDNA largely untouched. The moment therapy stops, cccDNA resumes templating new virus. By aiming a molecular scissors directly at the DNA source, Precision is attempting something categorically different: permanent deletion. The Technology: ARCUS Gene Editing PBGENE-HBV is built on Precision's proprietary ARCUS® genome editing platform , which derives from a class of naturally occurring enzymes called homing endonucleases. The specific precursor is I-CreI, a protein found in the green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii that belongs to the LAGLIDADG enzyme family — one of the oldest and most studied groups of sequence-specific DNA cutters in nature. Precision's protein engineers substantially redesigned I-CreI to redirect its specificity from the alga's own genome toward a conserved sequence in the HBV polymerase gene, converting the natural homodimer into a single-chain monomeric protein that recognizes roughly 22 base pairs of target sequence. That architecture distinguishes ARCUS from CRISPR-Cas9 in several practically important ways. CRISPR requires two components — the Cas9 protein and a separate guide RNA strand — to be packaged and delivered together. ARCUS is a single protein: its DNA recognition is encoded in the protein's own binding interface rather than in a separate nucleic acid. The result is a smaller mRNA payload, no guide RNA to trigger innate immune RNA sensors, and a longer recognition sequence (22 bp vs. the ~20 bp of a CRISPR spacer plus PAM) that statistically reduces the probability of off-target cutting events. In PBGENE-HBV, an mRNA blueprint for the ARCUS nuclease is encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) formulated by Acuitas Therapeutics — the same Vancouver-based LNP specialist whose platform was used in the Pfizer/BioNTech COVID-19 mRNA vaccine — and infused intravenously into the patient. The LNPs home preferentially to hepatocytes via the ApoE-LDL receptor pathway, where the mRNA is translated into the nuclease protein. The protein finds and cuts the HBV cccDNA at its target sequence, triggering the cell's own repair machinery to introduce small insertions or deletions — indels — that disrupt the viral polymerase gene and permanently inactivate replication from that copy of cccDNA. Crucially, unlike AAV-based gene therapies — which cannot be re-administered because patients generate immune responses against the viral capsid — PBGENE-HBV can be infused multiple times. Patients in ELIMINATE-B received multiple infusions across the dosing period, and the cumulative editing effect appears to build as a larger fraction of hepatocytes is progressively reached and edited. The Clinical Data in Detail pgRNA Loss: Durable and Complete at the Go-Forward Dose Among the 12 evaluable patients with detectable pgRNA at baseline, 11 reached undetectable levels. The one exception — dosed at the higher 0.65 mg/kg level but with only two administrations — still showed a 95% reduction in pgRNA at the data cut and continues on follow-up. At 0.4 mg/kg, the response was total. All six evaluable patients at that dose reached undetectable pgRNA, and among the subset with at least six months of follow-up, every single one has maintained undetectable pgRNA through the September 28, 2026 cutoff. The longest-running observation now approaches one year of sustained pgRNA loss , extending data first presented at the European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) Congress in Barcelona in May 2026. A Hard-to-Treat Patient: The HBeAg-Positive Signal One particularly notable data point involves the first HBeAg-positive patient enrolled in ELIMINATE-B. HBeAg positivity is a marker of active, high-level viral replication and is generally considered the more difficult phenotype to treat: HBeAg-positive patients carry logarithmically higher amounts of cccDNA and viral load in liver tissue. At the 0.4 mg/kg dose, that patient's pgRNA dropped from 5,750 copies/mL at baseline to undetectable after just the second administration of PBGENE-HBV, and remained undetectable through the data cutoff. That the editing machinery could penetrate and clear cccDNA even under those conditions is likely to attract close attention from hepatologists accustomed to treating this population with less certainty of outcome. Liver Biopsies: Proving the Mechanism pgRNA is a blood-based surrogate. The more direct measurement is what happens in the liver itself, and Precision presented paired biopsy data — tissue samples taken before and after treatment — from two patients dosed at 0.4 mg/kg. The results showed approximately 10-fold (1-log) and 35-fold (1.5-log) reductions in cccDNA , respectively. These findings reproduce and extend the first-ever biopsy evidence of cccDNA elimination in treated patients, which Precision disclosed at EASL 2026. The convergence between vanishing cccDNA in liver tissue and vanishing pgRNA in blood provides what researchers characterize as mechanistic confirmation that the therapy is doing precisely what it was designed to do. It is worth stating the biological caveat precisely: a reduction in cccDNA is not identical to its complete elimination. What the biopsy data demonstrate is a measurable, large-magnitude reduction in cccDNA copies per cell — reductions that, when combined with sustained pgRNA undetectability, provide the strongest available human evidence that ARCUS editing is progressively clearing the reservoir. Whether residual cccDNA below current detection thresholds persists is a question Phase 2 will need to address. HBsAg: Broad Antiviral Activity Across the Board Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) — a secondary viral marker produced from both cccDNA and from integrated HBV DNA embedded elsewhere in the genome — declined in all 24 evaluable patients across every dose level tested. At 0.4 mg/kg, maximal HBsAg reductions approached 94%. While HBsAg reductions alone are not sufficient to demonstrate cccDNA clearance (because integrated HBV DNA also contributes to surface antigen), the consistency of the effect across the entire evaluable population reinforces that PBGENE-HBV is producing broad antiviral activity in a diverse patient group. Safety: No Dose-Limiting Toxicities Across all 59 infusions in 25 patients, Precision reports no dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs). The most common adverse events were infusion-related reactions characteristic of lipid nanoparticle delivery — typically beginning and resolving within 24 hours of infusion. The 0.4 mg/kg dose was better tolerated than the higher 0.65 mg/kg dose, an observation that reinforces the Phase 2 dose selection. At 0.4 mg/kg, no serious adverse events (SAEs) have been recorded, and no Grade 3 or higher hypotension events have occurred across 15 administrations in eight patients. Transient, reversible elevations in liver enzymes (ALT and AST) were observed following some infusions, consistent with known LNP biology. One delayed elevation occurred after a third administration — peak ALT of 306 U/L, AST of 278 U/L — but resolved without intervention and without associated changes in bilirubin or any sign of synthetic liver dysfunction. No cases meeting Hy's Law criteria — a pharmacovigilance threshold for serious drug-induced liver injury — were observed at any dose level. Executive and Investigator Perspectives Michael Amoroso , President and CEO of Precision BioSciences, framed the data as a threshold moment: "The consistency of the findings at the 0.4 mg/kg dose, including complete and durable pgRNA loss to undetectable levels, reproducible liver biopsies demonstrating evidence of cccDNA elimination, and a treatment effect in all patients with a manageable safety profile, supports advancement to a global Phase 2 study." Dr. Cassie Gorsuch , Precision's Chief Scientific Officer, highlighted the HBeAg-positive result as the dataset's headline finding: "The highlight of the data was demonstrating pgRNA loss to undetectable levels in our first HBeAg positive patient dosed on study, indicating potent effect of PBGENE-HBV in a patient population that is very difficult to treat due to logarithmically higher amounts of cccDNA and viral load in the liver." Lead investigator Dr. Man-Fung Yuen connected the biopsy findings to the clinical ambition behind the program: "Reproducing the liver biopsy evidence of cccDNA elimination in a second patient treated at 0.4 mg/kg, together with durable pgRNA loss in patients with longer follow-up, is particularly important because it links the intended mechanism of action, cccDNA elimination, to ongoing antiviral activity. These findings provide a meaningful foundation for Phase 2 testing and for assessing whether directly targeting cccDNA can ultimately enable patients to stop long-term suppressive therapy and achieve cure." What Comes Next: ELIMINATE-B2 Based on the Phase 1 readout, Precision has formally selected 0.4 mg/kg as the go-forward dose and is advancing to ELIMINATE-B2 , a global Phase 2 study that will evaluate PBGENE-HBV both as a standalone treatment and in combination with an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) . The ASO combination arm is designed to address the integrated HBV DNA that is not targeted by PBGENE-HBV alone, with the goal of maximizing the probability of functional cure — a state in which patients can cease NUC therapy while maintaining undetectable HBV DNA. The FDA has previously indicated that sustained undetectable HBV DNA off NUC therapy is a validated endpoint for a curative label claim. PBGENE-HBV already holds FDA Fast Track designation for this indication. Precision expects to initiate dosing in ELIMINATE-B2 in Q1 2027 , with enrollment planned across multiple continents. Initial open-label data from Phase 2 are anticipated in the second half of 2027 . The company will host an investor and key opinion leader (KOL) webcast on Monday, November 9, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. ET to walk through the full AASLD dataset. Context: Why This Disease Has Been So Hard to Crack Chronic hepatitis B infects an estimated 254 million people globally and kills approximately 1.1 million people each year from cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma — making viral hepatitis the second-leading infectious cause of death worldwide, according to the WHO 2026 Global Hepatitis Report . Despite a preventive vaccine available since the early 1980s and highly effective antiviral drugs that have been available for decades, the number of people living with chronic infection has barely moved — in part because the vaccine cannot help those already infected, and in part because current antivirals cannot cure them. The cccDNA reservoir is the reason. Once a hepatocyte is infected, cccDNA forms in the nucleus as a stable, episomal (non-integrating, plasmid-like) minichromosome — a small circular piece of viral DNA wrapped in host cell proteins, maintained through rounds of cell division, invisible to the immune system, and not targeted by current antivirals. It can persist for the lifetime of an infected individual. Even when HBsAg seroconverts to undetectable — an event considered a functional cure in clinical practice today — cccDNA can remain dormant in the liver, capable of reactivating if immunity wanes. That reactivation risk is not hypothetical. Each year, an estimated 300,000 or more chronic HBV patients globally require immunosuppressive therapies — cancer chemotherapy, anti-rejection drugs after organ transplantation, biological therapies for autoimmune diseases. For these patients, residual cccDNA is a ticking clock; reactivation, when it occurs, can cause acute liver failure. A therapy that eliminates cccDNA would address this risk structurally, not just suppress its probability. That biological obstacle has made the PBGENE-HBV program one of the more closely watched in hepatology. No prior therapy had demonstrated direct, confirmed, repeat molecular editing of cccDNA in human liver tissue — until the biopsy data first shown at EASL and now expanded at AASLD. Competitive Landscape Precision is not alone in pursuing hepatitis B cure, but PBGENE-HBV occupies a distinct mechanistic category. GSK and Ionis's antisense oligonucleotide bepirovirsen completed Phase 3 trials (B-Well 1 & 2) targeting viral RNA and surface antigen, achieving a functional cure rate of 19% — a meaningful improvement over standard of care but still leaving the large majority of patients without durable cure, and without touching cccDNA. RNA interference agents from companies including Vir Biotechnology, Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, and Dicerna (now part of Novo Nordisk) have demonstrated potent suppression of circulating HBsAg. And a growing number of immunotherapeutic candidates — checkpoint inhibitors, T-cell engagers, therapeutic vaccines — aim to reinvigorate the immune response against the virus. What distinguishes PBGENE-HBV in this landscape is its direct attack on the cccDNA molecule itself, rather than on downstream products of cccDNA transcription. The theory is that eliminating the template could produce a more durable off-treatment response than any downstream suppression strategy — and could address the reactivation risk that even functional cure leaves unresolved. The Phase 2 data, expected in the second half of next year, will begin to test whether that theory translates into cure rates. The Bottom Line Precision BioSciences today presented the most detailed human evidence yet that in vivo gene editing can selectively reach, cut, and silence the hepatitis B cccDNA reservoir that has resisted every therapeutic approach for more than four decades. The Phase 1 signal — complete pgRNA loss in all evaluable patients at the go-forward dose, biopsy-confirmed cccDNA reductions reaching 35-fold, and a clean safety profile across nearly 60 infusions — is striking enough that the company is movi…

Dr. Cassie Gorsuch , Precision's Chief Scientific Officer, highlighted the HBeAg-positive result as the dataset's headline finding: "The highlight of the data was demonstrating pgRNA loss to undetectable levels in our first HBeAg positive patient dosed on study, indicating potent effect of PBGENE-HBV in a patient population that is very difficult to treat due to logarithmically higher amounts of cccDNA and viral load in the liver." Lead investigator Dr. Man-Fung Yuen connected the biopsy findings to the clinical ambition behind the program: "Reproducing the liver biopsy evidence of cccDNA elimination in a second patient treated at 0.4 mg/kg, together with durable pgRNA loss in patients with longer follow-up, is particularly important because it links the intended mechanism of action, cccDNA elimination, to ongoing antiviral activity. These findings provide a meaningful foundation for Phase 2 testing and for assessing whether directly targeting cccDNA can ultimately enable patients to stop long-term suppressive therapy and achieve cure." What Comes Next: ELIMINATE-B2 Based on the Phase 1 readout, Precision has formally selected 0.4 mg/kg as the go-forward dose and is advancing to ELIMINATE-B2 , a global Phase 2 study that will evaluate PBGENE-HBV both as a standalone treatment and in combination with an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) . The ASO combination arm is designed to address the integrated HBV DNA that is not targeted by PBGENE-HBV alone, with the goal of maximizing the probability of functional cure — a state in which patients can cease NUC therapy while maintaining undetectable HBV DNA. The FDA has previously indicated that sustained undetectable HBV DNA off NUC therapy is a validated endpoint for a curative label claim. PBGENE-HBV already holds FDA Fast Track designation for this indication. Precision expects to initiate dosing in ELIMINATE-B2 in Q1 2027 , with enrollment planned across multiple continents. Initial open-label data from Phase 2 are anticipated in the second half of 2027 . The company will host an investor and key opinion leader (KOL) webcast on Monday, November 9, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. ET to walk through the full AASLD dataset. Context: Why This Disease Has Been So Hard to Crack Chronic hepatitis B infects an estimated 254 million people globally and kills approximately 1.1 million people each year from cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma — making viral hepatitis the second-leading infectious cause of death worldwide, according to the WHO 2026 Global Hepatitis Report . Despite a preventive vaccine available since the early 1980s and highly effective antiviral drugs that have been available for decades, the number of people living with chronic infection has barely moved — in part because the vaccine cannot help those already infected, and in part because current antivirals cannot cure them. The cccDNA reservoir is the reason. Once a hepatocyte is infected, cccDNA forms in the nucleus as a stable, episomal (non-integrating, plasmid-like) minichromosome — a small circular piece of viral DNA wrapped in host cell proteins, maintained through rounds of cell division, invisible to the immune system, and not targeted by current antivirals. It can persist for the lifetime of an infected individual. Even when HBsAg seroconverts to undetectable — an event considered a functional cure in clinical practice today — cccDNA can remain dormant in the liver, capable of reactivating if immunity wanes. That reactivation risk is not hypothetical. Each year, an estimated 300,000 or more chronic HBV patients globally require immunosuppressive therapies — cancer chemotherapy, anti-rejection drugs after organ transplantation, biological therapies for autoimmune diseases. For these patients, residual cccDNA is a ticking clock; reactivation, when it occurs, can cause acute liver failure. A therapy that eliminates cccDNA would address this risk structurally, not just suppress its probability. That biological obstacle has made the PBGENE-HBV program one of the more closely watched in hepatology. No prior therapy had demonstrated direct, confirmed, repeat molecular editing of cccDNA in human liver tissue — until the biopsy data first shown at EASL and now expanded at AASLD. Competitive Landscape Precision is not alone in pursuing hepatitis B cure, but PBGENE-HBV occupies a distinct mechanistic category. GSK and Ionis's antisense oligonucleotide bepirovirsen completed Phase 3 trials (B-Well 1 & 2) targeting viral RNA and surface antigen, achieving a functional cure rate of 19% — a meaningful improvement over standard of care but still leaving the large majority of patients without durable cure, and without touching cccDNA. RNA interference agents from companies including Vir Biotechnology, Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, and Dicerna (now part of Novo Nordisk) have demonstrated potent suppression of circulating HBsAg. And a growing number of immunotherapeutic candidates — checkpoint inhibitors, T-cell engagers, therapeutic vaccines — aim to reinvigorate the immune response against the virus. What distinguishes PBGENE-HBV in this landscape is its direct attack on the cccDNA molecule itself, rather than on downstream products of cccDNA transcription. The theory is that eliminating the template could produce a more durable off-treatment response than any downstream suppression strategy — and could address the reactivation risk that even functional cure leaves unresolved. The Phase 2 data, expected in the second half of next year, will begin to test whether that theory translates into cure rates. The Bottom Line Precision BioSciences today presented the most detailed human evidence yet that in vivo gene editing can selectively reach, cut, and silence the hepatitis B cccDNA reservoir that has resisted every therapeutic approach for more than four decades. The Phase 1 signal — complete pgRNA loss in all evaluable patients at the go-forward dose, biopsy-confirmed cccDNA reductions reaching 35-fold, and a clean safety profile across nearly 60 infusions — is striking enough that the company is movi...

analysis.time: The study was presented at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) The Liver Meeting® 2026 in Denver, Colorado, on September 28, 2026. The data cutoff was September 28, 2026, and the trial began with patients receiving treatment in the lead-up to this date.
analysis.location_and_population: The study involved 25 patients with chronic hepatitis B, specifically those with detectable pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) at the start of the trial. The location is not explicitly stated, but the trial was conducted in the United States, as the company is based in Durham, North Carolina.
analysis.event: Precision BioSciences presented Phase 1 data from the ELIMINATE-B study showing that gene editing using PBGENE-HBV can eliminate the viral reservoir (cccDNA) in 92% of patients with detectable pgRNA, including all six evaluable patients at the 0.4 mg/kg dose level. This is considered the most complete human evidence yet for this approach.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study involved 25 patients, with 59 total drug administrations across four dose levels. The results indicate that 11 out of 12 patients (92%) with detectable pgRNA achieved undetectable pgRNA levels, suggesting a significant impact on the viral reservoir. The risk of reactivation of hepatitis B is reduced if cccDNA is eliminated, as it is the source of new virus particles.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study is in Phase 1, and the results are based on data up to September 28, 2026. The therapy is being advanced to a global Phase 2 study. The findings are based on a molecular readout (pgRNA) and are considered preliminary, as the long-term effects and cure status are not yet confirmed.

analysis.brief_en: A groundbreaking study presented at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) The Liver Meeting® 2026 in Denver, Colorado, on September 28, 2026, shows that gene editing using Precision BioSciences' PBGENE-HBV therapy can eliminate the hepatitis B viral reservoir (cccDNA) in 92% of patients with detectable pregenomic RNA (pgRNA). The trial involved 25 patients, with 59 total drug administrations across four dose levels. Among 12 patients with detectable pgRNA at the start, 11 achieved undetectable pgRNA levels, including all six evaluable patients at the 0.4 mg/kg dose. This is the most extensive human evidence to date for in vivo gene editing targeting hepatitis B. The therapy, based on the ARCUS platform, uses a single-chain monomeric protein to directly target the HBV polymerase gene, offering a more precise and potentially durable solution compared to existing antiviral treatments. The results suggest that eliminating cccDNA could reduce the risk of reactivation, but the findings are preliminary, and further studies are needed to confirm long-term efficacy and safety.

news.content_zh: HCPLive 于 2026 年 11 月 7 日发表的新闻报道讨论了一项使用贝匹罗韦森对 慢性乙型肝炎 的 功能性治愈 进行的研究,该研究显示出持续第 96 周的持久反应。该研究侧重于患者报告的数据和 治疗 结果,没有提供具体的病例数、死亡数或暴露数。这些发现基于临床试验的结果,并作为确认的结果呈现。该报告没有提及源数据中任何未解决的信息或限制。该分析以人类 乙型肝炎病毒 感染为中心,包括 慢性乙型肝炎 以及肝细胞癌和肝硬化等相关病症。证据不包括有关病毒传播、卫生系统影响或运营影响的详细信息。该研究是更广泛的乙型肝炎治疗方案的一部分,凸显了贝匹罗韦森在治疗该疾病方面的潜力。

According to research published in BMC Immunology, circulating T-cell receptor repertoires demonstrate distinct diversity, overlap, and segment usage patterns across these clinical cohorts. T cells play a vital role during hepatitis B virus infection by mediating both protective immunity and immunopathology. In-depth profiling of the complementarity-determining region 3 within the T-cell receptor provides critical insights into the composition and functional capacity of circulating T-cell populations. Prior to this investigation, the specific repertoire characteristics of the T-cell receptor alpha-chain and beta-chain across individuals with varying hepatitis B infection and vaccination statuses remained incompletely understood. To systematically evaluate these immune features, researchers employed high-throughput sequencing to profile the alpha-chain and beta-chain complementarity-determining region 3 repertoires within peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The study cohort comprised six inoculation-positive responders to hepatitis B vaccination, six individuals diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B, and five healthy donors. The research team systematically compared the frequency, diversity, sequence similarity, and variable and joining segment usage across the three examined groups. Discover more Study Biology Find Vaccines vaccine Vaccine Study Chemistry Sequence diversity comparisons demonstrated that the chronic hepatitis B group harbored significantly fewer unique alpha-chain and beta-chain complementarity-determining region 3 sequences than both the inoculation-positive responder group and the healthy donor group. Repertoire overlap analysis revealed marked differences in segment utilization among the study cohorts. The BUB overlap index for alpha-chain variable segments was significantly higher in inoculation-positive responders than in individuals with chronic hepatitis B (P = 0.0073) and healthy donors (P = 0.0317). For beta-chain variable segments, a significantly higher BUB index emerged specifically between inoculation-positive responders and chronic hepatitis B patients (P = 0.0002). Furthermore, identical alpha-chain complementarity-determining region 3 sequences were preferentially shared among individuals within each respective group, whereas beta-chain joining segment usage remained relatively stable across all three cohorts. The investigators concluded that circulating T cells display distinct alpha-beta complementarity-determining region 3 repertoire profiles in inoculation-positive responders and chronic hepatitis B patients. These observed signatures delineate immune differences linked to hepatitis B vaccination responsiveness and chronic disease state, which may help enhance understanding of protective vaccine-induced immunity and inform future investigations into alpha- and beta-chain strategies for hepatitis B virus diagnosis and prevention. news.content_zh: Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 11 月 8 日发表的一项研究表明,与乙型肝炎 疫苗 应答者和健康捐赠者相比,慢性乙型肝炎 患者表现出明显更少的独特 T 细胞受体 α 链和 β 链互补决定区 3 序列。该研究发表在《BMC 免疫学》上,分析了六名 疫苗 应答者、六名 慢性乙型肝炎 患者和五名健康捐赠者的 T 细胞受体库。研究发现,慢性乙型肝炎 组的 α 链和 β 链序列多样性均降低,片段利用率存在显着差异。该研究强调了与 疫苗接种 反应性和慢性疾病状态相关的免疫差异,可能有助于了解保护性免疫并为未来乙型肝炎的诊断和预防策略提供信息。没有报告具体病例或死亡人数,也没有明确说明风险水平。
