Hepatocellular carcinoma represents the predominant primary liver cancer worldwide, accounting for seventy-five to eighty-five percent of hepatic malignancies and ranking as the sixth leading cause of cancer mortality. In 2022, approximately 865,269 new cases and 757,948 deaths occurred globally. In Pakistan, disease incidence has climbed steadily, placing liver cancer among the most frequently diagnosed malignancies in adult males. The new qualitative synthesis integrates evidence from ninety-eight clinical studies published between 1990 and 2025 to delineate national disease trends and viral contributions across diverse Pakistani patient populations and healthcare settings. Pathologically, hepatocellular carcinoma develops after protracted hepatic damage and extensive cirrhosis caused by viral infections, alcohol, or non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. Within cirrhotic tissue, dysplastic macronodules progressively advance into early hepatocellular carcinoma through multi-step hepatocarcinogenesis before progressing to advanced stages. In rare instances, tumors develop within healthy liver tissue, possibly arising from malignant transformation of hepatocellular adenomas. Clinical tumor detection relies heavily on elevated alpha-fetoprotein serum biomarkers across regional medical centers. Because underlying cirrhosis remains asymptomatic in most patients, early diagnosis proves challenging, resulting in delayed clinical presentation and increased mortality. Over the course of malignant progression, the diseased liver progressively loses its capacity to maintain enzymatic balance, ultimately culminating in fatal systemic failure unless appropriate clinical intervention occurs promptly in specialized tertiary hospitals. Discover more Read Med Journals Study Biology Find Treatments To clarify national trends, investigators conducted their analysis following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines under prospective PROSPERO registration number CRD42023442582. The research protocol applied the Population, Intervention, Comparison, and Outcome framework, designating the Pakistani population as the study group and evaluating exposures to hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, viral co-infection, and alcohol consumption to assess their relative contributions. The primary measured outcome was the occurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma across patient cohorts. The review authors executed an extensive literature search across ScienceDirect, PubMed, Google Scholar, Springer, and BMC from January 2022 through March 2025, evaluating English-language studies published between 1990 and 2025 using tailored Boolean expressions, Medical Subject Headings, and manual reference screening of eligible articles to ensure comprehensive retrieval. Discover more Find Cancer Care Check Symptoms cancer Cancer Database searches initially identified 539 citations, which underwent rigorous multi-stage eligibility screening. After removing 122 duplicate publications, title and abstract evaluations excluded 263 irrelevant articles. Full-text assessments were performed on 158 candidate studies, of which 57 were eliminated for lacking sufficient data aligned with review objectives, leaving 98 eligible studies involving advanced-stage disease cohorts. A formal quantitative meta-analysis was initially considered to determine pooled prevalence figures; however, substantial methodological heterogeneity precluded statistical aggregation. The included investigations showed wide discrepancies in study design, sample sizes, patient selection, diagnostic criteria, and geographic coverage, while several reports provided qualitative findings without numerical numerators and denominators necessary for pooled estimation, prompting a descriptive qualitative systematic review approach instead of a formal statistical meta-analysis. Methodological quality across the 98 incorporated studies was evaluated using the Quality in Prognostic Studies tool across six standard domains: study participation, study attrition, prognostic factor measurement, outcome measurement, confounding account, and statistical analysis. Overall, 41 studies exhibited low risk of bias, 38 moderate risk, and 19 high risk. Prognostic factor and outcome assessments demonstrated the lowest risk of bias because most studies employed established diagnostic standards for hepatic malignancy and viral infections. Conversely, confounding measurement showed the highest proportion of moderate-to-high risk ratings due to inadequate adjustment for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, and cirrhosis severity. These statistical reporting limitations and retrospective designs yielded an overall moderate confidence in the evidence, requiring cautious interpretation across regional healthcare settings. Among evaluated causes, chronic hepatitis C virus infection proved to be the primary cause of liver cancer across Pakistan, examined across 32 included studies. Globally, hepatitis C affects roughly 71.1 million people, but in Pakistan the blood-borne RNA virus maintains hyper-endemic transmission that imposes an immense clinical and economic toll. Transmission occurs primarily through contaminated blood products, unsafe medical injections, and inadequate equipment sterilization during healthcare procedures. With approximately 1.5 million blood donations collected annually in Pakistan, rigorous donor screening remains central to transmission control, particularly given estimated hepatitis C prevalence of 3.31 percent plus or minus 1.96 percent among healthy blood donors. Of the 32 dedicated hepatitis C studies, 21 confirmed that chronic infection induced hepatocellular carcinoma, 8 observed the highest incidence from hepatitis C, and only 3 reported a low incidence. Geographical analyses across Pakistan revealed pronounced regional differences in viral hepatitis and cancer distribution. Southern Pakistan showed hepatitis C and hepatitis B population prevalence rates of 1.84 percent and 1.7 percent, whereas northern areas recorded 1.3 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively. Center-specific studies reflected these patterns: Islamabad’s Nuclear Medicine Oncology and Radiotherapy Institute found 44.7 percent of liver cancer patients positive for hepatitis C, 13.1 percent for hepatitis B, and 4.3 percent co-infected. In Lahore, Shaikh Zayed Postgraduate Medical Institute observed hepatitis C in 75 percent, hepatitis B in 10 percent, and co-infection in 10 percent. Multan recorded 80 percent hepatitis C and 11 percent hepatitis B, while Muzaffargarh reported 67.3 percent hepatitis C, 5.9 percent hepatitis B, and 7.9 percent co-infection. Additional regional data illustrated continued hepatitis C predominance in northwest and southern centers alongside distinct localized exceptions. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, provincial research showed that 77.78 percent of liver cancer patients carried hepatitis C, 17.78 percent had viral co-infection, and only 4.44 percent had isolated hepatitis B. In Sindh, combined data from Isra University Hospital and Liaquat University Hospital in Hyderabad demonstrated 72.5 percent hepatitis C, 21.0 percent hepatitis B, 10.5 percent concurrent alcoholic liver disease with hepatitis C, and 6.5 percent viral co-infections. In Baluchistan, 7.5 percent of evaluated tumor patients had prior exposure to hepatitis B, hepatitis C, or co-infection. Conversely, Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre in Karachi documented hepatitis B in 67 percent of cancer patients and hepatitis C in 33 percent, demonstrating substantial epidemiological heterogeneity across geographic regions. Twenty included studies specifically evaluated hepatitis B virus contributions to hepatocellular carcinoma across the country. Globally, hepatitis B affects approximately 284 million individuals, with associated annual mortality climbing from 580,500 deaths in 1990 to 799,000 deaths by 2017. Although national blood donor surveys show donor hepatitis B prevalence between 2.41 percent and 1.96 percent, reflecting a gradual reduction, specific districts in northern Pakistan exhibit substantial endemicity. Reported regional rates include 13.35 percent in Mardan, 13.5 percent in Bannu, 14.15 percent in Peshawar, 14.15 percent in Kohat, 14.63 percent in Dera Ismail Khan, and 16.35 percent in Malakand. Among the 20 evaluated hepatitis B studies, 13 confirmed chronic infection induction, 5 reported it as the primary cause, and 2 noted low incidence, reflecting an epidemiological transition from earlier decades when hepatitis B predominated. Viral co-infection was examined in 20 studies, demonstrating that dual hepatitis B and hepatitis C exposure causes severe disease burdens. Multiple clinical cohorts documented significant co-infection proportions: Butt and colleagues identified 10 percent co-infection alongside 5 percent non-viral cases, while Farooqi and Farooqi recorded 17.78 percent. Other cohorts observed co-infection frequencies ranging from 2.44 percent to 10.3 percent, occasionally alongside hepatitis D or non-B non-C etiologies. Long-term demographic forecasts by Zahoor and colleagues projected hepatitis B and hepatitis C infection prevalence rates of approximately 3.25 percent and 6.36 percent by 2030. These ongoing projections indicate that sustained viral circulation will continue to fuel chronic liver disease and primary liver cancer across Pakistan without enhanced clinical intervention, expanded screening programs, and active patient surveillance. In sharp contrast to Western cohorts where alcohol abuse represents a major cause of liver malignancy, alcohol-induced hepatocellular carcinoma remains exceptionally rare in Pakistan. Only six studies evaluated alcohol, with Khan and colleagues reporting that merely 2 percent of cancer patients had an alcohol history, despite general observations that regular alcohol intake increases cancer risk by approximately 6 percent. Low alcohol-associated frequencies were consistently observed across three studies from Lahore and two from Sindh, while a Peshawar cohort identified alcohol-related disease in 3.2 percent of cases. Concurrently, emerging non-viral risks including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obesity, type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, and dietary aflatoxin B1 exposure causing TP53 gene mutations represent recognized global carcinogens, but empirical clinical research systematically evaluating their contribution in Pakistan remains remarkably scarce. Regarding clinical management, a subset of included studies reported interventions across tertiary medical centers, encompassing surgical resection, liver transplantation, local ablation, transarterial procedures, and systemic pharmacological therapies. Surgical intervention constituted the most frequently utilized therapeutic modality, documented in 1,820 managed cases, alongside microwave ablation, radiofrequency ablation, transarterial chemoembolization, transarterial radioembolization, and systemic drugs such as sorafenib, lenvatinib, and immune checkpoint inhibitors. However, treatment reporting varied substantially across published literature, frequently omitting tumor staging, allocation guidelines, and survival outcomes, while access to liver transplantation and advanced immunotherapy remains geographically constrained. Review authors concluded that addressing referral bias, establishing comprehensive national cancer registries, expanding hepatitis B vaccination, and widening direct-acting antiviral coverage will be critical to mitigating the expanding burden of hepatocellular carcinoma in Pakistan. Published as a meeting report in BMC Proceedings, the summit examined the epidemiological landscape, programmatic frameworks, systemic barriers, and strategic pathways required to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat in India by 2030, aligned with the World Health Organization Global Health Sector Strategies 2022–2030 and Sustainable Development Goal 3.3. Across 14 sessions featuring 46 talks and four panel discussions, participants evaluated global models, regional data from Southeast Asia, diagnostic advances, and community-level initiatives. The proceedings underscored that while India established the National Viral Hepatitis Control Program in 2018 under the National Health Mission, urgent operational hurdles persist with only five years remaining to meet global elimination targets. Epidemiological evidence presented at the summit indicates that India accounts for 11.6 percent of the global hepatitis B virus and hepatitis C virus burden, representing about 29,800,000 people living with hepatitis B and 5,500,000 people living with hepatitis C. Globally, viral hepatitis causes between 1.3 million and 1.4 million deaths annually, an impact strikingly identical to the mortality caused by tuberculosis. However, summit discussions highlighted two distinct characteristics of viral hepatitis mortality: fatalities are actively increasing, yet they remain preventable through existing interventions, specifically preventive hepatitis B vaccines and curative direct-acting antiviral therapies for hepatitis C. Across the broader World Health Organization Southeast Asia Region, an estimated 61.4 million individuals live with hepatitis B and 9.1 million live with hepatitis C. These figures highlight a substantial concentration of chronic viral infections that place sustained pressure on regional healthcare delivery systems. Within the Southeast Asia Region, the disease burden comprises 24 percent of global viral hepatitis cases, 10 percent of human immunodeficiency virus infections, and 16 percent of sexually transmitted infections. Chronic hepatitis B and hepatitis C infections are responsible for two-thirds of cirrhosis cases worldwide, and in Southeast Asia, more than half of all cirrhosis cases stem from these viruses, with a documented hepatitis B to hepatitis C ratio of 0.9. To inform Indian strategy, summit participants reviewed international operational models, highlighting Egypt’s successful hepatitis C program, which achieved widespread elimination through universal adult testing, extensive public awareness campaigns, digitized registries, and comprehensive patient follow-up. In addition, Pakistan’s Local Hepatitis Elimination and Prevention program illustrated the effectiveness of door-to-door screening for hepatitis B and hepatitis C paired with direct referral to clinical care, demonstrating practical decentralized approaches that could be adapted to Indian healthcare delivery. Discover more Check Symptoms Find Treatments Healthcare Health health India’s domestic response is anchored in the National Viral Hepatitis Control Program, launched in 2018 under the National Health Mission and modeled on earlier regional successes in the state of Punjab. That initiative, the Mukh Mantri Punjab Hepatitis C Relief Fund, established standardized diagnostic algorithms and treatment guidelines to address high prevalence rates, especially among intravenous drug users. The Punjab framework trained approximately 120 primary care physicians across 25 regional centers and deployed a tracking mechanism that alerted medical staff after two to three months of lost contact, thereby significantly reducing loss to follow-up. Scaling this design nationwide, the national program now maintains 978 treatment sites across 711 districts and has trained approximately 4,900 master trainers, granting treatment access to about 300,000 patients. Summit delegates emphasized that further expansion requires collaboration with established networks such as the National AIDS Control Program and technical assistance from TREAT Asia to support same-day testing and treatment models. Addressing viral hepatitis within vulnerable populations represented another central priority during the summit, where delegates examined persistent social stigma and structural inequities. Viral hepatitis frequently co-occurs with psychiatric conditions, including depression, schizophrenia, and borderline personality disorder, where stigma and reduced awareness substantially delay clinical diagnosis and medical care. Women’s health faces comparable neglect, with documented discrimination within healthcare settings, an absence of women-centric clinical pathways, distant testing facilities, and physiological diagnostic challenges such as transient reductions in alanine aminotransferase enzyme levels during pregnancy. Additionally, individuals with comorbidities and disabilities experience acute barriers to accessing care, as demonstrated by the VaccinEquity evaluation during the COVID-19 pandemic, which uncovered widespread obstacles including software applications that lacked visual accessibility, an absence of physical ramps or accessible transport, rigid binary queues, and discriminatory conduct by healthcare facility staff. These structural shortcomings highlight an urgent need for disability-inclusive health interventions and decentralized female-focused clinics nationwide. Discover more Get Health Tips Soothe Digestion Study Biology Tailored community strategies were proposed to support people who inject drugs, sex workers, and members of LGBTQIA+ communities, who frequently encounter profound stigma. For transgender individuals and sex workers, recommendations focused on establishing testing camps in institutional settings, scheduling flexible operational hours that accommodate work routines, training healthcare personnel, offering peer counseling, and maintaining dedicated support helplines. Among people who inject drugs, systematic data regarding hepatitis testing and treatment remain scarce because these individuals rarely access conventional hospital care. To mitigate transmission risks, the summit advocated harm reduction measures including needle-syringe exchange programs, oral opioid substitution therapy, reflex laboratory testing, and designated care coordinators. Crucially, clinicians stressed educating patients about post-cure reinfection risks, condom usage for prevention, periodic re-testing protocols to prevent diagnostic delays, and rapid antiviral intervention for acute hepatitis C reinfections. Nationally, overcoming these challenges will require stronger political commitment, robust data management, and sustained funding from central and state steering committees. Innovative solutions discussed at the meeting incorporated public health design thinking centered on four interactive activities: listening, observing, reading, and conducting ongoing dialogue with patients across care pathways. Community-level engagements, including educational street plays in rural regions, demonstrated practical value in raising health literacy. Similarly, community-based entities such as the Community Network for Empowerment have pioneered decentralized, same-day test-and-treat models alongside hepatitis vaccination campaigns tailored for people who inject drugs. In terms of clinical technology, transient elastography was identified as a critical point-of-care tool to detect asymptomatic liver fibrosis and cirrhosis that routine screenings overlook. However, pharmacological advances encounter substantial hurdles; the direct-acting antiviral combination glecaprevir/pibrentasvir demonstrates a 98 percent cure rate in non-cirrhotic hepatitis C genotype 3 over eight weeks and 84 percent over four weeks, but its utilization in India remains severely restricted due to patent barriers, exclusion from voluntary manufacturing licenses, and common patient reliance on traditional alternatives. Institutional innovations highlighted how decentralized care models can reach isolated settings, exemplified by programs developed at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences Rishikesh. Having established preventive hepatology clinics in 2021 and regular screening camps for fatty liver conditions, AIIMS Rishikesh implemented the Liver Induction Training and Update Program to train clinical practitioners. In a targeted prison micro-elimination initiative in Uttarakhand, medical teams deployed unmanned aerial drones to deliver hepatitis C therapeutics directly to ten inmates at Haridwar District Jail, while using drones to transport blood samples to diagnostic laboratories and conducting inmate clinical evaluations via telemedicine. Digital innovations featured prominently, notably the launch of the Hepat App by the Chennai Liver Foundation in collaboration with the Indian Council of Medical Research and the National Institute of Epidemiology. The application functions offline, meets Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources standards, aligns with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, and supports clinical surveillance across viral hepatitis, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension. Participants emphasized that digital tools must be reinforced by user-friendly information systems, noting that the National Viral Hepatitis Control Program’s paperless management platform provides structured clinical modules and decision support. Delegates called for a national registry of healthcare professionals, along with the adoption of artificial intelligence chatbots for triage, voice-to-text documentation, and remote monitoring. To address severe capacity shortages, the Chennai Liver Foundation, ICMR, and NIE introduced an accredited online curriculum via learn.hepat.app aiming to train 10,000 healthcare workers. In clinical sessions addressing hepatocellular carcinoma, experts warned that although documented incidence appears low, liver cancer mortality in India is disproportionately elevated, with 80 to 90 percent of patients diagnosed too late for curative therapy. Driven by chronic hepatitis B, hepatitis C, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and alcohol consumption, liver cancer cases are projected to rise over two to three decades, necessitating integrated hepatology and alcohol clinics, early screening through tailors and barbers, and comprehensive palliative care linked to the national helpline 1800-202-7777. The summit concluded with comprehensive stakeholder commitments to accelerate national progress toward the 2030 viral elimination targets. Key priorities include strengthening national program implementation, boosting timely birth-dose hepatitis B vaccination and maternal interventions to reduce under-five hepatitis B prevalence to 0.1 percent or below, and securing stable supply chains for affordable vaccines, diagnostics, and antiviral drugs. Professional medical associations committed to training non-specialist clinicians, enhancing linkage to care, and integrating hepatitis services with primary care, HIV, tuberculosis, and maternal-child health programs. Civil society groups pledged to lead community-level awareness, combat discrimination, generate demand, and deliver decentralized peer support. Finally, private industry and pharmaceutical manufacturers agreed to invest in accessible point-of-care diagnostic tools, support educational campaigns, and establish innovative financing structures to reduce catastrophic out-of-pocket costs for individuals requiring treatment, solidifying a coordinated national framework to eliminate viral hepatitis across India. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 13, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Bibliometric Analysis Traces Global Hepatitis D Research and Evolving Antiviral Strategies by November 10, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Bibliometric Analysis Traces Global Hepatitis D Research and Evolving Antiviral Strategies Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive bibliometric investigation has mapped the global evolution of hepatitis D virus research and its emerging therapeutic landscape, quantitatively evaluating 1,074 scientific publications retrieved from the Scopus database to trace developments across virological biology, institutional networks, and therapeutics. Hepatitis D virus, designated as HDV, represents a unique animal pathogen possessing a concise 1.7-kilobase circular ribonucleic acid genome that functions as a satellite virus within host cells. Classified within the family Kolmioviridae and genus Deltavirus, the pathogen lacks the genetic capacity to encode its own envelope proteins or autonomous replication machinery. Consequently, HDV requires the obligate assistance of hepatitis B virus, known as HBV, as a helper virus to synthesize surface envelope structures and propagate within host tissue. Both viruses utilize identical hepatocyte entry mechanisms and share hepatitis B surface antigen envelope proteins to enter hepatocytes. By applying bibliometric methods to the literature, the study characterizes how molecular insights have guided research toward targeted antiviral candidates. The global public health burden imposed by hepatitis D virus infection remains substantial, with epidemiological estimates documented in the analysis indicating that the satellite pathogen affects at least 15 to 20 million individuals worldwide and causes severe liver disease. When coinfecting or superinfecting patients alongside hepatitis B virus, HDV dramatically accelerates disease progression toward hepatic fibrosis, liver cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, the second leading cause of cancer worldwide. Researchers have isolated eight major HDV genotypes distributed throughout diverse geographical regions, each displaying distinct clinical characteristics. Among these lineages, genotype 3, commonly designated as Amazonian HDV or HDV-3, exhibits marked pathogenicity compared to other genotypes, driving rapid progression toward end-stage liver cirrhosis in affected populations. Despite the severity of these clinical outcomes, developing targeted therapeutics has historically proven difficult due to the exceptional characteristics of the pathogen, leaving clinicians with minimal disease-specific interventions. Discover more Save on Rx Donate to Research Find Treatments Mechanistic evaluations in the study trace the recognition of hepatitis D virus to Torino during the mid-1970s, when researchers detected a novel antigen in patients with severe hepatitis B. Initially presumed to represent an internal delta antigen expressed directly by hepatitis B virus, subsequent investigations uncovered a distinct subtype of hepatitis B surface antigen, prompting the United States National Institutes of Health to identify the new RNA virus as hepatitis D virus. Following genome cloning in 1986, investigators confirmed that the virus encodes only hepatitis delta antigen, occurring in large and small forms. Because HDV lacks non-structural genes for replication and structural genes for envelope production, it relies on host cell polymerases to complete genomic replication and borrows HBV surface proteins for virion assembly. Hepatocyte entry depends upon host cellular factors, specifically sodium taurocholate co-transporting polypeptide and glypican 5, making receptor blockade a key therapeutic objective despite side effects associated with targeting host factors. Discover more Check Symptoms Learn Sociology Find Study Aids Study Biology To quantitatively assess scientific literature addressing hepatitis D virus and its potential treatments, the investigators established a systematic bibliometric extraction protocol utilizing the Scopus database through October 22, 2024. The data collection framework incorporated the search terms ‘Hepatitis D’ and ‘Treatment’ across titles, abstracts, and author keywords, adhering to standardized bibliometric guidelines formulated by Montazeri and colleagues. Extracted records included publication years, source journal identities, article titles, author affiliations, digital object identifiers, abstract texts, citation metrics, and keyword distributions, which were exported in comma-separated values and research information systems formats. Data curation, organization, and statistical breakdowns were subsequently conducted utilizing Microsoft Excel alongside RStudio running the dplyr data manipulation package. To examine relational structures within the global literature, the authors utilized VOSviewer software, generating network visualisations depicting co-citation connections, journal bibliometric coupling, author collaborative groups, and institutional co-occurrence patterns spanning thousands of peer-reviewed journals indexed across medical, technical, and social sciences. The bibliometric search yielded a total corpus of 1,074 published documents, demonstrating a dominant reliance on English-language dissemination while capturing regional contributions in other languages. English-language documents comprised 1,041 publications within the retrieved dataset, accompanied by 29 publications written in French and 9 published in Spanish. Within the 1,041 English documents selected for analysis, researchers cataloged 638 original articles, 280 reviews, 33 chapters, 30 letters, 21 editorials, 17 conference papers, and 9 notes. Annual publication output grew progressively, reaching a peak in 2023 with 107 published documents indexed under the keyword criteria. For the year 2024, the dataset captured 90 publications distributed across 60 academic journals through late October. The researchers noted that annual publication volume was higher in 2021 than in 2022, suggesting that attention toward hepatitis D research may have experienced temporary suppression during the global disruptions caused by the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. Geographical analysis of the 1,041 English-language publications demonstrated that hepatitis D research involves contributors across 102 countries, though productivity remains concentrated within a select group of heavily funded nations. The United States produced the largest volume of scholarship, accounting for 245 documents and generating 8,431 citations while exhibiting the highest network link strength of 26,085 in collaborative co-authorship mapping. Italy achieved the second highest productivity with 177 publications, closely followed by Germany with 170 published documents and 8,225 citations. When applying an analytical threshold requiring nations to possess at least three documents with a minimum of 50 citations each, only 38 countries satisfied the criteria. The authors observed that high publication output from specific countries is governed by access to research funding, specialized scientific infrastructure, and administrative policy priorities rather than regional disease prevalence, emphasizing that sheer publication counts do not inherently indicate the underlying scientific quality of individual investigations. Institutional and individual author evaluations mapped extensive research clusters across academic medical centers and specialized liver research institutes. Among 3,371 identified organizations, more than 1,000 contributed substantially, led by German centers: Hannover Medical School authored 31 documents with 2,138 citations, while University Hospital Heidelberg contributed 11 documents with 691 citations. Other active institutions included the National Institute of Infectious Diseases, the University of Ankara Medical School in Turkey, and the Center for Liver Disease at the University of Milan in Italy. Individual author rankings showed that H. Wedemeyer published 53 documents garnering 2,684 citations, followed by Cihan Yurdaydin with 34 publications and 1,457 citations, while five scientists—Graeme Alexander, Henri Bismuth, Beatrice Ducot, Luigi Fassati, and Rainer Muller—achieved over 1,000 citations on a single publication. The Journal of Hepatology led total volume with 65 documents and 3,626 citations, followed by Hepatology with 43 documents, while The Lancet Infectious Diseases achieved the highest average citation rate at 382.66. Topical keyword co-occurrence mapping provided granular insights into the evolving conceptual focus of hepatitis D therapeutic investigations. From a total collection of 6,477 extracted keywords, 232 terms met the frequency threshold of appearing at least 30 times, clustering into four primary thematic categories centered on ‘human’, ‘hepatitis d’, ‘hepatitis b’, and ‘antivirus/antiviral agent’. Terms relating to ‘human’ or ‘humans’ exhibited the highest overall abundance at 25 percent, while ‘hepatitis d’ or ‘hepatitis delta virus’ represented 19 percent, and ‘hepatitis b’ or ‘hepatitis b virus’ constituted 17 percent of keyword occurrences. Author-assigned keywords comprised 1,413 terms, with 103 appearing five or more times. Network mapping linked human study descriptors with clinical terminology including liver cirrhosis, adult demographics, and antiviral pharmacology. Concurrently, the antiviral agent cluster exhibited strong co-occurrence ties to distinct pharmacotherapies, highlighting terms such as lonafarnib, interferon-alpha, polyethylene glycol, bulevirtide, and lamivudine alongside broader measures of drug efficacy. Reviewing specific therapeutic classes, the authors detailed immunomodulatory approaches alongside newer receptor-targeting compounds. Interferon-alpha has served as the primary antiviral therapy since the 1980s, enhancing natural killer and T cells to suppress cell division-mediated viral spread, with the keyword appearing 497 times in the dataset. Pegylated interferon-alpha, administered for treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks, prolongs systemic half-life through polyethylene glycol conjugation and reduces both HDV and HBV replication, although its clinical utility is constrained by limited efficacy and significant adverse effects. Investigational type-III interferon-lambda has demonstrated improved tolerability in humanized mouse models and entered clinical evaluation. Targeting viral entry, bulevirtide, formerly designated Myrcludex B and referenced 125 times, acts as a synthetic entry inhibitor consisting of 47 myristoylated amino acids derived from the preS1 domain of large hepatitis B surface antigen. Approved in the European Union in 2020, bulevirtide binds the NTCP receptor, sustaining virological and biochemical responses across 48 to 96 weeks in ongoing monotherapy trials. Beyond entry inhibition, the bibliometric analysis outlined emerging therapeutic modalities targeting viral maturation, subviral assembly, and viral transcript stability. The farnesyltransferase inhibitor lonafarnib, an oral drug approved for progeria that appeared 55 times, blocks the farnesylation of large delta antigen, halting viral assembly and reducing viral RNA in phase 2a and ritonavir-boosted phase 3 trials. Phosphorothioate nucleic acid polymers, including REP-2055, REP-2139, and REP-2165, feature hydrophobic sulfur linkages that disrupt subviral particle release, with calcium-chelated REP-2139 reducing both surface antigen and HDV RNA. Additional pipeline candidates include small interfering RNAs elebsiran and JNJ-73763989 to degrade transcripts, capsid modulator bersacapavir, and monoclonal antibody tobevibart evaluated in chimeric mice. Concluding their assessment, the authors highlighted combination strategies, including bulevirtide with pegylated interferon-alpha, while noting that exclusive reliance on Scopus data constitutes an intrinsic methodological limitation of their bibliometric survey. (2025). A bibliometric analysis of the hepatitis D virus and its therapeutic options. The bibliometric search yielded a total corpus of 1,074 published documents, demonstrating a dominant reliance on English-language dissemination while capturing regional contributions in other languages. English-language documents comprised 1,041 publications within the retrieved dataset, accompanied by 29 publications written in French and 9 published in Spanish. Within the 1,041 English documents selected for analysis, researchers cataloged 638 original articles, 280 reviews, 33 chapters, 30 letters, 21 editorials, 17 conference papers, and 9 notes. Annual publication output grew progressively, reaching a peak in 2023 with 107 published documents indexed under the keyword criteria. For the year 2024, the dataset captured 90 publications distributed across 60 academic journals through late October. The researchers noted that annual publication volume was higher in 2021 than in 2022, suggesting that attention toward hepatitis D research may have experienced temporary suppression during the global disruptions caused by the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. Geographical analysis of the 1,041 English-language publications demonstrated that hepatitis D research involves contributors across 102 countries, though productivity remains concentrated within a select group of heavily funded nations. The United States produced the largest volume of scholarship, accounting for 245 documents and generating 8,431 citations while exhibiting the highest network link strength of 26,085 in collaborative co-authorship mapping. Italy achieved the second highest productivity with 177 publications, closely followed by Germany with 170 published documents and 8,225 citations. When applying an analytical threshold requiring nations to possess at least three documents with a minimum of 50 citations each, only 38 countries satisfied the criteria. The authors observed that high publication output from specific countries is governed by access to research funding, specialized scientific infrastructure, and administrative policy priorities rather than regional disease prevalence, emphasizing that sheer publication counts do not inherently indicate the underlying scientific quality of individual investigations. Institutional and individual author evaluations mapped extensive research clusters across academic medical centers and specialized liver research institutes. Among 3,371 identified organizations, more than 1,000 contributed substantially, led by German centers: Hannover Medical School authored 31 documents with 2,138 citations, while University Hospital Heidelberg contributed 11 documents with 691 citations. Other active institutions included the National Institute of Infectious Diseases, the University of Ankara Medical School in Turkey, and the Center for Liver Disease at the University of Milan in Italy. Individual author rankings showed that H. Wedemeyer published 53 documents garnering 2,684 citations, followed by Cihan Yurdaydin with 34 publications and 1,457 citations, while five scientists—Graeme Alexander, Henri Bismuth, Beatrice Ducot, Luigi Fassati, and Rainer Muller—achieved over 1,000 citations on a single publication. The Journal of Hepatology led total volume with 65 documents and 3,626 citations, followed by Hepatology with 43 documents, while The Lancet Infectious Diseases achieved the highest average citation rate at 382.66. Topical keyword co-occurrence mapping provided granular insights into the evolving conceptual focus of hepatitis D therapeutic investigations. From a total collection of 6,477 extracted keywords, 232 terms met the frequency threshold of appearing at least 30 times, clustering into four primary thematic categories centered on ‘human’, ‘hepatitis d’, ‘hepatitis b’, and ‘antivirus/antiviral agent’. Terms relating to ‘human’ or ‘humans’ exhibited the highest overall abundance at 25 percent, while ‘hepatitis d’ or ‘hepatitis delta virus’ represented 19 percent, and ‘hepatitis b’ or ‘hepatitis b virus’ constituted 17 percent of keyword occurrences. Author-assigned keywords comprised 1,413 terms, with 103 appearing five or more times. Network mapping linked human study descriptors with clinical terminology including liver cirrhosis, adult demographics, and antiviral pharmacology. Concurrently, the antiviral agent cluster exhibited strong co-occurrence ties to distinct pharmacotherapies, highlighting terms such as lonafarnib, interferon-alpha, polyethylene glycol, bulevirtide, and lamivudine alongside broader measures of drug efficacy. Reviewing specific therapeutic classes, the authors detailed immunomodulatory approaches alongside newer receptor-targeting compounds. Interferon-alpha has served as the primary antiviral therapy since the 1980s, enhancing natural killer and T cells to suppress cell division-mediated viral spread, with the keyword appearing 497 times in the dataset. Pegylated interferon-alpha, administered for treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks, prolongs systemic half-life through polyethylene glycol conjugation and reduces both HDV and HBV replication, although its clinical utility is constrained by limited efficacy and significant adverse effects. Investigational type-III interferon-lambda has demonstrated improved tolerability in humanized mouse models and entered clinical evaluation. Targeting viral entry, bulevirtide, formerly designated Myrcludex B and referenced 125 times, acts as a synthetic entry inhibitor consisting of 47 myristoylated amino acids derived from the preS1 domain of large hepatitis B surface antigen. Approved in the European Union in 2020, bulevirtide binds the NTCP receptor, sustaining virological and biochemical responses across 48 to 96 weeks in ongoing monotherapy trials. Beyond entry inhibition, the bibliometric analysis outlined emerging therapeutic modalities targeting viral maturation, subviral assembly, and viral transcript stability. The farnesyltransferase inhibitor lonafarnib, an oral drug approved for progeria that appeared 55 times, blocks the farnesylation of large delta antigen, halting viral assembly and reducing viral RNA in phase 2a and ritonavir-boosted phase 3 trials. Phosphorothioate nucleic acid polymers, including REP-2055, REP-2139, and REP-2165, feature hydrophobic sulfur linkages that disrupt subviral particle release, with calcium-chelated REP-2139 reducing both surface antigen and HDV RNA. Additional pipeline candidates include small interfering RNAs elebsiran and JNJ-73763989 to degrade transcripts, capsid modulator bersacapavir, and monoclonal antibody tobevibart evaluated in chimeric mice. Concluding their assessment, the authors highlighted combination strategies, including bulevirtide with pegylated interferon-alpha, while noting that exclusive reliance on Scopus data constitutes an intrinsic methodological limitation of their bibliometric survey. analysis.event: A bibliometric analysis traced the global evolution of hepatitis D virus research and its emerging therapeutic landscape, evaluating 1,074 scientific publications from the Scopus database. analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) affects at least 15 to 20 million individuals worldwide and causes severe liver disease. analysis.brief_en: A bibliometric analysis conducted by researchers has traced the global evolution of hepatitis D virus (HDV) research and its emerging therapeutic strategies. The study evaluated 1,074 scientific publications from the Scopus database, highlighting the role of HDV as a satellite virus that requires hepatitis B virus (HBV) for replication and propagation. HDV, classified within the family Kolmioviridae and genus Deltavirus, lacks the genetic capacity to encode its own envelope proteins or replication machinery, relying on HBV for these functions. The research identified eight major HDV genotypes, with genotype 3 (Amazonian HDV or HDV-3) showing marked pathogenicity and accelerating liver disease progression. The study also noted that HDV affects at least 15 to 20 million individuals worldwide and contributes to severe liver conditions, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. The analysis revealed that hepatitis D research involves contributors from 102 countries, though productivity is concentrated in a few heavily funded nations. The findings are based on published literature and do not include direct clinical or epidemiological data on outbreaks or cases.

Read more November 6th, 2026 Recent Guideline Updates in the Management of Urinary Tract Infections Recent urinary tract infection guideline updates from multiple international medical societies highlight evolving recommendations, including a major shift in classification, moving from anatomy- and risk factor–based definitions toward distinguishing localized from systemic infections. Read more September 26th, 2026 Environmental Stewardship: The Role of Antimicrobials in Climate Change Widespread antimicrobial use disrupts vital microbial communities that regulate Earth’s biogeochemical cycles, driving antimicrobial resistance, worsening human and environmental health, and significantly contributing to climate change. Read more September 17th, 2026 New Diagnositics for Legionella Pneumonia May Streamline Care Continuum Reported cases of Legionnaires’ disease have been on the rise for the past decade, and identifying Legionella bacteria requires specialized testing in the microbiology lab. Here is a clinical overview of Legionella bacteria, including required testing, treatment, and reporting to public health officials. Read more September 16th, 2026 Ceftriaxone Safety: Separating Signal From Risk A retrospective multihospital study found that severe adverse events occurred at similarly low rates with ceftriaxone and other IV cephalosporins suggesting there is no evidence to support avoiding ceftriaxone despite recent health department safety alerts. Read more September 12th, 2026 Treatment of Latent Tuberculosis in a Trice A retrospective study of 225 patients across Cook County Department of Health clinics found that the novel 1-month 1HP regimen (isoniazid plus rifapentine) for latent TB infection had a completion rate comparable to standard longer regimens and was well tolerated, suggesting it may be a viable shorter alternative. Read more September 10th, 2026 This Is the “Weight” Forward: GLP-1 Use in HIV Care Here is a review of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use in people with HIV. Read more August 16th, 2026 When Daptomycin Fails: Practical Approaches to Resistant Enterococcus faecium Daptomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium bacteremia is an emerging, high-mortality challenge in transplant and other high-risk patients, requiring early recognition, aggressive source control, and reliance on limited alternatives—most notably linezolid—with combination or salvage therapies considered when options are constrained. Published on November 9, 2026, the report indicates that these drugs showed effectiveness in treating Hepatitis Delta, a virus closely related to the Hepatitis B virus. However, the evidence does not specify the exact location or population affected, nor does it provide details on the number of cases, deaths, or exposures. The report also does not mention the current status of the investigation or any uncertainties related to the findings. This study is part of broader efforts to address Hepatitis B-related conditions, including chronic and acute infections, and associated complications like hepatocellular carcinoma and cirrhosis. The results suggest potential advancements in treatment options for Hepatitis B and its related viruses, but further research and clinical validation are needed to confirm their efficacy and safety in real-world settings.

news.title_zh: Elebsiran 和 Tobevibart 达到了 Delta 型肝炎研究的主要终点 - Contagion Live
news.source_body_en: The news report from Contagion Live highlights that Elebsiran and Tobevibart have met the primary endpoint in a study focused on Hepatitis Delta. Published on November 9, 2026, the report indicates that these drugs showed effectiveness in treating Hepatitis Delta, a virus closely related to the Hepatitis B virus. However, the evidence does not specify the exact location or population affected, nor does it provide details on the number of cases, deaths, or exposures. The report also does not mention the current status of the investigation or any uncertainties related to the findings. This study is part of broader efforts to address Hepatitis B-related conditions, including chronic and acute infections, and associated complications like hepatocellular carcinoma and cirrhosis. The results suggest potential advancements in treatment options for Hepatitis B and its related viruses, but further research and clinical validation are needed to confirm their efficacy and safety in real-world settings.
news.content_zh: Contagion Live 的新闻报道强调,Elebsiran 和 Tobevibart 在一项针对 Delta 型肝炎的研究中已达到主要终点。该报告于 2026 年 11 月 9 日发布,表明这些药物对治疗丁型肝炎有效,丁型肝炎是一种与 乙型肝炎病毒 密切相关的病毒。然而,证据没有具体说明受影响的确切地点或人口,也没有提供有关病例、死亡或暴露数量的详细信息。该报告也没有提及调查的当前状况或与调查结果相关的任何不确定性。这项研究是解决乙型肝炎相关疾病(包括慢性和急性感染,以及肝细胞癌和肝硬化等相关并发症)的更广泛努力的一部分。结果表明,治疗 针对乙型肝炎及其相关病毒的选择具有潜在的进步,但需要进一步的研究和临床验证来确认其在现实环境中的有效性和安全性。

The study focuses on the efficacy of bepirovirsen in treating HBV, with no mention of other related viruses or hard exclusions. The results are based on clinical trial data from the B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 trials, indicating a promising treatment option for chronic hepatitis B. However, the report does not provide further details on the investigation, testing, or prevention measures related to this treatment.

研究人员构建了一种复合淋巴结靶向纳米佐剂NA@DCM,用于增强乙型肝炎亚单位疫苗的免疫应答。该体系以DSPE-PEG2000胶束为递送平台,通过酰胺键将CpG-NH2共轭至DSPE-PEG-NHS形成DSPE-PEG–CpG(DCM),再与纳米铝佐剂(NA)经界面物理组装构成NA@DCM。研究人员利用该体系将抗原与佐剂共递送至引流淋巴结(dLN)并实现持续滞留。结果表明,NA@DCM可诱导偏向Th1型的IgG应答、多功能T细胞反应以及生发中心(GC)免疫应答;机制上,其通过TLR9–NF-κB信号通路与线粒体ATP合成协同促进B细胞活化。该研究为乙型肝炎疫苗佐剂的理性设计提供了兼具递送优化与免疫代谢调控的新策略。 研究背景方面,乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染仍是全球重大公共卫生问题,现有重组亚单位乙肝疫苗安全性高但免疫原性有限,依赖佐剂增强。传统铝佐剂(Alum)主要诱导Th2型体液免疫,对Th1依赖的细胞免疫不足;CpG寡脱氧核苷酸作为TLR9激动剂虽能强效激活固有免疫,但游离CpG存在细胞摄取低、易核酸酶降解、体内半衰期短等问题。单一佐剂难以满足复杂免疫保护需求,而纳米递送系统可改善抗原与佐剂向引流淋巴结的运输、滞留与细胞摄取。既往纳米铝/CpG体系多依赖静电吸附或直接共轭,存在再聚集与组件关联不稳定等局限。因此,研究人员设计了一种基于胶束介导组装的复合纳米佐剂,整合CpG的TLR9刺激与纳米铝的颗粒递送优势。 免费索取义翘神州Anti-His 标签单抗详细资料领 取 该研究由研究人员构建复合纳米佐剂NA@DCM,并在小鼠模型中评估其理化性质、淋巴结分布、免疫原性与生物安全性,进一步通过转录组、蛋白印迹、代谢功能检测及药理抑制实验阐释TLR9信号与线粒体代谢在B细胞活化中的作用。论文发表于《Materials Today Bio》。核心结论为:NA@DCM可实现CpG与铝组分在dLN中的高效共富集与空间共定位,显著增强HBsAg特异性体液与细胞免疫,并通过TLR9–NF-κB通路伴随线粒体呼吸链活性、ATP合成与线粒体活性氧(mtROS)相关荧光增强驱动B细胞活化;抑制线粒体ATP合成可削弱该活化效应。 主要关键技术方法包括:以薄膜水化与界面自组装制备NA@DCM并进行动态光散射、透射电镜、XPS等理化表征;采用荧光标记与活体成像追踪dLN分布;使用雌性C57BL/6小鼠(6–8周龄,SPF级)进行三剂免疫评价,结合ELISA、胞内细胞因子染色、ELISpot分析抗体与T细胞应答;通过流式分析cDC、Tfh、GC B细胞与浆细胞;对原代小鼠B细胞及人Namalwa B细胞系开展转录组测序、Western blot、耗氧与ATP检测、呼吸链复合物活性分析,并以寡霉素A抑制线粒体ATP合酶进行功能验证。 研究结果如下: 合成与表征:研究人员通过酰胺化、胶束自组装与界面复合构建NA@DCM,表征确认其粒径约130 nm、分散均匀、CpG共轭稳定,组件间存在有机-无机界面相互作用与较好储存稳定性。 淋巴结靶向与免疫增强:活体荧光示踪显示NA@DCM在dLN中富集与滞留显著优于游离CpG;免疫后诱导更高总IgG、IgG2c偏向及Th1型T细胞应答,相较物理混合物更具优势,且与AS04-like参考佐剂可比。 早期免疫激活:NA@DCM促进树突细胞对抗原模型的摄取,并在dLN中扩增cDC、B细胞与T细胞,形成利于抗原加工与适应的微环境。 TLR9与线粒体机制:转录组富集于B细胞活化、NF-κB、TLR9级联与线粒体组织相关通路;体外实验证实NA@DCM上调TLR9、p-p65、TNF-α、IL-6,同时提升耗氧相关荧光、ATP含量及复合物I/III/IV/V活性。 线粒体ATP合成的必要性:以寡霉素A抑制复合物V后,NA@DCM引起的CD69、CD86上调与净细胞累积被显著削弱,说明线粒体ATP合成是B细胞充分活化的必要环节。 GC与浆细胞应答:体内结果显示NA@DCM促进Tfh、GC B细胞与浆细胞早期并持续扩增,B细胞活化标志与blasts形态改变明显。 生物安全性:溶血率低于5%,重复接种与剂量递增条件下未见明显毒性,具备良好生物相容性。 讨论与结论翻译:研究人员指出,NA@DCM的优势不仅在于递送效率,更在于将固有免疫信号与免疫代谢重编程耦合。TLR9–NF-κB提供上游炎症信号,线粒体氧化磷酸化与ATP合成支撑B细胞增殖、抗体类别转换与效应分化。抑制实验证明代谢重编程为功能性必需,而非单纯伴随现象。结论为:NA@DCM是一种兼具淋巴结靶向、强免疫原性与可接受安全性的复合纳米佐剂,其“递送+代谢调控”双重机制为下一代乙肝疫苗及需Th1型应答的亚单位疫苗提供了可转化的设计范式。 研究人员构建了一种复合淋巴结靶向纳米佐剂NA@DCM,用于增强乙型肝炎亚单位疫苗的免疫应答。该体系以DSPE-PEG2000胶束为递送平台,通过酰胺键将CpG-NH2共轭至DSPE-PEG-NHS形成DSPE-PEG–CpG(DCM),再与纳米铝佐剂(NA)经界面物理组装构成NA@DCM。研究人员利用该体系将抗原与佐剂共递送至引流淋巴结(dLN)并实现持续滞留。结果表明,NA@DCM可诱导偏向Th1型的IgG应答、多功能T细胞反应以及生发中心(GC)免疫应答;机制上,其通过TLR9–NF-κB信号通路与线粒体ATP合成协同促进B细胞活化。该研究为乙型肝炎疫苗佐剂的理性设计提供了兼具递送优化与免疫代谢调控的新策略。 研究背景方面,乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染仍是全球重大公共卫生问题,现有重组亚单位乙肝疫苗安全性高但免疫原性有限,依赖佐剂增强。传统铝佐剂(Alum)主要诱导Th2型体液免疫,对Th1依赖的细胞免疫不足;CpG寡脱氧核苷酸作为TLR9激动剂虽能强效激活固有免疫,但游离CpG存在细胞摄取低、易核酸酶降解、体内半衰期短等问题。单一佐剂难以满足复杂免疫保护需求,而纳米递送系统可改善抗原与佐剂向引流淋巴结的运输、滞留与细胞摄取。既往纳米铝/CpG体系多依赖静电吸附或直接共轭,存在再聚集与组件关联不稳定等局限。因此,研究人员设计了一种基于胶束介导组装的复合纳米佐剂,整合CpG的TLR9刺激与纳米铝的颗粒递送优势。 免费索取义翘神州Anti-His 标签单抗详细资料领 取 该研究由研究人员构建复合纳米佐剂NA@DCM,并在小鼠模型中评估其理化性质、淋巴结分布、免疫原性与生物安全性,进一步通过转录组、蛋白印迹、代谢功能检测及药理抑制实验阐释TLR9信号与线粒体代谢在B细胞活化中的作用。论文发表于《Materials Today Bio》。核心结论为:NA@DCM可实现CpG与铝组分在dLN中的高效共富集与空间共定位,显著增强HBsAg特异性体液与细胞免疫,并通过TLR9–NF-κB通路伴随线粒体呼吸链活性、ATP合成与线粒体活性氧(mtROS)相关荧光增强驱动B细胞活化;抑制线粒体ATP合成可削弱该活化效应。 主要关键技术方法包括:以薄膜水化与界面自组装制备NA@DCM并进行动态光散射、透射电镜、XPS等理化表征;采用荧光标记与活体成像追踪dLN分布;使用雌性C57BL/6小鼠(6–8周龄,SPF级)进行三剂免疫评价,结合ELISA、胞内细胞因子染色、ELISpot分析抗体与T细胞应答;通过流式分析cDC、Tfh、GC B细胞与浆细胞;对原代小鼠B细胞及人Namalwa B细胞系开展转录组测序、Western blot、耗氧与ATP检测、呼吸链复合物活性分析,并以寡霉素A抑制线粒体ATP合酶进行功能验证。 研究结果如下: 合成与表征:研究人员通过酰胺化、胶束自组装与界面复合构建NA@DCM,表征确认其粒径约130 nm、分散均匀、CpG共轭稳定,组件间存在有机-无机界面相互作用与较好储存稳定性。 淋巴结靶向与免疫增强:活体荧光示踪显示NA@DCM在dLN中富集与滞留显著优于游离CpG;免疫后诱导更高总IgG、IgG2c偏向及Th1型T细胞应答,相较物理混合物更具优势,且与AS04-like参考佐剂可比。 早期免疫激活:NA@DCM促进树突细胞对抗原模型的摄取,并在dLN中扩增cDC、B细胞与T细胞,形成利于抗原加工与适应的微环境。 TLR9与线粒体机制:转录组富集于B细胞活化、NF-κB、TLR9级联与线粒体组织相关通路;体外实验证实NA@DCM上调TLR9、p-p65、TNF-α、IL-6,同时提升耗氧相关荧光、ATP含量及复合物I/III/IV/V活性。 线粒体ATP合成的必要性:以寡霉素A抑制复合物V后,NA@DCM引起的CD69、CD86上调与净细胞累积被显著削弱,说明线粒体ATP合成是B细胞充分活化的必要环节。 GC与浆细胞应答:体内结果显示NA@DCM促进Tfh、GC B细胞与浆细胞早期并持续扩增,B细胞活化标志与blasts形态改变明显。 生物安全性:溶血率低于5%,重复接种与剂量递增条件下未见明显毒性,具备良好生物相容性。 讨论与结论翻译:研究人员指出,NA@DCM的优势不仅在于递送效率,更在于将固有免疫信号与免疫代谢重编程耦合。TLR9–NF-κB提供上游炎症信号,线粒体氧化磷酸化与ATP合成支撑B细胞增殖、抗体类别转换与效应分化。抑制实验证明代谢重编程为功能性必需,而非单纯伴随现象。结论为:NA@DCM是一种兼具淋巴结靶向、强免疫原性与可接受安全性的复合纳米佐剂,其“递送+代谢调控”双重机制为下一代乙肝疫苗及需Th1型应答的亚单位疫苗提供了可转化的设计范式。 news.content_title: Vir hepatitis D drug succeeds in first pivotal study
news.content: An article from Vir hepatitis D drug succeeds in first pivotal study A program that’s survived Vir’s pivot away from infectious disease research hit all of its study objectives and appeared more potent than a rival drug also in late-stage development. Published Nov. 9, 2026 Delilah Alvarado Reporter Vir Biotechnology is developing a drug combination for chronic hepatitis D infections. Getty Images An experimental two-drug combination from Vir Biotechnology has succeeded in the first of three Phase 3 trials against chronic hepatitis D, the company said Sunday. Vir’s drugs, “elebsiran” and “tobevibart,” met their main objective in the study by largely eliminating detectable signs of the virus and normalizing levels of an important liver enzyme in 44% of treatment participants after 48 weeks. By comparison, none in a “delayed treatment” cohort achieved those results, according to Vir. The regimen also met a key secondary endpoint focused solely on dropping viral levels, with 79% of treated patients achieving a treatment response. Two additional Phase 3 trials are ongoing and should produce data early next year. Results from all three studies, if positive, would support a regulatory submission in 2027. Vir was initially formed to go after infectious diseases and, in 2021, successfully brought to market a COVID-19 antibody drug called Xevudy. But the company has since restructured and changed course. It’s now primarily working on T-cell engagers for cancer. Vir clung to some of its infectious disease research, however. Even after its transition, the company kept pursuing preclinical HIV research and a pivotal-stage program in hepatitis D. Hepatitis D is a liver infection that only occurs in people who have already contracted the hepatitis B virus. People can either be infected by both viruses at the same time or get a “superinfection” when hepatitis D gets into the body after hepatitis B. The latter situation is linked to long-term illness, such as liver scarring and organ failure, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . The condition is uncommon in the U.S., but is believed by the World Health Organization to affect 5% of people with chronic hepatitis B infections worldwide . There are limited treatment options for chronic hepatitis D infections, but the landscape could be quickly changing. Earlier this year, the Food and Drug Administration made Gilead Sciences’ Hepcludex , a once-daily injection, the first approved treatment in the U.S. for chronic hepatitis D. And in September, a drug Mirum Pharmaceuticals acquired in a buyout succeeded in a Phase 3 trial. In a Monday note to clients, Evercore ISI analyst Cory Kasimov predicted that Vir’s drug combination should become the “preferred” medicine for hepatitis D and has the “potential to become a dominant front-line product upon approval.” Kasimov added that the drug’s results compared favorably to the data Gilead and Mirum have presented for their rival therapies. “Cross-trial caveats apply, but the gap is wide,” he added. Vir shares climbed by about 12% in early Monday trading. Filed Under: Biotech , Clinical Trials

news.content: 今日动态 生物通首页 今日动态 新技术专栏 人才市场 生物通首页 > 今日动态 > 正文 1990—2021年全球乙型肝炎病毒相关疾病年龄别负担特征、驱动因素量化及至2050年的趋势预测 时间:2026年11月10日 来源:Tropical Medicine and Health 编辑推荐: 背景:普及儿童免疫接种已使年轻人群中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)相关疾病的疾病负担有所下降,但人口老龄化正在增加老年人群的相关疾病负担。本研究评估了1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病的年龄别趋势,量化了驱动因素,并对至2050 广告 X 领取10x Genomics的单细胞多组学分析解决方案>> 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 “畅读会员”登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 背景:普及儿童免疫接种已使年轻人群中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)相关疾病的疾病负担有所下降,但人口老龄化正在增加老年人群的相关疾病负担。本研究评估了1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病的年龄别趋势,量化了驱动因素,并对至2050年的疾病负担进行预测,以期为优化预防策略提供依据。 方法:研究人员利用2021年全球疾病负担研究(Global Burden of Disease 2021,GBD 2021)数据,分析了1990—2021年间HBV相关疾病的发病率、患病率、死亡及伤残调整生命年(disability-adjusted life-years,DALYs)趋势。研究人员按年龄组(<20岁、20—54岁、≥55岁)对分析结果进行分层,采用Das Gupta分解法定量评估疾病负担变化的驱动因素,并按社会人口学指数(socio-demographic index,SDI)描述地理分布格局。研究人员应用贝叶斯年龄-时期-队列(Bayesian age-period-cohort,BAPC)建模对至2050年的疾病负担进行预测。 结果:1990年至2021年,全球HBV相关疾病年龄标化发病率、患病率、死亡率及DALY率均下降,而死亡与DALY的绝对数量增加。年龄分层分析显示,<20岁人群的所有疾病负担指标均急剧、一致下降;20—54岁人群及更显著的是≥55岁人群的降幅较为温和且病例数量增加。分解分析表明,流行病学改善驱动了年轻人群疾病负担的下降,而人口增长与老龄化抵消了老年人群中的这些获益。地理分布上,最高疾病负担仍集中于撒哈拉以南非洲和东南亚,而高SDI地区维持在最低水平。相对变化显示全球<20岁人群发病率降幅显著,而老年人群降幅较小。预测提示,尽管总体率将持续下降,≥55岁人群的绝对疾病负担将持续上升至2050年。 结论:尽管HBV相关疾病负担在年轻人群中持续下降,人口增长与老龄化正重塑全球HBV疾病负担格局,使其向≥55岁人群转移,凸显了针对性预防与管理策略的必要性。 一、研究背景与问题提出 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)感染仍是全球重大公共卫生挑战,其健康影响远超急性感染,还包括肝硬化和肝细胞癌等严重长期结局。随着预防控制策略推进与人口结构变化,HBV相关疾病流行病学已发生深刻转变:普及儿童免疫接种改变了年轻一代疾病趋势,而快速人口老龄化则形成了截然不同的疾病负担路径。既往研究多聚焦总体时间趋势、区域差异或疾病构成的特定组分,且年龄特异性模式、分解分析与年龄-时期-队列效应等分析视角常被单独考察,未在统一框架内整合评估;既往感染队列老化所致的老年人群绝对疾病负担上升趋势尚不明确。理解HBV相关疾病负担的年龄别转变对未来预防与管理策略制定至关重要。 Visium HD以您所需的分辨率开展全转录组空间探索,下载产品手册>> 二、研究开展概况 研究人员基于GBD 2021数据(覆盖204个国家和地区1990—2021年),将年龄别负担评估、基于社会人口学指数(socio-demographic index,SDI)的区域比较、Das Gupta分解与贝叶斯年龄-时期-队列(Bayesian age-period-cohort,BAPC)预测整合于单一分析框架,量化了流行病学变化、人口老龄化与人口增长对疾病负担变化的贡献,并预测年龄别轨迹至2050年。核心结论为:全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄别分化日益显著,人口增长与老龄化正推动疾病负担向≥55岁人群转移。 关键方法概括:研究数据源自GBD 2021数据库(204个国家和地区1990—2021年),以整合急性乙型肝炎、慢性乙型肝炎(含乙肝相关肝硬化)和乙肝相关肝癌的HBV总负担为结局指标,采用发病率、患病率、死亡及DALYs计数和年龄标化率评估负担;运用Das Gupta分解法将绝对变化拆分为流行病学率、年龄结构与人口规模三类效应;应用R软件BAPC包构建年龄-时期-队列模型,以1990—2011年数据拟合、2012—2021年数据回溯验证并以平均绝对百分比误差(mean absolute percentage error,MAPE)评估预测性能,同时设定≥55、≥60、≥65岁三种老年界点开展敏感性分析。 三、研究结果 (一)1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病年龄别负担:2021年全球HBV相关疾病发病6851万例,年龄标化发病率848.62/10万,较1990年下降41.61%;患病2.9123亿例,标化患病率3583.57/10万,下降39.05%;死亡64.918万例,标化死亡率7.57/10万,下降37.88%;DALYs达2147万,标化率252.48/10万,下降39.36%。年龄分层显示<20岁组所有指标一致下降;20—54岁与≥55岁组绝对负担轻微上升而率仅温和下降。疾病谱方面,急性乙型肝炎集中于<20岁组,HBV相关肝硬化DALY计数在20—54岁组最高,≥55岁组HBV相关肝癌DALY计数增幅最大且DALY率持续最高。 (二)全球HBV相关疾病负担变化的驱动因素:总体人群中流行病学率下降是各负担指标下降的主要贡献者(如发病例数变化中流行病学率贡献369.46%的下降,人口增长抵消270.62%,年龄结构仅贡献1.16%);年龄分层显示流行病学率效应在<20岁组最显著,而20—54岁及≥55岁组中年龄结构与人口规模的贡献常超过流行病学率改善的减少量,≥55岁组死亡中人口老龄化与人口增长分别贡献121.31%和113.59%,大幅抵消流行病学改善134.91%的下降。敏感性分析证实界点为≥55、≥60或≥65岁时结论一致。 (三)2021年全球HBV相关疾病负担的地理分布:最高负担集中于撒哈拉以南非洲和东南亚部分地区,最低年龄标化率见于西欧、北美和大洋洲等高SDI地区;<20岁组全球负担低,20—54岁组为发病与患病主要人群,≥55岁组死亡和DALY率显著更高。各年龄组地理分布相似且集中于低、中SDI地区,随年龄增长负担由以发病、患病为主转向以死亡、DALY为主。 (四)1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病负担的地理变化趋势:全球标化发病与患病率普遍下降,发病降幅最大地区为波兰、意大利和中国台湾省,患病降幅最大地区为波兰、沙特阿拉伯和中国台湾省,丹麦、匈牙利和英国降幅最小。年龄分层呈地理异质性:<20岁组几乎所有地区各率值下降超25%,部分地区超75%;20—54岁组俄罗斯联邦和乌克兰死亡与DALY率升幅超100%;≥55岁组英国、俄罗斯联邦及部分欧洲国家死亡和DALY率上升。 (五)按年龄组划分的SDI区域HBV相关疾病负担的相对变化:<20岁组所有SDI区域绝对负担均下降,中高SDI区域降幅最大;20—54岁组低SDI区域绝对负担增幅最大、高SDI区域降幅最大;≥55岁组所有SDI区域绝对负担均上升,中低SDI区域增长最陡。率值在所有年龄组和SDI区域均下降,<20岁组在中高SDI区域降幅最大,20—54岁和≥55岁组在中或更高SDI区域降幅最大。 (六)2022—2050年全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄组预测:全年龄绝对负担预计持续下降,但年龄别模式差异显著,<20岁和20—54岁组绝对负担下降,≥55岁组上升(如≥55岁组发病例数预计从2030年1250万增至2050年1578万,而<20岁组从722万降至311万)。所有年龄组率值预计下降,<20岁组降幅最大(发病率由2022年394.30/10万降至2050年127.15/10万),≥55岁组降幅最小(703.01降至583.45/10万)。回溯检验显示多数MAPE值低于10%,敏感性分析结果与主分析一致。 四、讨论部分总结 讨论指出,各年龄组间的鲜明分歧是最关键发现,解释了总体率下降与总人群绝对负担上升并存的悖论。<20岁组负担急剧一致下降,流行病学率改善为主导驱动,与疫苗接种在健康婴儿、儿童和青少年中诱导的超过95%血清保护率一致;而老年人疫苗血清保护率降至60%—70%且多出生于普遍接种之前,形成独特流行病学模式。≥55岁组所有绝对指标显著上升(发病增74.10%、患病增87.38%、死亡增42.77%、DALYs增35.86%),人口增长与老龄化联合效应远超流行病学率改善的减少量,人口压力主导了老年人群流行病学格局;这些发现应解释为人群水平模式而非个体纵向转变。地理差异与年龄别异质性并存,部分欧洲区域死亡与DALY率上升超100%,反映预防控制收益分配不均。世界卫生组织(World Health Organization,WHO)2030年消除病毒性肝炎的目标面临疾病负担老龄化的重大人口学挑战。政策启示包括:维持青少年疫苗接种进展(及时接种首针并补种);对≥55岁人群扩大筛查、强化诊断并促进抗病毒治疗;针对不同SDI区域实施差异化策略。局限性包括BAPC模型依赖历史数据、≥55岁组预测不确定性区间(uncertainty intervals,UIs)较宽、未量化疫苗接种与抗病毒治疗贡献及未详察国家内部差异。 五、研究结论部分翻译 总之,尽管全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄标化率(age-standardized rates,ASRs)已下降,≥55岁人群绝对负担却增加,人口增长和老龄化在很大程度上促成了这一转变,抵消了有利流行病学变化带来的减少。区域差异依然显著,低、中SDI地区承担最大负担。预测表明这种年龄相关转变可能持续,凸显实现WHO定义的2030年肝炎消除目标仍面临持续挑战。应对挑战需加强针对性筛查、改善老年人群抗病毒治疗可及性,并实施区域特异性的预防控制策略。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 背景:普及儿童免疫接种已使年轻人群中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)相关疾病的疾病负担有所下降,但人口老龄化正在增加老年人群的相关疾病负担。本研究评估了1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病的年龄别趋势,量化了驱动因素,并对至2050 广告 X 领取10x Genomics的单细胞多组学分析解决方案>> 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 “畅读会员”登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 背景:普及儿童免疫接种已使年轻人群中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)相关疾病的疾病负担有所下降,但人口老龄化正在增加老年人群的相关疾病负担。本研究评估了1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病的年龄别趋势,量化了驱动因素,并对至2050年的疾病负担进行预测,以期为优化预防策略提供依据。 方法:研究人员利用2021年全球疾病负担研究(Global Burden of Disease 2021,GBD 2021)数据,分析了1990—2021年间HBV相关疾病的发病率、患病率、死亡及伤残调整生命年(disability-adjusted life-years,DALYs)趋势。研究人员按年龄组(<20岁、20—54岁、≥55岁)对分析结果进行分层,采用Das Gupta分解法定量评估疾病负担变化的驱动因素,并按社会人口学指数(socio-demographic index,SDI)描述地理分布格局。研究人员应用贝叶斯年龄-时期-队列(Bayesian age-period-cohort,BAPC)建模对至2050年的疾病负担进行预测。 结果:1990年至2021年,全球HBV相关疾病年龄标化发病率、患病率、死亡率及DALY率均下降,而死亡与DALY的绝对数量增加。年龄分层分析显示,<20岁人群的所有疾病负担指标均急剧、一致下降;20—54岁人群及更显著的是≥55岁人群的降幅较为温和且病例数量增加。分解分析表明,流行病学改善驱动了年轻人群疾病负担的下降,而人口增长与老龄化抵消了老年人群中的这些获益。地理分布上,最高疾病负担仍集中于撒哈拉以南非洲和东南亚,而高SDI地区维持在最低水平。相对变化显示全球<20岁人群发病率降幅显著,而老年人群降幅较小。预测提示,尽管总体率将持续下降,≥55岁人群的绝对疾病负担将持续上升至2050年。 结论:尽管HBV相关疾病负担在年轻人群中持续下降,人口增长与老龄化正重塑全球HBV疾病负担格局,使其向≥55岁人群转移,凸显了针对性预防与管理策略的必要性。 一、研究背景与问题提出 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)感染仍是全球重大公共卫生挑战,其健康影响远超急性感染,还包括肝硬化和肝细胞癌等严重长期结局。随着预防控制策略推进与人口结构变化,HBV相关疾病流行病学已发生深刻转变:普及儿童免疫接种改变了年轻一代疾病趋势,而快速人口老龄化则形成了截然不同的疾病负担路径。既往研究多聚焦总体时间趋势、区域差异或疾病构成的特定组分,且年龄特异性模式、分解分析与年龄-时期-队列效应等分析视角常被单独考察,未在统一框架内整合评估;既往感染队列老化所致的老年人群绝对疾病负担上升趋势尚不明确。理解HBV相关疾病负担的年龄别转变对未来预防与管理策略制定至关重要。 Visium HD以您所需的分辨率开展全转录组空间探索,下载产品手册>> 二、研究开展概况 研究人员基于GBD 2021数据(覆盖204个国家和地区1990—2021年),将年龄别负担评估、基于社会人口学指数(socio-demographic index,SDI)的区域比较、Das Gupta分解与贝叶斯年龄-时期-队列(Bayesian age-period-cohort,BAPC)预测整合于单一分析框架,量化了流行病学变化、人口老龄化与人口增长对疾病负担变化的贡献,并预测年龄别轨迹至2050年。核心结论为:全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄别分化日益显著,人口增长与老龄化正推动疾病负担向≥55岁人群转移。 关键方法概括:研究数据源自GBD 2021数据库(204个国家和地区1990—2021年),以整合急性乙型肝炎、慢性乙型肝炎(含乙肝相关肝硬化)和乙肝相关肝癌的HBV总负担为结局指标,采用发病率、患病率、死亡及DALYs计数和年龄标化率评估负担;运用Das Gupta分解法将绝对变化拆分为流行病学率、年龄结构与人口规模三类效应;应用R软件BAPC包构建年龄-时期-队列模型,以1990—2011年数据拟合、2012—2021年数据回溯验证并以平均绝对百分比误差(mean absolute percentage error,MAPE)评估预测性能,同时设定≥55、≥60、≥65岁三种老年界点开展敏感性分析。 三、研究结果 (一)1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病年龄别负担:2021年全球HBV相关疾病发病6851万例,年龄标化发病率848.62/10万,较1990年下降41.61%;患病2.9123亿例,标化患病率3583.57/10万,下降39.05%;死亡64.918万例,标化死亡率7.57/10万,下降37.88%;DALYs达2147万,标化率252.48/10万,下降39.36%。年龄分层显示<20岁组所有指标一致下降;20—54岁与≥55岁组绝对负担轻微上升而率仅温和下降。疾病谱方面,急性乙型肝炎集中于<20岁组,HBV相关肝硬化DALY计数在20—54岁组最高,≥55岁组HBV相关肝癌DALY计数增幅最大且DALY率持续最高。 (二)全球HBV相关疾病负担变化的驱动因素:总体人群中流行病学率下降是各负担指标下降的主要贡献者(如发病例数变化中流行病学率贡献369.46%的下降,人口增长抵消270.62%,年龄结构仅贡献1.16%);年龄分层显示流行病学率效应在<20岁组最显著,而20—54岁及≥55岁组中年龄结构与人口规模的贡献常超过流行病学率改善的减少量,≥55岁组死亡中人口老龄化与人口增长分别贡献121.31%和113.59%,大幅抵消流行病学改善134.91%的下降。敏感性分析证实界点为≥55、≥60或≥65岁时结论一致。 (三)2021年全球HBV相关疾病负担的地理分布:最高负担集中于撒哈拉以南非洲和东南亚部分地区,最低年龄标化率见于西欧、北美和大洋洲等高SDI地区;<20岁组全球负担低,20—54岁组为发病与患病主要人群,≥55岁组死亡和DALY率显著更高。各年龄组地理分布相似且集中于低、中SDI地区,随年龄增长负担由以发病、患病为主转向以死亡、DALY为主。 (四)1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病负担的地理变化趋势:全球标化发病与患病率普遍下降,发病降幅最大地区为波兰、意大利和中国台湾省,患病降幅最大地区为波兰、沙特阿拉伯和中国台湾省,丹麦、匈牙利和英国降幅最小。年龄分层呈地理异质性:<20岁组几乎所有地区各率值下降超25%,部分地区超75%;20—54岁组俄罗斯联邦和乌克兰死亡与DALY率升幅超100%;≥55岁组英国、俄罗斯联邦及部分欧洲国家死亡和DALY率上升。 (五)按年龄组划分的SDI区域HBV相关疾病负担的相对变化:<20岁组所有SDI区域绝对负担均下降,中高SDI区域降幅最大;20—54岁组低SDI区域绝对负担增幅最大、高SDI区域降幅最大;≥55岁组所有SDI区域绝对负担均上升,中低SDI区域增长最陡。率值在所有年龄组和SDI区域均下降,<20岁组在中高SDI区域降幅最大,20—54岁和≥55岁组在中或更高SDI区域降幅最大。 (六)2022—2050年全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄组预测:全年龄绝对负担预计持续下降,但年龄别模式差异显著,<20岁和20—54岁组绝对负担下降,≥55岁组上升(如≥55岁组发病例数预计从2030年1250万增至2050年1578万,而<20岁组从722万降至311万)。所有年龄组率值预计下降,<20岁组降幅最大(发病率由2022年394.30/10万降至2050年127.15/10万),≥55岁组降幅最小(703.01降至583.45/10万)。回溯检验显示多数MAPE值低于10%,敏感性分析结果与主分析一致。 四、讨论部分总结 讨论指出,各年龄组间的鲜明分歧是最关键发现,解释了总体率下降与总人群绝对负担上升并存的悖论。<20岁组负担急剧一致下降,流行病学率改善为主导驱动,与疫苗接种在健康婴儿、儿童和青少年中诱导的超过95%血清保护率一致;而老年人疫苗血清保护率降至60%—70%且多出生于普遍接种之前,形成独特流行病学模式。≥55岁组所有绝对指标显著上升(发病增74.10%、患病增87.38%、死亡增42.77%、DALYs增35.86%),人口增长与老龄化联合效应远超流行病学率改善的减少量,人口压力主导了老年人群流行病学格局;这些发现应解释为人群水平模式而非个体纵向转变。地理差异与年龄别异质性并存,部分欧洲区域死亡与DALY率上升超100%,反映预防控制收益分配不均。世界卫生组织(World Health Organization,WHO)2030年消除病毒性肝炎的目标面临疾病负担老龄化的重大人口学挑战。政策启示包括:维持青少年疫苗接种进展(及时接种首针并补种);对≥55岁人群扩大筛查、强化诊断并促进抗病毒治疗;针对不同SDI区域实施差异化策略。局限性包括BAPC模型依赖历史数据、≥55岁组预测不确定性区间(uncertainty intervals,UIs)较宽、未量化疫苗接种与抗病毒治疗贡献及未详察国家内部差异。 五、研究结论部分翻译 总之,尽管全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄标化率(age-standardized rates,ASRs)已下降,≥55岁人群绝对负担却增加,人口增长和老龄化在很大程度上促成了这一转变,抵消了有利流行病学变化带来的减少。区域差异依然显著,低、中SDI地区承担最大负担。预测表明这种年龄相关转变可能持续,凸显实现WHO定义的2030年肝炎消除目标仍面临持续挑战。应对挑战需加强针对性筛查、改善老年人群抗病毒治疗可及性,并实施区域特异性的预防控制策略。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP source_language_evidence.time: 方法:研究人员利用2021年全球疾病负担研究(Global Burden of Disease 2021,GBD 2021)数据,分析了1990—2021年间HBV相关疾病的发病率、患病率、死亡及伤残调整生命年(disability-adjusted life-years,DALYs)趋势。研究人员按年龄组(<20岁、20—54岁、≥55岁)对分析结果进行分层,采用Das Gupta分解法定量评估疾病负担变化的驱动因素,并按社会人口学指数(socio-demographic index,SDI)描述地理分布格局。研究人员应用贝叶斯年龄-时期-队列(Bayesian age-period-cohort,BAPC)建模对至2050年的疾病负担进行预测。

source_language_evidence.scale_impact_and_risk: (五)按年龄组划分的SDI区域HBV相关疾病负担的相对变化:<20岁组所有SDI区域绝对负担均下降,中高SDI区域降幅最大;20—54岁组低SDI区域绝对负担增幅最大、高SDI区域降幅最大;≥55岁组所有SDI区域绝对负担均上升,中低SDI区域增长最陡。率值在所有年龄组和SDI区域均下降,<20岁组在中高SDI区域降幅最大,20—54岁和≥55岁组在中或更高SDI区域降幅最大。
source_language_evidence.brief_en: 今日动态 生物通首页 今日动态 新技术专栏 人才市场 生物通首页 > 今日动态 > 正文 1990—2021年全球乙型肝炎病毒相关疾病年龄别负担特征、驱动因素量化及至2050年的趋势预测 时间:2026年11月10日 来源:Tropical Medicine and Health 编辑推荐: 背景:普及儿童免疫接种已使年轻人群中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)相关疾病的疾病负担有所下降,但人口老龄化正在增加老年人群的相关疾病负担。本研究评估了1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病的年龄别趋势,量化了驱动因素,并对至2050 广告 X 领取10x Genomics的单细胞多组学分析解决方案>> 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 “畅读会员”登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 背景:普及儿童免疫接种已使年轻人群中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)相关疾病的疾病负担有所下降,但人口老龄化正在增加老年人群的相关疾病负担。本研究评估了1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病的年龄别趋势,量化了驱动因素,并对至2050年的疾病负担进行预测,以期为优化预防策略提供依据。 方法:研究人员利用2021年全球疾病负担研究(Global Burden of Disease 2021,GBD 2021)数据,分析了1990—2021年间HBV相关疾病的发病率、患病率、死亡及伤残调整生命年(disability-adjusted life-years,DALYs)趋势。研究人员按年龄组(<20岁、20—54岁、≥55岁)对分析结果进行分层,采用Das Gupta分解法定量评估疾病负担变化的驱动因素,并按社会人口学指数(socio-demographic index,SDI)描述地理分布格局。研究人员应用贝叶斯年龄-时期-队列(Bayesian age-period-cohort,BAPC)建模对至2050年的疾病负担进行预测。 结果:1990年至2021年,全球HBV相关疾病年龄标化发病率、患病率、死亡率及DALY率均下降,而死亡与DALY的绝对数量增加。年龄分层分析显示,<20岁人群的所有疾病负担指标均急剧、一致下降;20—54岁人群及更显著的是≥55岁人群的降幅较为温和且病例数量增加。分解分析表明,流行病学改善驱动了年轻人群疾病负担的下降,而人口增长与老龄化抵消了老年人群中的这些获益。地理分布上,最高疾病负担仍集中于撒哈拉以南非洲和东南亚,而高SDI地区维持在最低水平。相对变化显示全球<20岁人群发病率降幅显著,而老年人群降幅较小。预测提示,尽管总体率将持续下降,≥55岁人群的绝对疾病负担将持续上升至2050年。 结论:尽管HBV相关疾病负担在年轻人群中持续下降,人口增长与老龄化正重塑全球HBV疾病。

news.content_title: HBV相关肝癌免疫治疗再认识:病毒持续感染如何重塑肿瘤免疫编辑
news.content: 顶部 首页 首页 雾 / 1° 隐私 HBV相关肝癌免疫治疗再认识:病毒持续感染如何重塑肿瘤免疫编辑 新浪财经 (来源:医学界) 免疫检查点抑制剂(ICI)及其联合治疗不断改变晚期肝细胞癌(HCC)的治疗格局。然而,对于乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌(HBV-HCC)而言,免疫治疗面对的不只是肿瘤本身。长期HBV感染、持续病毒抗原刺激、肝脏免疫耐受以及肿瘤发生后的免疫逃逸相互交织,共同塑造了具有特殊生物学特征的肿瘤免疫微环境。 Biochimica et Biophysica Acta-Molecular Basis of Disease期刊发表了一篇聚焦HBV-HCC免疫编辑与免疫治疗优化的综述。文章以“清除—平衡—逃逸”为主线,提出HBV-HCC可以被理解为一个受到抗病毒免疫和抗肿瘤免疫双重选择压力影响的动态免疫编辑过程[1]。 清除阶段:抗病毒免疫尚未结束,免疫功能障碍已经开始 在经典肿瘤免疫编辑理论中,免疫系统首先识别并清除异常细胞。但HBV-HCC的特殊之处在于,在恶性肿瘤真正形成之前,免疫系统已经经历了长期的病毒抗原刺激。 HBV本身并不直接造成明显的肝细胞裂解,病毒清除很大程度上依赖宿主免疫反应。当免疫介导的病毒清除不完全时,持续的病毒抗原暴露可逐渐造成抗病毒免疫功能障碍。HBV特异性CD8+ T细胞长期受到抗原刺激后可出现功能耗竭,并伴随PD-1等抑制性受体表达增加;CD4+ T细胞辅助功能受损又可能进一步影响CD8+ T细胞维持及树突状细胞功能。这一过程中,免疫功能变化并非简单的“增强”或“减弱”。例如,肝脏CXCR6+ CD8+ T细胞可受到cAMP-PKA-CREM信号轴调控而出现活化和效应功能受限;不同PD-1+ T细胞亚群之间也存在明显功能异质性。 展开剩余 83 % 因此,HBV-HCC形成之前的免疫环境可能已经发生深刻改变。肿瘤免疫逃逸并非从癌细胞出现后才开始,而可能建立在长期抗病毒免疫失衡的基础之上。 中的免疫编辑阶段。 平衡阶段:HBV整合将病毒持续感染与肿瘤克隆演化连接起来 当异常细胞未被完全清除,又尚未形成彻底的免疫逃逸时,肿瘤进入与免疫系统长期博弈的平衡阶段。在HBV-HCC中,HBV DNA整合为这一过程增加了病毒相关的特殊驱动力。 HBV DNA整合可造成基因组不稳定、染色体重排及拷贝数改变,并形成明显的肿瘤克隆异质性。在持续免疫选择压力下,具有更强生存能力或较低免疫原性的克隆可能逐渐获得优势,从而推动肿瘤适应性演化。与此同时,HBV相关分子机制也可能直接参与免疫逃逸和肿瘤生存,例如HBV DNA聚合酶与PD-L1调控,以及HBx相关的HSPA8-SLC7A11-GPX4抗铁死亡机制等。 值得关注的是,HBV整合不仅参与肿瘤发生,也可能留下可被动态监测的分子“痕迹”。由HBV整合产生的病毒-宿主嵌合DNA(vh-DNA)可在循环游离DNA中检测,为残留病灶及复发监测提供潜在的液体活检工具。然而,其检测阈值、标准化方法及临床应用价值仍需要进一步前瞻性验证。 肝癌中免疫编辑的分子标志物。 逃逸阶段:真正需要突破的,是多层次免疫抑制网络 进入免疫逃逸阶段后,HBV-HCC逐渐形成由T细胞耗竭、免疫抑制细胞富集、抗原呈递异常和基质屏障等共同组成的免疫抑制生态。 慢性HBV感染可促进CD8+ T细胞耗竭,并伴随PD-1等免疫检查点表达增加;TIM-3、LAG-3、TIGIT、CTLA-4等共同构成更复杂的抑制性检查点网络。与此同时,Treg、MDSC和肿瘤相关巨噬细胞等进一步抑制效应免疫。 髓系细胞和基质同样参与其中。CCL18、CREM和SPP1相关巨噬细胞亚群可表现出免疫抑制特征,其中SPP1+巨噬细胞与癌相关成纤维细胞相互作用,可形成限制免疫细胞浸润的肿瘤免疫屏障。HBsAg及肿瘤来源GDF15还可能影响树突状细胞抗原呈递,使免疫启动进一步受损。 因此,HBV-HCC的免疫逃逸更适合被理解为一个病毒持续存在、肿瘤适应性演化与免疫网络功能障碍共同驱动的多层次过程,而不是单一PD-1/PD-L1通路异常。PDF中的免疫编辑示意图也将这一过程概括为从早期免疫功能障碍,到HBV整合与克隆选择,再到耗竭T细胞、TAM、CAF及缺氧等共同构成的免疫逃逸状态。 从单药ICI走向联合治疗:关键是针对免疫编辑的不同环节 ICI能够解除部分免疫抑制,但对于已经形成深度T细胞耗竭、髓系抑制、抗原呈递障碍和肿瘤异质性的HBV-HCC,仅依靠单一检查点阻断可能难以充分逆转整个免疫生态。现有证据也提示,HBV阳性本身不能被简单视为统一的ICI疗效预测指标,病毒载量、抗病毒治疗、肝功能及免疫背景等因素均可能影响治疗结局。 这也为联合治疗提供了机制依据。ICI联合抗血管生成治疗可同时作用于免疫抑制与异常血管环境;TKI除抑制肿瘤增殖和血管生成外,还可能影响MDSC、Treg及效应T细胞浸润;TACE、SBRT和消融等局部治疗则可通过肿瘤细胞死亡和抗原释放影响免疫启动。双免疫检查点阻断也是其中的重要方向。 双免疫检查点阻断是晚期HCC免疫治疗的重要探索方向之一。III期HIMALAYA研究评估了单次曲麦利尤单抗联合度伐利尤单抗(STRIDE方案)在不可切除HCC中的疗效,与索拉非尼相比显示出总体生存获益。亚洲亚组分析显示,在HBV相关HCC占比较高的亚洲患者中,STRIDE方案的疗效趋势与全球研究结果总体一致;其中STRIDE组62.8%的患者为HBV相关HCC,STRIDE相较索拉非尼的OS HR为0.68(95% CI 0.52-0.89)[2]。与此同时,以抗血管生成药物为基础的靶免联合策略已在III期研究中积累了更为充分的生存证据。例如IMbrave150研究显示,阿替利珠单抗联合贝伐珠单抗组的mOS和中位PFS较索拉非尼组均有明显延长:mOS达19.2个月;mPFS达6.9个月;CARES-310研究显示,阿帕替尼联合卡瑞利珠单抗组与索拉非尼单药组相比亦明显延长。 因此,联合治疗的意义不仅在于增加治疗手段,而是基于HBV介导的免疫编辑特点,针对T细胞耗竭、髓系细胞抑制、异常血管生成以及抗原呈递障碍等不同环节进行综合干预。 HBV控制应成为免疫治疗全程管理的重要组成部分 与非病毒性HCC相比,HBV-HCC还有一个无法回避的问题——肿瘤治疗过程中病毒仍然存在。 高基线HBV病毒载量与ICI治疗较差结局存在关联,而抗病毒治疗可能改善患者预后。因此,对于高病毒载量患者,核苷(酸)类似物治疗、HBV DNA动态监测以及肝功能评估应成为ICI治疗管理的重要组成部分。对于活动性HBV感染患者,在有效抗病毒治疗和密切监测基础上实施ICI治疗具有一定可行性,但仍需要注意HBV再激活以及免疫相关性肝炎等不同原因所致肝损伤的鉴别。 这一点意味着,HBV-HCC的精准免疫治疗不能只回答“选择哪一种抗肿瘤药物”,还需要同时回答“患者当前的病毒状态如何,以及如何在抗肿瘤治疗过程中管理HBV”。 从单一指标走向“病毒—肿瘤—免疫”多维画像 HBV-HCC高度异质,也使单一生物标志物难以完整预测ICI获益。未来更值得关注的可能是多模态标志物组合:HBV DNA、HBcrAg、循环HBV RNA以及HBV整合来源cfDNA/vh-DNA可反映病毒活动和克隆演化;AFP、DCP和AFP-L3可补充肿瘤负荷信息;DNA甲基化特征以及T细胞耗竭、髓系细胞极化、可溶性免疫检查点等则可进一步描绘肿瘤免疫状态。 这种“病毒—肿瘤—免疫”多维画像,可能比单纯依据某一个免疫标志物更符合HBV-HCC的生物学特点,并为患者分层、复发监测和机制导向的联合治疗提供新的研究方向。 总结与展望 HBV-HCC并不是单纯发生于HBV感染背景下的HCC,而是长期病毒持续感染、宿主免疫反应和肿瘤克隆演化共同塑造的结果。从清除阶段的抗病毒免疫功能障碍,到平衡阶段HBV整合驱动的基因组不稳定和克隆选择,再到逃逸阶段形成的T细胞耗竭与免疫抑制微环境,“免疫编辑”提供了一条连接HBV感染与HCC免疫治疗异质性的动态主线。 因此,HBV-HCC免疫治疗的进一步优化可能需要超越单纯的检查点阻断,将肿瘤免疫状态评估、HBV病毒活动监测、规范抗病毒管理以及机制导向的联合治疗纳入同一治疗框架。未来结合HBV整合来源液体活检、病毒学指标、肿瘤负荷以及免疫状态建立多维生物标志物体系,并针对不同免疫编辑特征开展前瞻性分层研究,有望进一步推动HBV-HCC从“统一的免疫治疗”走向真正基于病毒、肿瘤和免疫特征的个体化治疗。 参考文献: 免疫检查点抑制剂(ICI)及其联合治疗不断改变晚期肝细胞癌(HCC)的治疗格局。然而,对于乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌(HBV-HCC)而言,免疫治疗面对的不只是肿瘤本身。长期HBV感染、持续病毒抗原刺激、肝脏免疫耐受以及肿瘤发生后的免疫逃逸相互交织,共同塑造了具有特殊生物学特征的肿瘤免疫微环境。 Biochimica et Biophysica Acta-Molecular Basis of Disease期刊发表了一篇聚焦HBV-HCC免疫编辑与免疫治疗优化的综述。文章以“清除—平衡—逃逸”为主线,提出HBV-HCC可以被理解为一个受到抗病毒免疫和抗肿瘤免疫双重选择压力影响的动态免疫编辑过程[1]。 清除阶段:抗病毒免疫尚未结束,免疫功能障碍已经开始 在经典肿瘤免疫编辑理论中,免疫系统首先识别并清除异常细胞。但HBV-HCC的特殊之处在于,在恶性肿瘤真正形成之前,免疫系统已经经历了长期的病毒抗原刺激。 HBV本身并不直接造成明显的肝细胞裂解,病毒清除很大程度上依赖宿主免疫反应。当免疫介导的病毒清除不完全时,持续的病毒抗原暴露可逐渐造成抗病毒免疫功能障碍。HBV特异性CD8+ T细胞长期受到抗原刺激后可出现功能耗竭,并伴随PD-1等抑制性受体表达增加;CD4+ T细胞辅助功能受损又可能进一步影响CD8+ T细胞维持及树突状细胞功能。这一过程中,免疫功能变化并非简单的“增强”或“减弱”。例如,肝脏CXCR6+ CD8+ T细胞可受到cAMP-PKA-CREM信号轴调控而出现活化和效应功能受限;不同PD-1+ T细胞亚群之间也存在明显功能异质性。 展开剩余 83 % 因此,HBV-HCC形成之前的免疫环境可能已经发生深刻改变。肿瘤免疫逃逸并非从癌细胞出现后才开始,而可能建立在长期抗病毒免疫失衡的基础之上。 中的免疫编辑阶段。 平衡阶段:HBV整合将病毒持续感染与肿瘤克隆演化连接起来 当异常细胞未被完全清除,又尚未形成彻底的免疫逃逸时,肿瘤进入与免疫系统长期博弈的平衡阶段。在HBV-HCC中,HBV DNA整合为这一过程增加了病毒相关的特殊驱动力。 HBV DNA整合可造成基因组不稳定、染色体重排及拷贝数改变,并形成明显的肿瘤克隆异质性。在持续免疫选择压力下,具有更强生存能力或较低免疫原性的克隆可能逐渐获得优势,从而推动肿瘤适应性演化。与此同时,HBV相关分子机制也可能直接参与免疫逃逸和肿瘤生存,例如HBV DNA聚合酶与PD-L1调控,以及HBx相关的HSPA8-SLC7A11-GPX4抗铁死亡机制等。 进入免疫逃逸阶段后,HBV-HCC逐渐形成由T细胞耗竭、免疫抑制细胞富集、抗原呈递异常和基质屏障等共同组成的免疫抑制生态。 慢性HBV感染可促进CD8+ T细胞耗竭,并伴随PD-1等免疫检查点表达增加;TIM-3、LAG-3、TIGIT、CTLA-4等共同构成更复杂的抑制性检查点网络。与此同时,Treg、MDSC和肿瘤相关巨噬细胞等进一步抑制效应免疫。 髓系细胞和基质同样参与其中。CCL18、CREM和SPP1相关巨噬细胞亚群可表现出免疫抑制特征,其中SPP1+巨噬细胞与癌相关成纤维细胞相互作用,可形成限制免疫细胞浸润的肿瘤免疫屏障。HBsAg及肿瘤来源GDF15还可能影响树突状细胞抗原呈递,使免疫启动进一步受损。 因此,HBV-HCC的免疫逃逸更适合被理解为一个病毒持续存在、肿瘤适应性演化与免疫网络功能障碍共同驱动的多层次过程,而不是单一PD-1/PD-L1通路异常。PDF中的免疫编辑示意图也将这一过程概括为从早期免疫功能障碍,到HBV整合与克隆选择,再到耗竭T细胞、TAM、CAF及缺氧等共同构成的免疫逃逸状态。 从单药ICI走向联合治疗:关键是针对免疫编辑的不同环节 ICI能够解除部分免疫抑制,但对于已经形成深度T细胞耗竭、髓系抑制、抗原呈递障碍和肿瘤异质性的HBV-HCC,仅依靠单一检查点阻断可能难以充分逆转整个免疫生态。现有证据也提示,HBV阳性本身不能被简单视为统一的ICI疗效预测指标,病毒载量、抗病毒治疗、肝功能及免疫背景等因素均可能影响治疗结局。 这也为联合治疗提供了机制依据。ICI联合抗血管生成治疗可同时作用于免疫抑制与异常血管环境;TKI除抑制肿瘤增殖和血管生成外,还可能影响MDSC、Treg及效应T细胞浸润;TACE、SBRT和消融等局部治疗则可通过肿瘤细胞死亡和抗原释放影响免疫启动。双免疫检查点阻断也是其中的重要方向。 双免疫检查点阻断是晚期HCC免疫治疗的重要探索方向之一。III期HIMALAYA研究评估了单次曲麦利尤单抗联合度伐利尤单抗(STRIDE方案)在不可切除HCC中的疗效,与索拉非尼相比显示出总体生存获益。亚洲亚组分析显示,在HBV相关HCC占比较高的亚洲患者中,STRIDE方案的疗效趋势与全球研究结果总体一致;其中STRIDE组62.8%的患者为HBV相关HCC,STRIDE相较索拉非尼的OS HR为0.68(95% CI 0.52-0.89)[2]。与此同时,以抗血管生成药物为基础的靶免联合策略已在III期研究中积累了更为充分的生存证据。例如IMbrave150研究显示,阿替利珠单抗联合贝伐珠单抗组的mOS和中位PFS较索拉非尼组均有明显延长:mOS达19.2个月;mPFS达6.9个月;CARES-310研究显示,阿帕替尼联合卡瑞利珠单抗组与索拉非尼单药组相比亦明显延长。 因此,联合治疗的意义不仅在于增加治疗手段,而是基于HBV介导的免疫编辑特点,针对T细胞耗竭、髓系细胞抑制、异常血管生成以及抗原呈递障碍等不同环节进行综合干预。 HBV控制应成为免疫治疗全程管理的重要组成部分 与非病毒性HCC相比,HBV-HCC还有一个无法回避的问题——肿瘤治疗过程中病毒仍然存在。 高基线HBV病毒载量与ICI治疗较差结局存在关联,而抗病毒治疗可能改善患者预后。因此,对于高病毒载量患者,核苷(酸)类似物治疗、HBV DNA动态监测以及肝功能评估应成为ICI治疗管理的重要组成部分。对于活动性HBV感染患者,在有效抗病毒治疗和密切监测基础上实施ICI治疗具有一定可行性,但仍需要注意HBV再激活以及免疫相关性肝炎等不同原因所致肝损伤的鉴别。 这一点意味着,HBV-HCC的精准免疫治疗不能只回答“选择哪一种抗肿瘤药物”,还需要同时回答“患者当前的病毒状态如何,以及如何在抗肿瘤治疗过程中管理HBV”。 从单一指标走向“病毒—肿瘤—免疫”多维画像 HBV-HCC高度异质,也使单一生物标志物难以完整预测ICI获益。未来更值得关注的可能是多模态标志物组合:HBV DNA、HBcrAg、循环HBV RNA以及HBV整合来源cfDNA/vh-DNA可反映病毒活动和克隆演化;AFP、DCP和AFP-L3可补充肿瘤负荷信息;DNA甲基化特征以及T细胞耗竭、髓系细胞极化、可溶性免疫检查点等则可进一步描绘肿瘤免疫状态。 这种“病毒—肿瘤—免疫”多维画像,可能比单纯依据某一个免疫标志物更符合HBV-HCC的生物学特点,并为患者分层、复发监测和机制导向的联合治疗提供新的研究方向。 总结与展望 HBV-HCC并不是单纯发生于HBV感染背景下的HCC,而是长期病毒持续感染、宿主免疫反应和肿瘤克隆演化共同塑造的结果。从清除阶段的抗病毒免疫功能障碍,到平衡阶段HBV整合驱动的基因组不稳定和克隆选择,再到逃逸阶段形成的T细胞耗竭与免疫抑制微环境,“免疫编辑”提供了一条连接HBV感染与HCC免疫治疗异质性的动态主线。 因此,HBV-HCC免疫治疗的进一步优化可能需要超越单纯的检查点阻断,将肿瘤免疫状态评估、HBV病毒活动监测、规范抗病毒管理以及机制导向的联合治疗纳入同一治疗框架。未来结合HBV整合来源液体活检、病毒学指标、肿瘤负荷以及免疫状态建立多维生物标志物体系,并针对不同免疫编辑特征开展前瞻性分层研究,有望进一步推动HBV-HCC从“统一的免疫治疗”走向真正基于病毒、肿瘤和免疫特征的个体化治疗。 参考文献: source_language_evidence.brief_en: 顶部 首页 首页 雾 / 1° 隐私 HBV相关肝癌免疫治疗再认识:病毒持续感染如何重塑肿瘤免疫编辑 新浪财经 (来源:医学界) 免疫检查点抑制剂(ICI)及其联合治疗不断改变晚期肝细胞癌(HCC)的治疗格局。然而,对于乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌(HBV-HCC)而言,免疫治疗面对的不只是肿瘤本身。长期HBV感染、持续病毒抗原刺激、肝脏免疫耐受以及肿瘤发生后的免疫逃逸相互交织,共同塑造了具有特殊生物学特征的肿瘤免疫微环境。 Biochimica et Biophysica Acta-Molecular Basis of Disease期刊发表了一篇聚焦HBV-HCC免疫编辑与免疫治疗优化的综述。文章以“清除—平衡—逃逸”为主线,提出HBV-HCC可以被理解为一个受到抗病毒免疫和抗肿瘤免疫双重选择压力影响的动态免疫编辑过程[1]。 清除阶段:抗病毒免疫尚未结束,免疫功能障碍已经开始 在经典肿瘤免疫编辑理论中,免疫系统首先识别并清除异常细胞。但HBV-HCC的特殊之处在于,在恶性肿瘤真正形成之前,免疫系统已经经历了长期的病毒抗原刺激。 HBV本身并不直接造成明显的肝细胞裂解,病毒清除很大程度上依赖宿主免疫反应。当免疫介导的病毒清除不完全时,持续的病毒抗原暴露可逐渐造成抗病毒免疫功能障碍。HBV特异性CD8+ T细胞长期受到抗原刺激后可出现功能耗竭,并伴随PD-1等抑制性受体表达增加;CD4+ T细胞辅助功能受损又可能进一步影响CD8+ T细胞维持及树突状细胞功能。这一过程中,免疫功能变化并非简单的“增强”或“减弱”。例如,肝脏CXCR6+ CD8+ T细胞可受到cAMP-PKA-CREM信号轴调控而出现活化和效应功能受限;不同PD-1+ T细胞亚群之间也存在明显功能异质性。 展开剩余 83 % 因此,HBV-HCC形成之前的免疫环境可能已经发生深刻改变。肿瘤免疫逃逸并非从癌细胞出现后才开始,而可能建立在长期抗病毒免疫失衡的基础之上。 平衡阶段:HBV整合将病毒持续感染与肿瘤克隆演化连接起来 当异常细胞未被完全清除,又尚未形成彻底的免疫逃逸时,肿瘤进入与免疫系统长期博弈的平衡阶段。在HBV-HCC中,HBV DNA整合为这一过程增加了病毒相关的特殊驱动力。 HBV DNA整合可造成基因组不稳定、染色体重排及拷贝数改变,并形成明显的肿瘤克隆异质性。在持续免疫选择压力下,具有更强生存能力或较低免疫原性的克隆可能逐渐获得优势,从而推动肿瘤适应性演化。与此同时,HBV相关分子机制也可能直接参与免疫逃逸和肿瘤生存,例如HBV DNA聚合酶与PD-L1调控,以及HBx相关的HSPA8-SLC7A11-GPX4抗铁死亡机制等。
